title: 隆慶元年應天府鄉試錄
text:
應天府鄉試錄序
隆慶元年丁卯應天當鄉試是
我
皇上御極之第一科也先期府臣以
請
上命〔臣希烈〕暨〔臣〕鋌竝輟
講事來司文柄〔臣〕丙〔臣〕愧譾薄嘗再分
校禮闈一典會武乃今責愈加
隆而此心益惟不稱
===
任使是懼既
陛辭兼程以南比至內外執事咸
集同考試則推官〔臣〕梗知州〔臣〕
誥〔臣〕惟喬知縣〔臣〕家卿〔臣〕愼修教授〔臣〕
奮〔臣〕本中教諭〔臣〕侯慶〔臣〕元倬監試則
punctuated:
應天府鄉試錄序

隆慶元年丁卯，應天當鄉試，是我皇上御極之第一科也。先期，府臣以請，上命〔臣希烈〕暨〔臣〕鋌竝輟講事，來司文柄。〔臣〕丙〔臣〕愧譾薄，嘗再分校禮闈，一典會武。乃今責愈加隆，而此心益惟不稱任使是懼。既陛辭，兼程以南。比至，內外執事咸集。同考試則推官〔臣〕梗、知州〔臣〕誥、〔臣〕惟喬、知縣〔臣〕家卿、〔臣〕愼修、教授〔臣〕奮、〔臣〕本中、教諭〔臣〕侯慶、〔臣〕元倬。監試則
translation_en:
Preface to the Record of the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination

In the dingmao year, the first year of Longqing [1567], Yingtian was due to hold its Provincial Examination. This was the first examination since our emperor ascended the throne. Before the appointed time, the prefectural officials submitted a request, and His Majesty ordered your servant Xilie and your servant Ting both to suspend their lecturing duties and come to take charge of selecting literary talent. Your servants [?—the transcription here reads 臣丙臣], ashamed of our shallow learning and limited abilities, had previously served twice as Associate Examiners at the Metropolitan Examination and once presided over the Metropolitan Military Examination. Now our responsibility had grown still weightier, and we feared all the more that we would prove unequal to our commission.

After taking leave of His Majesty, we traveled south by forced stages. By the time we arrived, all the officials serving inside and outside the examination compound had assembled. The Associate Examiners were your servant Geng, a prefectural judge; your servants Gao and Weiqiao, department magistrates; your servants Jiaqing and Shenxiu, county magistrates; your servants Fen and Benzhong, prefectural school instructors; and your servants Houqing and Yuanzhuo, county school instructors. As for those overseeing the examination, they were …

title: 隆慶元年應天府鄉試錄
text:
御史臣貢臣烈提調寔府臣掌
之乃府尹臣譚〔大初〕以晉陟工部
右侍郎且行而府丞臣應總其
事偕入鎖院臣儕申告之曰
聖天子踐序履元萬物快覩百度惟
貞設科求賢玆惟首舉兩畿又
首善地也頃
===
僉言官之請釐正文體精覈考校
以須真材吾儕其何以仰稱
德意于時更相戒飭而後即事合
提學御史臣耿〔定向〕暨六館諸曹
所選士凡四千有奇三試之□
制拔其尤者百三十五人幷文之
可式者以
punctuated: 御史臣貢、臣烈，提調寔府臣掌之。乃府尹臣譚〔大初〕以晉陟工部右侍郎且行，而府丞臣應總其事，偕入鎖院。臣儕申告之曰：「聖天子踐序履元，萬物快覩，百度惟貞。設科求賢，玆惟首舉；兩畿又首善地也。頃僉言官之請，釐正文體，精覈考校，以須真材。吾儕其何以仰稱德意？」于時更相戒飭，而後即事。合提學御史臣耿〔定向〕暨六館諸曹所選士，凡四千有奇。三試之，□制拔其尤者百三十五人，幷文之可式者，以
translation_en:
…the Censors, your servants Gong and Lie; responsibility for serving as Proctors lay with the officials of the prefecture. Prefect Tan〔Dachu〕, having been promoted to Right Vice Minister of Works, was about to depart, so Vice Prefect Ying took overall charge of the proceedings. Together we entered the examination compound and were sequestered. We solemnly addressed those assembled: “The sagely Son of Heaven has succeeded to the throne and inaugurated his reign. All creation rejoices to behold him, and the hundred institutions are set right. This is the first examination held to seek worthy men; moreover, the two metropolitan regions are places foremost in exemplary conduct. Recently, following the collective request of the remonstrance officials [?], literary style has been rectified and the scrutiny of examination papers made exacting, in expectation of finding true talent. How shall we fulfill His Majesty’s virtuous intentions?” We thereupon admonished one another before undertaking our duties.

The candidates selected by Censor for the Supervision of Education Geng〔Dingxiang〕and by the various offices of the Six Halls numbered more than four thousand in all. We examined them in three sessions and, according to the prescribed system [?], selected the most outstanding, numbering 135 men, together with essays that could serve as models, in order to…

title: 隆慶元年應天府鄉試錄
text:
獻告成事也臣聞賢才鍾於地靈
符乎氣運而其盛也必肇於幾
邑昔周宅岐豐多士生於王國
曁後佐中興大業其名世之材
輩出故宣王策命召虎必于岐
周重本始也我
高皇帝啓運東南定鼎金陵以當王
氣無論岐豐一時震起雲從爲
===
開
國元臣類産江淮間不忝王國之
多士嗣以科目進者明道德佐
勳業繫綱常以翊戴
聖朝斌斌甲海內化所從來二百餘
年于兹已今
punctuated:
獻，告成事也。臣聞賢才鍾於地靈，符乎氣運，而其盛也必肇於幾邑。昔周宅岐豐，多士生於王國，曁後佐中興大業，其名世之材輩出。故宣王策命召虎，必于岐周，重本始也。
我高皇帝啓運東南，定鼎金陵，以當王氣，無論岐豐。一時震起雲從，爲開國元臣，類産江淮間，不忝王國之多士。嗣以科目進者，明道德，佐勳業，繫綱常，以翊戴聖朝，斌斌甲海內。化所從來，二百餘年于兹已。今
translation_en:
…to present them, reporting the completion of our task. Your servant has heard that worthy talent gathers where the land possesses spiritual potency and accords with the currents of destiny, and that its flourishing must begin in a few localities. In ancient times, when the Zhou established their home at Qi and Feng, many worthy men arose within the royal domain. Later, to assist the great undertaking of dynastic restoration, talents renowned in their age emerged in succession. Thus, when King Xuan formally invested Shao Hu, he insisted on doing so at Qizhou, honoring the place of original beginnings.
Our Emperor Gao inaugurated his destined rule in the southeast and established his capital at Jinling, where the kingly aura converged; there is scarcely any need to speak of Qi and Feng in comparison. Those who rose at his call and followed him like gathering clouds, becoming the dynasty’s chief founding ministers, were mostly born between the Yangzi and Huai rivers. They were worthy counterparts to the many eminent men of the Zhou royal domain. Those who subsequently advanced through the examinations elucidated the Way and virtue, assisted in great achievements, and upheld the cardinal bonds and constant principles of human relations, thereby supporting our sagely dynasty. Accomplished and cultivated, they ranked foremost throughout the realm. More than two hundred years have now passed since this transforming influence began. Now…

title: 隆慶元年應天府鄉試錄
text:
皇上纘
列聖大統際熙洽宣朗之運
登極一詔罷冗費蠲逋賦停額外征
徭與民更始而又
廣開言路
拔忠義正直之士於摧廢中以
風示天下即遐陬絕域自別於凡
民者咸思致身顯名矧江淮諸
郡爲豐芑之所詒者乎然則諸
===
士附
景光躡風雲膺玆
龍飛首舉誠千載一時矣易曰觀乎
人文以化成天下文者道之顯
也人才之盛衰觀焉者也臣旣
punctuated: 皇上纘列聖大統，際熙洽宣朗之運，登極一詔，罷冗費，蠲逋賦，停額外征徭，與民更始，而又廣開言路，拔忠義正直之士於摧廢中，以風示天下。即遐陬絕域，自別於凡民者，咸思致身顯名，矧江淮諸郡爲豐芑之所詒者乎？然則諸士附景光，躡風雲，膺玆龍飛首舉，誠千載一時矣！《易》曰：「觀乎人文，以化成天下。」文者，道之顯也；人才之盛衰，觀焉者也。臣旣
translation_en:
…His Majesty has succeeded to the great imperial line of the sage sovereigns, at a time of flourishing concord and radiant enlightenment. With a single edict upon his accession, he abolished unnecessary expenditure, remitted tax arrears, and suspended levies and labor services beyond the prescribed quotas, making a fresh beginning together with the people. Moreover, he opened wide the channels for presenting opinions and raised loyal, righteous, upright men from among those who had been cast down and dismissed, setting an example for all under Heaven. Even in remote corners and distant regions, those who distinguish themselves from ordinary people all aspire to enter service and make their names illustrious. How much more must this be so in the prefectures of Jiangnan and Huainan, heirs to the legacy of “abundant millet”—the nurturing of talent for posterity!

Thus, for these scholars to share in the imperial radiance, ride upon the winds and clouds, and participate in this first examination following the dragon’s ascent to the throne is truly an opportunity encountered once in a thousand years! The Book of Changes says: “Observe human culture, and thereby transform and bring order to all under Heaven.” Literary expression is the manifestation of the Way; through it one may discern the flourishing or decline of human talent. Your servant has already…

title: 隆慶元年應天府鄉試錄
text:
慶多士之遭而觀于其文言人
人殊類皆根極理要發抒性真
舊習浮靡掃除殆盡至其綜貫
天人揚搉今古治亂興衰之原
邪正得失之辨鑿鑿如指諸掌
間有畏天悲人憂時憤事感槩
於中而義形於詞者臣覽之輙
欽䄂嘆曰玆非忠義正直之餘
===
庶幾
明詔之所奬掖者乎
聖天子作新化理轉移人才其速如
此竊伏自慶謂有士若斯庶其
少自稱塞矣乎雖然士篤守一
經覽載籍見古人事憤悱於心
punctuated: 慶多士之遭，而觀于其文，言人人殊類，皆根極理要，發抒性真，舊習浮靡掃除殆盡。至其綜貫天人，揚搉今古，治亂興衰之原，邪正得失之辨，鑿鑿如指諸掌。間有畏天悲人、憂時憤事，感槩於中而義形於詞者，臣覽之，輙欽䄂嘆曰：「玆非忠義正直之餘，庶幾明詔之所奬掖者乎？」聖天子作新化理，轉移人才，其速如此！竊伏自慶，謂有士若斯，庶其少自稱塞矣乎！雖然，士篤守一經，覽載籍，見古人事，憤悱於心，
translation_en:
…rejoice in the opportunity these many scholars have encountered, and examine their writings. Though their expression differs from person to person, all probe the essential principles to their roots and give voice to their genuine nature. The old habits of superficiality and extravagance have been almost entirely swept away. In comprehensively linking Heaven and humanity and discussing past and present, they make the sources of order and disorder, rise and decline, and the distinctions between the deviant and the upright, success and failure, as clear and certain as something pointed out in the palm of one’s hand. Among them are those who revere Heaven and grieve for humanity, worry over the times and feel indignation at events: deeply moved within, they give expression to righteousness in their words. On reading these, your servant invariably exclaims in admiration [?]: “Is this not an outgrowth of loyalty, righteousness, uprightness, and integrity, approaching what the illustrious edict seeks to encourage?”

Such is the speed with which the sagely Son of Heaven renews moral transformation and good government and reshapes men of talent! I humbly rejoice to myself, thinking that, with scholars such as these, perhaps I may have discharged my responsibility in some small measure!

Nevertheless, scholars devote themselves steadfastly to a single Classic, read the written records, and encounter the deeds of the ancients, their hearts stirred by thoughts they struggle to comprehend and express…

title: 隆慶元年應天府鄉試錄
text:
思以自見操觚談當世務即節
士才人何讓焉乃其所樹立或
至悖謬不類臣竊懼焉夫學以
明諸心也言發於心今茲之言
其心之誠然否耶逆其非心之
誠然而測其未至是誣士也然
而其所樹立異者則弗學之過
===
耳夫學無時可已也孟子曰學
問之道無他求其放心而已夫
人未有學問而心不存者未有
弗學弗問而心不放者心苟存
矣雖一命之士必有所立況其
上者乎心苟放矣雖勲極宦成
罔以自戢況其下者乎諸士今
punctuated:
思以自見，操觚談當世務，即節士才人何讓焉？乃其所樹立，或至悖謬不類，臣竊懼焉。夫學以明諸心也，言發於心，今茲之言，其心之誠然否耶？逆其非心之誠然而測其未至，是誣士也。然而其所樹立異者，則弗學之過耳。
夫學無時可已也。孟子曰：「學問之道無他，求其放心而已。」夫人未有學問而心不存者，未有弗學弗問而心不放者。心苟存矣，雖一命之士必有所立，況其上者乎？心苟放矣，雖勲極宦成，罔以自戢，況其下者乎？諸士今
translation_en:
…they think of making themselves known, take up the writing tablet, and discuss the affairs of the age. In this, what need have they to concede to men of integrity or talent? Yet what they actually establish for themselves may prove perverse and misguided, quite at odds with their words. Your servant privately fears this. Learning serves to bring clarity to the mind, and words issue from the mind. Do the words they offer now truly express what is in their minds? To presume that they do not, and to conjecture that these men will fall short, would be to malign them. Yet when their actual conduct differs from their words, the fault lies simply in their failure to learn.
There is no time when learning may cease. Mencius said: “The way of learning and inquiry is none other than this: to seek out one's strayed mind.” No one pursues learning and inquiry without keeping the mind present; no one neglects learning and inquiry without letting the mind stray. If the mind is kept present, even a man holding the lowest official appointment will surely achieve something of worth—how much more those above him! If the mind is allowed to stray, even one whose achievements are unsurpassed and whose official career is fully established has no means of restraining himself—how much less those below him! You gentlemen now…

title: 隆慶元年應天府鄉試錄
text:
錄於鄉幼學可徵已由此爲焉
官對
大廷策名效用其學之爲行業何
如耶記曰玉不琢不成器人不
學不知道諸士南國之良産誠
玉也亦既剖之俾出璞矣學者
所以琢爲圭璋瑚璉之器以需
===
用於
清廟明堂者也是在諸士自愛耳
弗自追琢輕用其質而失其所
爲良亦何以爲賢科重哉臣猥
守章句遭際
聖明罔効尺寸學焉而未逮也乃告
語諸士相與切磨且因以自勖
punctuated: 錄於鄉，幼學可徵已。由此爲焉官，對大廷，策名效用，其學之爲行業何如耶？《記》曰：「玉不琢，不成器；人不學，不知道。」諸士南國之良産，誠玉也，亦既剖之，俾出璞矣。學者，所以琢爲圭璋瑚璉之器，以需用於清廟明堂者也。是在諸士自愛耳。弗自追琢，輕用其質，而失其所爲良，亦何以爲賢科重哉？臣猥守章句，遭際聖明，罔効尺寸，學焉而未逮也。乃告語諸士，相與切磨，且因以自勖
translation_en:
…selected at the provincial level, you gentlemen have already demonstrated your youthful learning. Proceeding from here to become officials [?], to answer before the imperial court, and to have your names enrolled for service, how will you turn your learning into conduct and achievement? The Record of Rites says: “Jade, unless carved, does not become a vessel; people, unless they study, do not understand the Way.” You gentlemen, the finest products of the southern region, are indeed jade. The stone has already been split open to bring you forth from its rough matrix. Learning is the means of carving you into ceremonial jade tablets and sacrificial vessels, ready for service in the pure ancestral temple and the Hall of Enlightenment. This depends solely on your cherishing your own worth. If you fail to carve and polish yourselves, squander your native qualities, and lose what makes you excellent, how can you lend distinction to the examination that selects the worthy?
I, your servant, unworthily occupied with textual interpretation, have had the good fortune to live under a sagely and enlightened sovereign, yet have rendered not the slightest service. I study but have not yet attained my goal. Thus I address you gentlemen, that we may cut and polish one another, and thereby encourage myself as well…

title: 隆慶元年應天府鄉試錄
text:
云
左春坊左諭德兼翰林院侍
讀王希烈謹序
punctuated:
云。

左春坊左諭德兼翰林院侍讀王希烈謹序。
translation_en:
…thus.

Preface respectfully written by Wang Xilie, Left Exhorter of the Left Secretariat of the Heir Apparent, concurrently Reader-in-Waiting in the Hanlin Academy.

title: 隆慶元年應天府鄉試錄
text:

提調官
中順大夫應天府府丞徐　應〔順叔浙江蘭谿縣人　庚戌進士〕
考試官
左春坊左諭德兼翰林院侍讀王希烈〔子忠江西南昌縣籍　臨川縣人癸丑進士〕

承事郎南京江西道監察御史賀　賁〔懋文河南靈寶縣人　丙辰進士〕
punctuated:
隆慶元年應天府鄉試。

提調官：
中順大夫、應天府府丞徐　應〔順叔，浙江蘭谿縣人，庚戌進士〕。

title: 隆慶元年應天府鄉試錄
text:
第壹場
四書
子貢問政子曰足食足兵民信之矣
知所以脩身則知所以治人知所以治人
則知所以治天下國家矣凡爲天下國
家有九經曰脩身也
人性之善也猶水之就下也人無有不善
水無有不下
易
===
九五飛龍在天利見大人
利貞剛柔正而位當也
擬之而後言議之而後動擬議以成其變
化鳴鶴在陰其子和之我有好爵吾與
爾靡之子曰君子居其室出其言善則
千里之外應之况其邇者乎居其室出
其言不善則千里之外違之况其邇者
乎言出乎身加乎民行發乎邇見乎遠
言行君子之樞機樞機之發榮辱之主
punctuated:
第壹場

四書

子貢問政。子曰：「足食，足兵，民信之矣。」

知所以脩身，則知所以治人；知所以治人，則知所以治天下國家矣。凡爲天下國家有九經，曰脩身也。

人性之善也，猶水之就下也。人無有不善，水無有不下。

易

九五，飛龍在天，利見大人。

利貞，剛柔正而位當也。

擬之而後言，議之而後動，擬議以成其變化。「鳴鶴在陰，其子和之。我有好爵，吾與爾靡之。」子曰：「君子居其室，出其言善，則千里之外應之，况其邇者乎？居其室，出其言不善，則千里之外違之，况其邇者乎？言出乎身，加乎民；行發乎邇，見乎遠。言行，君子之樞機；樞機之發，榮辱之主
translation_en:
First Session

Four Books

Zigong asked about government. The Master said: “Sufficient food, sufficient arms, and the people's trust.”

Knowing how to cultivate oneself, one knows how to govern others; knowing how to govern others, one knows how to govern all under Heaven, the states, and the families. There are nine guiding principles for governing all under Heaven, the states, and the families. The first is cultivating oneself.

The goodness of human nature is like water's tendency to flow downward. There is no person whose nature is not good, just as there is no water that does not flow downward.

Book of Changes

Nine in the fifth place: A flying dragon is in Heaven. It is beneficial to see the great man.

“Beneficial to remain steadfast”: the firm and yielding are correctly disposed, and their positions are appropriate.

Consider before speaking; deliberate before acting. Through consideration and deliberation, one brings changes and transformations to completion. “A crane calls in the shade; its young answers it. I have a fine cup of wine; I will share it with you.” The Master said: “When the gentleman remains in his room and speaks good words, people a thousand li away respond to him—how much more those nearby! When he remains in his room and speaks words that are not good, people a thousand li away turn against him—how much more those nearby! Words issue from oneself and affect the people; actions originate nearby and become manifest far away. Words and actions are the gentleman's hinge and trigger; their activation determines honor or disgrace…

title: 隆慶元年應天府鄉試錄
text:
也言行君子之所以動天地也可不愼
乎
乾坤其易之門耶
書
嘉言罔攸伏野無遺賢萬邦咸寧
賁若草木兆民允殖
我聞曰昔在殷王中宗嚴恭寅畏天命自
度治民祗懼不敢荒寧肆中宗之享國
七十有五年
政貴有恒辭尚體要不惟好異
===
詩
羔裘豹飾孔武有力彼其之子邦之司直
民之質矣日用飲食
天生烝民有物有則民之秉彝好是懿德
天監有周昭假于下保茲天子生仲山
甫
載見辟王曰求厥章龍旂陽陽和鈴央央
鞗革有鶬休有烈光率見昭考以孝以
punctuated:
也。言行，君子之所以動天地也，可不愼乎？
乾坤，其易之門耶？

書
嘉言罔攸伏，野無遺賢，萬邦咸寧。
賁若草木，兆民允殖。
我聞曰：「昔在殷王中宗，嚴恭寅畏，天命自度，治民祗懼，不敢荒寧。肆中宗之享國七十有五年。」
政貴有恒，辭尚體要，不惟好異。

詩
羔裘豹飾，孔武有力。彼其之子，邦之司直。
民之質矣，日用飲食。
天生烝民，有物有則。民之秉彝，好是懿德。天監有周，昭假于下，保茲天子，生仲山甫。
載見辟王，曰求厥章。龍旂陽陽，和鈴央央。鞗革有鶬，休有烈光。率見昭考，以孝以
translation_en:
… Words and deeds are the means by which the gentleman moves Heaven and Earth. Can he fail to be cautious?
Are Qian and Kun—the Creative and the Receptive—the gateway to the Changes?

Book of Documents
No worthy counsel remained concealed, and no worthy man was left undiscovered in the countryside. The myriad states were all at peace.
Flourishing like grasses and trees, the multitudes of the people truly multiplied.
I have heard it said: “Of old, King Zhongzong of Yin was solemn, reverent, respectful, and fearful. He measured himself against Heaven’s mandate and governed the people with reverence and apprehension, never daring to indulge in idle ease. Thus Zhongzong enjoyed his reign for seventy-five years.”
In government, constancy is prized; in speech, substance and essentials are esteemed. Do not merely delight in novelty.

Book of Odes
In a lambskin robe trimmed with leopard fur, he is truly martial and strong. That man is the upholder of uprightness in the state.
The people’s simple nature finds expression in their daily eating and drinking.
Heaven gave birth to the multitude of people; for every thing there is its governing rule. The people hold fast to their constant nature and love this excellent virtue. Heaven looked upon Zhou, its radiance reaching down below. To protect this Son of Heaven, it brought forth Zhong Shanfu.
They came to audience with the sovereign king, seeking his statutes. Dragon banners streamed brightly; carriage bells rang harmoniously. The leather reins gleamed with metal fittings, splendid and brilliantly shining. Together they came before the illustrious deceased father, with filial devotion and with …

title: 隆慶元年應天府鄉試錄
text:
享以介眉壽永言保之思皇多祜烈文
辟公綏以多福俾緝熙于純嘏
春秋
春公觀魚于棠〔隱公五年夏公如齊觀社〕
〔莊公二十有三年〕
許叔入于許〔桓公十有五年秋八月蔡季〕
自陳歸于蔡〔桓公十有七年夏秦伯之〕
弟鍼出奔晉〔昭公元年宋公之弟辰暨〕
仲佗石彄出奔陳〔定公十年〕
===
春王正月叔孫得臣會晉人宋人陳人衛
人鄭人伐沈沈潰〔文公三年〕
初稅畝〔宣公十有五年三月作丘甲成公〕
〔元年春用田賦哀公十有二年〕
禮記
頌而無諂諫而無驕
天高地下萬物散殊而禮制行矣流而不
息合同而化而樂興焉春作夏長仁也
秋斂冬藏義也仁近於樂義近於禮樂
punctuated:
享，以介眉壽，永言保之，思皇多祜。烈文辟公，綏以多福，俾緝熙于純嘏。

春秋
春，公觀魚于棠〔隱公五年。夏，公如齊觀社〕〔莊公二十有三年〕。
許叔入于許〔桓公十有五年。秋，八月，蔡季〕自陳歸于蔡〔桓公十有七年。夏，秦伯之〕弟鍼出奔晉〔昭公元年。宋公之弟辰暨〕仲佗、石彄出奔陳〔定公十年〕。
春，王正月，叔孫得臣會晉人、宋人、陳人、衛人、鄭人伐沈，沈潰〔文公三年〕。
初稅畝〔宣公十有五年。三月，作丘甲。成公〕〔元年。春，用田賦。哀公十有二年〕。

禮記
頌而無諂，諫而無驕。
天高地下，萬物散殊，而禮制行矣；流而不息，合同而化，而樂興焉。春作夏長，仁也；秋斂冬藏，義也。仁近於樂，義近於禮。樂
translation_en:
…to present offerings and thereby obtain long life. May they preserve this forever! How splendid and abundant are the blessings! Illustrious and accomplished lords, may you be granted many blessings and brought to enduring brilliance and great good fortune.

Spring and Autumn Annals

“In spring, the duke watched the fishing at Tang.” (Duke Yin, fifth year.) “In summer, the duke went to Qi to observe the sacrifice at the altar of the soil.” (Duke Zhuang, twenty-third year.)

“Xu Shu entered Xu.” (Duke Huan, fifteenth year.) “In autumn, in the eighth month, Cai Ji returned from Chen to Cai.” (Duke Huan, seventeenth year.) “In summer, Qian, younger brother of the Earl of Qin, fled to Jin.” (Duke Zhao, first year.) “Chen, younger brother of the Duke of Song, together with Zhong Tuo and Shi Kou, fled to Chen.” (Duke Ding, tenth year.)

“In spring, in the first month of the royal calendar, Shusun Dechen joined men of Jin, Song, Chen, Wei, and Zheng in attacking Shen. Shen collapsed.” (Duke Wen, third year.)

“For the first time, a tax was levied on land by the mu.” (Duke Xuan, fifteenth year.) “In the third month, an armor levy was instituted by the qiu land unit.” (Duke Cheng, first year.) “In spring, a levy based on farmland was imposed.” (Duke Ai, twelfth year.)

Record of Rites

“Praise without flattery; remonstrate without arrogance.”

“Heaven is high and earth is low; the myriad things are dispersed and distinct, and thus the ordering of ritual operates. They flow without ceasing, unite in harmony and undergo transformation, and thus music arises. Spring’s generation and summer’s growth are benevolence; autumn’s gathering and winter’s storing are righteousness. Benevolence is akin to music; righteousness is akin to ritual. Music …

title: 隆慶元年應天府鄉試錄
text:
者敦和率神而從天禮者别宜居鬼而
從地故聖人作樂以應天制禮以配地
禮樂明備天地官矣
夫孝置之而塞乎天地溥之而横乎四海
施諸後世而無朝夕推而放諸東海而
準推而放諸西海而準推而放諸南海
而準推而放諸北海而準
明其義者君也
第貳塲
===
論
聖神繼天立極
詔誥表〔内科一道〕
擬漢明帝幸辟雍行大射養老禮詔〔永平二年〕
擬唐以韓愈爲京兆尹誥〔長慶三年〕
擬宋輯尚書所載事作敬天圖成輔臣賀表〔乾道七年〕
判語五條
punctuated:
者敦和，率神而從天；禮者别宜，居鬼而從地。故聖人作樂以應天，制禮以配地。禮樂明備，天地官矣。
夫孝，置之而塞乎天地，溥之而横乎四海，施諸後世而無朝夕。推而放諸東海而準，推而放諸西海而準，推而放諸南海而準，推而放諸北海而準。
明其義者，君也。
第貳塲
論
聖神繼天立極。
詔誥表〔内科一道〕
擬漢明帝幸辟雍行大射養老禮詔〔永平二年〕。
擬唐以韓愈爲京兆尹誥〔長慶三年〕。
擬宋輯《尚書》所載事作《敬天圖》成，輔臣賀表〔乾道七年〕。
判語五條。
translation_en:
…[Music] deepens harmony, leads the spirits, and accords with Heaven; ritual distinguishes what is appropriate, gives the ghosts their places, and accords with Earth. Thus the sage creates music to respond to Heaven and establishes ritual to match Earth. When ritual and music are manifest and complete, Heaven and Earth fulfill their offices.
As for filial piety, establish it and it fills Heaven and Earth; extend it and it reaches across the Four Seas; apply it to later generations and it holds at all times. Extend and apply it to the eastern sea, and it is the standard; extend and apply it to the western sea, and it is the standard; extend and apply it to the southern sea, and it is the standard; extend and apply it to the northern sea, and it is the standard.
One who understands its meaning is a ruler.
Second Session
Discourse
The sage of divine wisdom carries on Heaven’s work and establishes the supreme standard.
Edicts, proclamations, and memorials 〔One topic in the section [?].〕
Compose an edict as if issued when Emperor Ming of the Han visited the Biyong imperial academy and performed the ceremonies of the Great Archery Contest and honoring the elderly. 〔Second year of Yongping, 59.〕
Compose a proclamation as if issued by the Tang appointing Han Yu Metropolitan Governor of Jingzhao. 〔Third year of Changqing, 823.〕
Compose a congratulatory memorial from the chief ministers as if presented upon the Song court’s completion of the Illustrations of Reverence for Heaven (Jingtian tu), compiled from events recorded in the Book of Documents. 〔Seventh year of Qiandao, 1171.〕
Five legal judgments.

title: 隆慶元年應天府鄉試錄
text:
上書奏事犯諱
監臨勢要中鹽
關防内使出入
赦前斷罪不當
織造違禁段疋
第叅場
策五道
問書曰兢兢業業一日二日萬幾又曰學
于古訓乃有獲自古帝王之治天下必
以勤政務學爲本由堯舜至周成王可
===
考而知也三代而下政與學爲二事然
亦有齋居决事日昃罷朝詢問政事夜
以繼日者有几杖執業吏日侍讀首召
大儒說書崇政者其於古帝王之政之
學何如耶洪惟我
太祖高皇帝
成祖文皇帝創業埀統致帝王之治功崇文體
道紹帝王之心學�POSTIER
punctuated:
上書奏事犯諱。
監臨勢要中鹽。
關防内使出入。
赦前斷罪不當。
織造違禁段疋。

第叅場
策五道

問：書曰：「兢兢業業，一日二日萬幾。」又曰：「學于古訓，乃有獲。」自古帝王之治天下，必以勤政務學爲本，由堯舜至周成王，可考而知也。三代而下，政與學爲二事，然亦有齋居决事、日昃罷朝、詢問政事夜以繼日者，有几杖執業、吏日侍讀、首召大儒、說書崇政者，其於古帝王之政之學何如耶？洪惟我太祖高皇帝、成祖文皇帝，創業埀統，致帝王之治功；崇文體道，紹帝王之心學�POSTIER
translation_en:
Submitting a written report to the throne that violates a taboo on imperial names.
Supervisory officials and powerful persons obtaining salt-trading rights.
Controlling the entry and exit of palace eunuchs.
Improper adjudication of offenses before an amnesty.
Weaving prohibited silk fabrics.

Third Session
Five Policy Questions

Question: The Book of Documents says: “Be cautious and diligent: in a day or two, myriad affairs demand attention.” It also says: “Study the teachings of antiquity, and you will gain understanding.” Since antiquity, emperors and kings governing All under Heaven have invariably taken diligence in government and devotion to learning as their foundation. This can be known by examining the period from Yao and Shun down to King Cheng of Zhou. After the Three Dynasties, government and learning became separate pursuits. Yet there were still rulers who decided affairs while dwelling in ritual seclusion, dismissed court only when the sun was declining, or inquired into government affairs by night as well as by day. There were also those who provided stools and staffs for teachers imparting instruction [?], had officials attend daily to read to them, summoned eminent Confucian scholars as their first priority, or held expositions of the classics in the Chongzheng Hall. How did their government and learning compare with those of the emperors and kings of antiquity?

We reverently reflect that our Emperor Taizu Gao and Emperor Chengzu Wen founded the imperial enterprise and transmitted its succession, attaining the achievements in government of the ancient emperors and kings. They honored cultural learning and embodied the Way, continuing the ancient emperors’ and kings’ learning of the mind [corrupt text: �POSTIER] …

title: 隆慶元年應天府鄉試錄
text:
訓諭咨諸臣直與典謨相表裏也可得而鋪
張其盛與我
皇上嗣承大統
恭己臨朝
虛懷納諫
開講筵以陳治道
視太學以重師儒孜孜勤政務學之念蓋與
二祖同一揆者天下固拭目以仰維新之化矣
然舜禹大聖諸臣矢謨儆戒交至誠忠
愛無已也即今侍從論思之臣期所以
===
為
聖政
聖學之助其道安在爾諸士必有槩於中者其
敷陳之將以轉聞於
上
問史記曰謚者行之迹行出於已名生於
人語謚法也前所未有周公創之宋儒
有言春秋孔子之刑書語書法也前所
punctuated:
訓諭咨諸臣，直與典謨相表裏也，可得而鋪張其盛與？我皇上嗣承大統，恭己臨朝，虛懷納諫，開講筵以陳治道，視太學以重師儒，孜孜勤政務學之念，蓋與二祖同一揆者。天下固拭目以仰維新之化矣。然舜禹大聖，諸臣矢謨，儆戒交至，誠忠愛無已也。即今侍從論思之臣，期所以為聖政、聖學之助，其道安在？爾諸士必有槩於中者，其敷陳之，將以轉聞於上。

問：《史記》曰：「謚者，行之迹；行出於已，名生於人。」語謚法也。前所未有，周公創之。宋儒有言：「春秋，孔子之刑書。」語書法也。前所
translation_en:
…Their instructions and admonitions addressed to their ministers directly complement the Canons and Counsels. Can you expound their magnificence in full? Our Emperor has succeeded to the imperial line. With reverent bearing he presides at court; with an open mind he accepts remonstrance. He convenes imperial lectures to elucidate the way of government and visits the Imperial University to honor teachers and Confucian scholars. His unflagging devotion to diligent government and earnest study surely accords with the same principles as those of the two ancestral emperors. All under Heaven indeed look eagerly upward for the transforming influence of renewed rule. Yet even with such great sages as Shun and Yu, their ministers presented counsels, and warnings and admonitions came from every side: truly, their loyalty and loving concern knew no end. Where, then, lies the way by which the present attendant ministers, charged with deliberation and counsel, may assist His Majesty’s governance and learning? You scholars must have some understanding of this in your hearts. Set it forth fully, so that it may be conveyed to His Majesty.

Question: The Records of the Grand Historian says: “A posthumous name is the trace of one’s conduct. Conduct proceeds from oneself; reputation arises from others.” This refers to the rules for conferring posthumous names. Previously nonexistent, these were created by the Duke of Zhou. A Confucian scholar of the Song said: “The Spring and Autumn Annals is Confucius’s book of punishments.” This refers to its principles of historical writing. Previously…

title: 隆慶元年應天府鄉試錄
text:
未有孔子任之兩聖立法不同各有主
謂也諸士學周孔之學嘗深繹其旨與
後周公者爲謚至十有五家後孔子者
爲書至二十有一史若此非寸晷所能
悉數也亦可得而指其槩與說者謂後
之謚與書互有得失信乎否與將明其
說必証以事試舉一二可疑辨者若臧
孫辰管夷吾呂賈充許敬宗人各有謚董
宣諸葛亮李義甫柳宗元事見於書其
===
得失安在也辨乎此即一可知百矣無
亦諸人之外可維舉而互評之與夫謚
以尊名得之爲榮書以紀續錄之爲美
乃古人之言曰周公作謚法而孝子慈
孫不能改孔子作書法而亂臣賊子不
得肆則凜之乎其可畏也已夫善惡定
於心行謚書徵諸久遠逈往昔千百年
之故以垂後來千百年之鑒當事者將
持此兩端風世願相與求立法之原其
punctuated: 未有，孔子任之。兩聖立法不同，各有主謂也。諸士學周孔之學，嘗深繹其旨與？後周公者，爲謚至十有五家；後孔子者，爲書至二十有一史。若此，非寸晷所能悉數也，亦可得而指其槩與？說者謂後之謚與書互有得失，信乎否與？將明其說，必証以事。試舉一二可疑辨者：若臧孫辰、管夷吾、呂賈充、許敬宗，人各有謚；董宣、諸葛亮、李義甫、柳宗元，事見於書。其得失安在也？辨乎此，即一可知百矣。無亦諸人之外，可維舉而互評之與？夫謚以尊名，得之爲榮；書以紀續，錄之爲美。乃古人之言曰：「周公作謚法，而孝子慈孫不能改；孔子作書法，而亂臣賊子不得肆。」則凜之乎，其可畏也已！夫善惡定於心行，謚書徵諸久遠，逈往昔千百年之故，以垂後來千百年之鑒。當事者將持此兩端風世，願相與求立法之原，其
translation_en:
…had not previously existed; Confucius undertook it. The two sages established different rules, each with a particular purpose. You candidates study the teachings of the Duke of Zhou and Confucius: have you ever pondered their meaning deeply? Those who followed the Duke of Zhou produced as many as fifteen schools of writings on posthumous names; those who followed Confucius produced as many as twenty-one histories. These cannot all be enumerated in a brief moment, but might you outline their general features? Some maintain that later posthumous naming and historical writing each have their successes and failings. Is this true or not? To elucidate this claim, you must substantiate it with actual cases.

Let us raise one or two cases open to doubt and debate. Zangsun Chen, Guan Yiwu, Lü Jia Chong [?], and Xu Jingzong each received a posthumous name; the deeds of Dong Xuan, Zhuge Liang, Li Yifu, and Liu Zongyuan appear in historical writings. Where do the successes and failings lie? By discerning these, you can understand a hundred cases from a single one. Might you also adduce examples beyond these men and assess them comparatively [?]?

Posthumous names dignify a person's name, and receiving one is an honor; historical writings record the succession of events, and inclusion in them is considered a distinction. Yet the ancients said: “The Duke of Zhou established the rules for posthumous naming, and filial sons and loving grandsons could not alter them; Confucius established the rules for historical writing, and rebellious ministers and treacherous sons could no longer act without restraint.” How this inspires dread—how fearsome it is! Good and evil are determined by one's intentions and conduct; posthumous names and historical writings bear witness to them across the ages, reaching back [?] to events hundreds and thousands of years past to transmit lessons for hundreds and thousands of years to come. Those responsible for affairs intend to use these two means to influence the world. We hope that you will together investigate the original principles underlying the establishment of these rules, and …

title: 隆慶元年應天府鄉試錄
text:
柔者于篇毋剿陳言而可
問序氣成物助流政敎昭德參功樂之爲
用莫大焉英莖之制美哉邈矣術家制
尺較黍之類言近繁瑣姑舉其大者訴
之宋儒有言寓器以聲當求之聲而不
當求之器者有言審音之難不在於聲
而在於律不在於宮而在於黃鍾者可
指而言與黃鍾之長九寸其說何所昉
與其損益相生可得聞與其果然與又
===
有謂黃鍾爲三寸九分者亦有所本與
其損益相生之論視黃鍾九寸者同與
否與其清濁之辨多少之數果孰爲當
與彼作爲通解鍾律律呂新書者其中
亦有相發明者與在昔有得牛鐸而知
爲黃鍾之宮得玉磬而識爲黃鍾之缺
者豈以
明盛之世而顧無神解其人乎此固主司者
所欲聞也
punctuated:
柔者于篇，毋剿陳言而可。

問：序氣成物，助流政敎，昭德參功，樂之爲用莫大焉。英莖之制，美哉，邈矣！術家制尺較黍之類，言近繁瑣，姑舉其大者訴之。宋儒有言寓器以聲，當求之聲而不當求之器者；有言審音之難，不在於聲而在於律，不在於宮而在於黃鍾者。可指而言與？黃鍾之長九寸，其說何所昉與？其損益相生，可得聞與？其果然與？又有謂黃鍾爲三寸九分者，亦有所本與？其損益相生之論，視黃鍾九寸者，同與否與？其清濁之辨、多少之數，果孰爲當與？彼作爲《通解鍾律》《律呂新書》者，其中亦有相發明者與？在昔有得牛鐸而知爲黃鍾之宮，得玉磬而識爲黃鍾之缺者，豈以明盛之世而顧無神解其人乎？此固主司者所欲聞也。
translation_en:
…set this forth in your essay [?]; simply refrain from plagiarizing stale expressions.

Question: In ordering the vital energies and bringing things to completion, assisting the spread of government and instruction, manifesting virtue and contributing to achievement, nothing surpasses the efficacy of music. How beautiful, yet how remote, are the musical institutions of Ying and Jing! Such matters as specialists’ construction of measuring rules and comparison of millet grains tend toward excessive minutiae in their discussion. Let us therefore raise the principal issues for consideration.

Some Song Confucian scholars said that sound is lodged in instruments, and that one should seek it in sound rather than in the instruments. Others said that the difficulty of discerning musical tones lies not in sound but in pitch standards, and not in the gong note but in Huangzhong, the Yellow Bell pitch. Can you explain these statements specifically? Where did the claim that the Huangzhong pitch pipe is nine cun long originate? May we hear how the pitches generate one another through diminution and augmentation? Is this account indeed correct?

Others maintain that the Huangzhong pipe measures three cun and nine fen. Does this too have a basis? Is their account of the successive generation of pitches through diminution and augmentation the same as that of those who hold that Huangzhong measures nine cun, or is it different? In distinguishing high and low tones and determining numerical quantities, which account is actually correct? Do the works Comprehensive Explanation of Bells and Pitch Standards [?] and New Book on Pitch Standards contain discussions that illuminate one another?

In former times, there were people who, on obtaining a cattle bell, recognized it as the gong note of Huangzhong, and who, on obtaining a jade chime stone, recognized it as supplying what was missing from Huangzhong. Could it be that in this enlightened and flourishing age there is nevertheless no one with such inspired understanding? This is precisely what those presiding over the examination wish to hear.

title: 隆慶元年應天府鄉試錄
text:
問古之君子以一身任天下之重則視天
下事若叢脞委於身而不容辭其規畫
劑量爲計慮深遠矣不必俟其位遇隆
而職任及也唐陸宣公嘗以五術八計
三科四賦六德五要說黜陟使者而宋
范文正公亦嘗以朝政得失民間利病
爲萬言書上宰相于時二公所居職末
矣而志慮弘遠若此可得而言其槩與
二公訖爲唐宋名相其居位所建白質
===
言成信固未易更僕數也若宣公所陳
馭吏恤民備邊之三疏及文正公對天
章閣後所上之十事磊磊皆深言至計
不知與前所論亦出一揆與夫以二公
之才之節三代而下可謂純臣當其柄
用君心之所虛佇天下之所想望何如
也乃竟不得久於其位以盡行其言何
與今其言炳炳具在後之經世者取資
焉不知其學亦有所本與古今人非不
punctuated: 問：古之君子以一身任天下之重，則視天下事若叢脞委於身而不容辭，其規畫劑量，爲計慮深遠矣，不必俟其位遇隆而職任及也。唐陸宣公嘗以五術、八計、三科、四賦、六德、五要說黜陟使者，而宋范文正公亦嘗以朝政得失、民間利病爲萬言書上宰相。于時二公所居職末矣，而志慮弘遠若此，可得而言其槩與？二公訖爲唐宋名相，其居位所建白，質言成信，固未易更僕數也。若宣公所陳馭吏、恤民、備邊之三疏，及文正公對天章閣後所上之十事，磊磊皆深言至計，不知與前所論亦出一揆與？夫以二公之才之節，三代而下可謂純臣。當其柄用，君心之所虛佇、天下之所想望何如也！乃竟不得久於其位，以盡行其言，何與？今其言炳炳具在，後之經世者取資焉，不知其學亦有所本與？古今人非不
translation_en:
Question: When gentlemen of antiquity took upon themselves the weighty responsibilities of the realm, they regarded its affairs, however numerous and minute, as entrusted to them personally, with no possibility of declining. Their planning and assessment were profound and far-reaching; they did not have to wait until they attained high position and favor, or until their official responsibilities extended to these matters. Lu Xuangong of the Tang (Lu Zhi) once addressed a commissioner for demotions and promotions concerning five methods, eight measures, three categories, four levies, six virtues, and five essentials. Fan Wenzhenggong of the Song (Fan Zhongyan) likewise submitted to the chief councilor a letter of ten thousand words concerning the successes and failures of court government and the benefits and hardships experienced by the people. At the time, both men held minor posts, yet their aspirations and deliberations were so broad and far-reaching. Can you explain their main outlines?

The two eventually became celebrated chief councilors of the Tang and Song. The proposals they submitted while in office, their substantive words and demonstrated trustworthiness [?], would certainly be difficult to enumerate even with successive relays of attendants. Consider Xuangong’s three memorials on managing officials, caring for the people, and preparing frontier defenses, and the ten proposals Wenzhenggong submitted after his audience in the Tianzhang Pavilion: each was an outstanding example of profound counsel and consummate planning. Did these proceed from the same principles as their earlier arguments?

With their talents and integrity, these two men may be called ministers of unsullied loyalty among those who lived after the Three Dynasties. When they wielded authority, how eagerly their rulers awaited their counsel with receptive minds, and how great were the expectations of the realm! Why, then, were they ultimately unable to remain long in office and put all their recommendations into effect? Their words now survive in full, clear and brilliant, and later practitioners of statecraft draw upon them. Did their learning also have a fundamental source? It is not that people of ancient and modern times cannot …

title: 隆慶元年應天府鄉試錄
text:
相及諸士抱藝而來志於用世豈無有
以天下自任如鄉先哲二公者乎願相
與究析之評古有徵即施於政者可知
也
問學者明體貴適用適用貴濟時諸士學
成而待用者也如或用爾則何以哉今
聖天子御極際
中興之運執更化之權君子湍朝圖惟治理
欲置民以安固有日不暇給者而議者
猶以爲民未安也豈法制之初令行未
遍民未受其賜與何天災之不常而水
火盜賊之數數見也司農告匱
===
國用不充必取充於民乎且民何以自給也
語曰開財源節財流莫民事爲急也無
乃宂食者耗之與富與教兩者不相離
今時士風所尚有害於農者否與治民
者吏也今之吏治亦既振飭乃其弊猶
有存而未袪何者爲最甚也夫政繁則
punctuated:
相及。諸士抱藝而來，志於用世，豈無有以天下自任如鄉先哲二公者乎？願相與究析之。評古有徵，即施於政者可知也。
問：學者明體貴適用，適用貴濟時。諸士學成而待用者也，如或用爾，則何以哉？今聖天子御極，際中興之運，執更化之權，君子湍朝，圖惟治理，欲置民以安，固有日不暇給者。而議者猶以爲民未安也，豈法制之初，令行未遍，民未受其賜與？何天災之不常，而水火盜賊之數數見也？司農告匱，國用不充，必取充於民乎？且民何以自給也？語曰：開財源，節財流。莫民事爲急也，無乃宂食者耗之與？富與教，兩者不相離，今時士風所尚，有害於農者否與？治民者，吏也。今之吏治亦既振飭，乃其弊猶有存而未袪，何者爲最甚也？夫政繁則
translation_en:
…equal one another. You gentlemen have come bearing your scholarly accomplishments, intent on serving the world. Are there none among you who take responsibility for all under Heaven, as did those two earlier worthies of our region? I hope you will examine and analyze these matters together. If your assessment of the past rests on evidence, its applications to government can also be understood.
Question: For scholars, understanding fundamental principles should lead to practical application, and practical application should meet the needs of the times. You gentlemen have completed your studies and await appointment. If someone were to employ you, what would you do? Now the sagely Son of Heaven occupies the throne at a time of dynastic resurgence and holds the authority to reform governance. Worthy men fill the court [?], deliberating on how to bring about good government. In seeking to secure peace for the people, they indeed find the days too short for all that must be done. Yet critics still consider the people unsettled. Is this because the laws and institutions are newly established, their commands have not yet been implemented everywhere, and the people have not yet received their benefits? Why are natural disasters so unpredictable, and why do floods, fires, and banditry occur so frequently? The Minister of Revenue reports depleted reserves. If funds for state expenditure are insufficient, must the shortfall be made up by levies on the people? And how, then, are the people to provide for themselves? As the saying goes, open up sources of revenue and restrain its outflow. Nothing is more urgent than the people's livelihood. Could it be that those who consume without productive employment are draining these resources? Enriching the people and educating them cannot be separated. Do the values currently esteemed among scholars include anything harmful to agriculture? Officials govern the people. The administration of officials has already been reinvigorated and put in order, yet some abuses persist and have not been eliminated. Which are the most serious? For when governmental measures become overcomplicated, then …

title: 隆慶元年應天府鄉試錄
text:
民亂當必有易簡之道逞于法制之外
者茲欲收人心彌天災足國儲修兵政
釐士習核吏治而使天下之民舉安願
悉陳其實求其要歸以觀作用如何諸
士其明以復我
punctuated: 民亂，當必有易簡之道逞于法制之外者。茲欲收人心，彌天災，足國儲，修兵政，釐士習，核吏治，而使天下之民舉安，願悉陳其實，求其要歸，以觀作用如何。諸士其明以復我！
translation_en: …the people fall into disorder. Surely there must be a way of ease and simplicity that operates beyond laws and regulations [?]. Now we seek to win the people’s hearts, mitigate natural calamities, replenish state reserves, improve military administration, rectify the habits of scholars, and scrutinize the administration of officials, so that all the people under Heaven may enjoy peace. Please set forth the actual circumstances fully and identify the essential principles, so that we may see how these measures would work in practice. You scholars, reply to me clearly!

title: 隆慶元年應天府鄉試錄
text:
第壹場
四書
子貢問政子曰足食足兵民信之矣
周汝礪
同考試官教諭楊　批〔體格高古辭氣冲雅可以見經世之略矣錄之〕
同考試官推官沈　批〔體格雄渾筆力峻古辭意精鑿不當以時□□之宜錄爲式〕
考試官左中允孫　批〔是實知政體者〕
考試官左諭德王　批〔詞理精確宜冠多士〕
===
聖人與賢者言政皆庇民之實也夫政因乎民
者也其端有三而以爲民庇則均焉王道之全
蓋如此且夫學而入政聖賢濟世之本心政在
庇民王人經國之大務子貢之材達乎政矣乃
問於孔子豈非以今之從政者舉失其道而夫
子之得邦家當必有見諸行事者耶孔子曰民
之生聚於斯而仰給乎上者謂可恃以無饑也
食不足則無恒心矣故必因民之利制國之用
punctuated:
第壹場
四書
「子貢問政。子曰：『足食，足兵，民信之矣。』」
周汝礪
同考試官教諭楊，批〔體格高古，辭氣冲雅，可以見經世之略矣。錄之。〕
同考試官推官沈，批〔體格雄渾，筆力峻古，辭意精鑿，不當以時□□之，宜錄爲式。〕
考試官左中允孫，批〔是實知政體者。〕
考試官左諭德王，批〔詞理精確，宜冠多士。〕

聖人與賢者言政，皆庇民之實也。夫政因乎民者也，其端有三，而以爲民庇則均焉。王道之全，蓋如此。且夫學而入政，聖賢濟世之本心；政在庇民，王人經國之大務。子貢之材達乎政矣，乃問於孔子，豈非以今之從政者舉失其道，而夫子之得邦家，當必有見諸行事者耶？孔子曰：「民之生聚於斯，而仰給乎上者，謂可恃以無饑也。食不足，則無恒心矣。故必因民之利，制國之用，
translation_en:
First Session
Four Books

“Zigong asked about government. The Master said: ‘Sufficient food, sufficient military forces, and the people’s trust in their ruler.’”

Zhou Ruli

Associate Examiner Yang, Instructor, comments: 〔“The composition is lofty and antique in form, its language restrained and elegant. Here one can discern a strategy for ordering the world. Select it.”〕
Associate Examiner Shen, Judge, comments: 〔“The composition is powerful and full in form, its writing forceful and antique, its language and ideas precise and penetrating. It should not be judged by contemporary … [?]. Select it as a model.”〕
Examiner Sun, Left Assistant Director of Instruction, comments: 〔“Here is someone who truly understands the essentials of government.”〕
Examiner Wang, Left Adviser to the Heir Apparent, comments: 〔“Its language and reasoning are precise. It deserves to rank first among the candidates.”〕

When the sage speaks of government with a worthy man, all that he discusses concerns the concrete means of protecting the people. Government takes the people as its basis. It has three principal elements, and all alike serve to protect the people. Such, indeed, is the completeness of the kingly Way. To study and then enter government is the fundamental intention of sages and worthies in bringing aid to the world; to make government serve the protection of the people is the great task of the king’s servants in ordering the state. Zigong’s abilities qualified him for government, yet he questioned Confucius. Was this not because those governing in his day had all lost the proper way, whereas, if the Master obtained a state or a noble house to govern, he would surely have principles to put into practice?

Confucius said: “The people live and gather here, looking to those above to provide for them because they believe they can rely on them to remain free from hunger. If food is insufficient, they will have no constancy of heart. Thus one must build upon what benefits the people and regulate the state’s expenditure …

title: 隆慶元年應天府鄉試錄
text:
使其三年耕有一年之蓄九年耕有三年之蓄
而豐歉胥賴焉此先王養民之政所宜行也民
之安處於斯而仰藉乎上者謂可恃以無恐也
兵不足則無固志矣故必乘國之暇修民之備
使其無事爲比閭族黨之人有事爲伍兩卒旅
之衆而緩急胥賴焉此先王衛民之政所宜行
也若夫彰信兆民先王之大政寓兵食之間者
也既富矣因加之以教有勇矣且使之知方居
常而粟米力役之征莫不用情焉信之結於束
===
也遇變而饑饉師旅之加莫不用命焉信之積
於素也使兵食足而不施信於民則雖有粟惡
得而食有兵其誰與守哉賜欲行政修此三者
故全也吁孔子語子貢王政之常而通變宜民
之權可知所辨矣於從政乎何有嘗謂論治有
要識體爲先行政有經信心爲上兵食信三者
豈足矣然非小信爲也在有庇民之實心而晉
之伐原秦之徙木不與焉不然列國之政務在
富强孰不假信爲名而何離叛之民之不可止
punctuated:
使其三年耕有一年之蓄，九年耕有三年之蓄，而豐歉胥賴焉，此先王養民之政所宜行也。民之安處於斯而仰藉乎上者，謂可恃以無恐也。兵不足則無固志矣，故必乘國之暇，修民之備，使其無事爲比閭族黨之人，有事爲伍兩卒旅之衆，而緩急胥賴焉，此先王衛民之政所宜行也。若夫彰信兆民，先王之大政寓兵食之間者也。既富矣，因加之以教；有勇矣，且使之知方。居常而粟米力役之征，莫不用情焉，信之結於束也；遇變而饑饉師旅之加，莫不用命焉，信之積於素也。使兵食足而不施信於民，則雖有粟，惡得而食？有兵，其誰與守哉？賜欲行政，修此三者，故全也。
吁！孔子語子貢王政之常，而通變宜民之權，可知所辨矣，於從政乎何有？嘗謂論治有要，識體爲先；行政有經，信心爲上。兵食信三者，豈足矣？然非小信爲也，在有庇民之實心，而晉之伐原、秦之徙木不與焉。不然，列國之政務在富强，孰不假信爲名，而何離叛之民之不可止
translation_en:
…so that three years of cultivation yield reserves for one year, and nine years of cultivation yield reserves for three years, on which the people can rely in both abundant and lean years. This is the former kings’ policy for nourishing the people, which ought to be implemented. The people dwell here in peace and look to those above for support because they believe they can rely on them to be free from fear. If military provision is insufficient, the people will lack steadfast resolve. Thus one must take advantage of the state’s leisure to prepare the people’s defenses, so that in peaceful times they belong to the neighborhood groupings of bi, lü, zu, and dang, and in times of trouble they form the military units of wu, liang, zu, and lü. These arrangements can be relied upon in ordinary times and emergencies alike. This is the former kings’ policy for protecting the people, which ought to be implemented. As for making good faith manifest to the multitude, this great policy of the former kings is embedded in the provision of troops and food. Once the people have been enriched, instruction should follow; once they possess courage, they should also be made to understand the right direction. In ordinary times, levies of grain and labor are invariably administered with regard for the people’s circumstances: trust is thereby bound together [?]. When calamity strikes and famine or warfare is visited upon them, all obey commands: this is because trust has been accumulated in ordinary times. If troops and food are sufficient but good faith is not shown to the people, then even if there is grain, how can one obtain it to eat? Even if there are troops, who will join in defending the state? Ci, if you wish to administer government, attend to these three things, and it will thus be complete.
Ah! Confucius told Zigong the constant principles of kingly government; from these one can discern the discretionary judgment needed to respond to change and act fittingly for the people. What difficulty, then, would there be in taking part in government? I have often said that discussion of governance has its essentials, foremost among them recognizing its fundamental structure; administering government has its enduring principles, foremost among them a trustworthy heart. Can these three—troops, food, and trust—suffice? Yet this is not a matter of petty displays of good faith. It depends upon a sincere intention to shelter the people; Jin’s attack on Yuan and Qin’s moving of the timber do not belong in this category. Otherwise, since the governments of the various states were intent upon wealth and power, which of them did not borrow the name of good faith? And why could the people’s estrangement and rebellion not be stopped…

title: 隆慶元年應天府鄉試錄
text:
耶傳曰信國之寶也民之所庇也諒矣
知所以脩身則知所以治人知所以治人
則知所以治天下國家矣凡爲天下國
家有九經曰脩身也
吳達聰
同考試官教諭蔣　批〔脩身爲用人行政之本孔子通章要指結上起下正在數語此文精〕
同考試官知州楊　批〔格古詞精發題脩身義貫徹而詞復粹古他作無與並者〕
之意最爲明盡誦之惕然深省非徒以其文者
===
宜錄以傳
考試官左中允孫　批〔有忠愛意〕
考試官左諭德王　批〔以古文發時義非凡作也〕
聖人望君以身治天下而因指其爲先務焉蓋
治天下有本身之謂也人君所當務孰有先於
此哉此孔子對魯君一篇之大指也意曰爲政
之事多端求治之則不遠吾謂以人立政而不
可以不脩身者君之身道德之宗天下國家之
punctuated:
耶？傳曰：「信，國之寶也，民之所庇也。」諒矣！

知所以脩身，則知所以治人；知所以治人，則知所以治天下國家矣。凡爲天下國家有九經，曰脩身也。

吳達聰

同考試官教諭蔣，批〔脩身爲用人行政之本，孔子通章要指，結上起下，正在數語。此文精〕
同考試官知州楊，批〔格古詞精，發題脩身義貫徹，而詞復粹古，他作無與並者。〕
之意最爲明盡，誦之惕然深省，非徒以其文者，宜錄以傳。
考試官左中允孫，批〔有忠愛意。〕
考試官左諭德王，批〔以古文發時義，非凡作也。〕

聖人望君以身治天下，而因指其爲先務焉。蓋治天下有本，身之謂也。人君所當務，孰有先於此哉？此孔子對魯君一篇之大指也。意曰：爲政之事多端，求治之則不遠。吾謂以人立政，而不可以不脩身者，君之身，道德之宗，天下國家之
translation_en:
…indeed? The Commentary says: “Trustworthiness is the treasure of the state and that which shelters the people.” Truly so!

“When one knows how to cultivate oneself, one knows how to govern others; when one knows how to govern others, one knows how to govern the world, states, and families. There are nine guiding principles for governing the world, states, and families: self-cultivation…”

Wu Dacong

Associate Examiner Jiang, Instructor, comments: “Self-cultivation is the foundation for employing men and conducting government. The essential purport of Confucius’s entire chapter, linking what precedes to what follows, lies precisely in these few words. This essay is refined…” [?]
Associate Examiner Yang, Department Magistrate, comments: “Its form is antique and its language precise. In developing the theme, the meaning of self-cultivation runs throughout, while the language is also pure and antique. No other composition can equal it.”
“…the meaning is expressed with the utmost clarity and completeness. Reading it aloud prompts an awakened sense of caution and profound reflection, beyond mere appreciation of its literary qualities. It should be recorded and transmitted.” [The placement and connection of this continuation are uncertain.]
Examiner Sun, Left Rectifier, comments: “It conveys loyalty and loving concern.”
Examiner Wang, Left Admonisher, comments: “It uses ancient prose to elucidate the meaning of the examination theme. This is no ordinary composition.”

The Sage expected the ruler to govern the world through his own person, and accordingly identified this as his foremost task. For governing the world has a foundation: one’s own person. Among the tasks incumbent upon a ruler, what could take precedence over this? Such is the central purport of the entire passage in which Confucius replies to the ruler of Lu. Its meaning is this: the affairs of government are manifold, but the standard by which good government is sought is not far away. When I say that government is established through men and that one therefore cannot neglect self-cultivation, it is because the ruler’s person is the fountainhead of the Way and virtue, and the … of the world, states, and families…

title: 隆慶元年應天府鄉試錄
text:
主也信能知德之所從入而先明諸心體道之
所以行而愼厥身脩矣由是而治人人亦身也
其分雖殊其所以治之者在我德可使入道可
使行因此通彼舉而加之無難也由是而治天
下國家天下國家皆人也其勢雖渙其所以治
之者則同德與俱入道與俱行以一觀萬推而
廣之無異也夫身脩而天下國家治則君立而
政舉矣若此者非始望於今日也主治之大凡
也非直施於一時也保治之常經也其目有九
其一維何不遠曰天下國家也天下觀於國而
===
觀於家而觀於身責有所必歸此其揆事宰物
之本非不曰天下國家也由身及於家以及於
國以及於天下務有所當急此其求端用力之
方道率人性之同而身蹈之斯爲道天地立君
以來未之有改也德主天下之善而身得之斯
爲德帝王致治之盛由此其選也使不先脩其
身而他務之是亟不知其一焉知其九惡能治
天下國家抑此萬世法程之訓也周文武之所
punctuated: 主也。信能知德之所從入而先明諸心，體道之所以行而愼厥身，脩矣。由是而治人，人亦身也；其分雖殊，其所以治之者在我。德可使入，道可使行，因此通彼，舉而加之，無難也。由是而治天下國家，天下國家皆人也；其勢雖渙，其所以治之者則同。德與俱入，道與俱行，以一觀萬，推而廣之，無異也。夫身脩而天下國家治，則君立而政舉矣。若此者，非始望於今日也，主治之大凡也；非直施於一時也，保治之常經也。其目有九，其一維何？不遠。曰天下國家也，天下觀於國，而觀於家，而觀於身，責有所必歸，此其揆事宰物之本。非不曰天下國家也，由身及於家，以及於國，以及於天下，務有所當急，此其求端用力之方。道率人性之同，而身蹈之，斯爲道，天地立君以來未之有改也。德主天下之善，而身得之，斯爲德，帝王致治之盛由此其選也。使不先脩其身，而他務之是亟，不知其一，焉知其九？惡能治天下國家？抑此萬世法程之訓也。周文武之所
translation_en:
…master. If he can truly understand how virtue is entered into and first illuminate it in his heart, comprehend how the Way is put into practice and exercise care over his own person, then his person will be cultivated. From this he proceeds to govern others. Others, too, are persons; although their stations differ, the means of governing them lie within me. They can be brought to enter into virtue and to practice the Way. Connecting their case with one's own and extending this to them presents no difficulty. From this he proceeds to govern all under Heaven, the state, and the family. All under Heaven, the state, and the family consist entirely of people. Although their circumstances are dispersed, the means of governing them are the same. Together with them he enters into virtue; together with them he practices the Way. Viewing the myriad through the one and extending this more broadly involves no difference.

When the person is cultivated and all under Heaven, the state, and the family are well governed, the ruler is established and government is carried out. Such expectations are not first placed upon him today: this is the general principle of presiding over government. Nor does it apply only at a particular time: it is the constant rule for preserving good government. Its principal articles number nine. What is the first? It is not far away. We speak of all under Heaven, the state, and the family: all under Heaven looks to the state, then to the family, then to the person. Responsibility must ultimately come to rest somewhere; this is the foundation for assessing affairs and directing things. It is not that we do not speak of all under Heaven, the state, and the family. Rather, one proceeds from the person to the family, then to the state, then to all under Heaven. Among one's tasks, something must take priority; this is the method of seeking the starting point and applying one's efforts.

The Way follows what is common to human nature, and only when one personally treads it does it constitute the Way. Since Heaven and Earth established rulers, this has never changed. Virtue takes as its guiding principle the goodness of all under Heaven, and only when one personally attains it does it constitute virtue. The flourishing government achieved by emperors and kings derived its excellence from this. If a ruler does not first cultivate his person but instead treats other tasks as urgent, then, not knowing the first, how can he know the nine? How could he govern all under Heaven, the state, and the family? Indeed, this is an admonition that serves as a standard for all ages. That by which Kings Wen and Wu of Zhou…

title: 隆慶元年應天府鄉試錄
text:
脩其身者曰敬止曰敬勝至於不顯不聞允致
謹焉不猶所云齊明盛服非禮不動者與能法
乎此而舉方冊之政魯其東周矣固孔子憲章
之初心也後世乃有謂祖宗法不足守者何可
與共政哉
人性之善也猶水之就下也人無有不善
水無有不下
同考試官教授梁　批〔意精到而詞古雅可庶幾〕
===
以式矣
同考試官教授趙　批〔發明性善之旨精徹是有功於孟子者〕
同考試官知州陳　批〔以水喻性乃孟子因告子之所明而折之是作發揮精透場中絕少〕
考試官左中允孫　批〔莊雅明潔不類衆作〕
考試官左諭德王　批〔說性善意親切〕
大賢即喻以明人性之善而決其無不善焉甚
矣人性之本善也觀於水之必下而性善不亦
punctuated:
脩其身者，曰敬止，曰敬勝，至於不顯不聞，允致謹焉。不猶所云齊明盛服、非禮不動者與？能法乎此而舉方冊之政，魯其東周矣，固孔子憲章之初心也。後世乃有謂祖宗法不足守者，何可與共政哉？

人性之善也，猶水之就下也。人無有不善，水無有不下。

同考試官教授梁　批〔意精到而詞古雅，可庶幾〕以式矣。
同考試官教授趙　批〔發明性善之旨精徹，是有功於孟子者。〕
同考試官知州陳　批〔以水喻性，乃孟子因告子之所明而折之。是作發揮精透，場中絕少。〕
考試官左中允孫　批〔莊雅明潔，不類衆作。〕
考試官左諭德王　批〔說性善意親切。〕

大賢即喻以明人性之善，而決其無不善焉。甚矣，人性之本善也！觀於水之必下，而性善不亦
translation_en:
…in cultivating themselves, spoke of abiding in reverence and of reverence prevailing. Even in what was neither seen nor heard, they exercised the utmost care. Is this not like what is meant by being purified and clear-minded, wearing proper ceremonial dress, and making no movement contrary to ritual propriety? If one could follow this example and put into practice the government recorded in the books, Lu would become an Eastern Zhou. This was indeed Confucius’s original intention in taking those kings as his models. Yet in later ages there have been those who claim that ancestral laws are not worth preserving. How could one share the work of government with them?

“The goodness of human nature is like water’s flowing downward. There is no person who is not good; there is no water that does not flow downward.”

Associate Examiner Liang, Professor, comments: “The ideas are refined and fully developed, and the language is classically elegant. It may almost serve as a model.”
Associate Examiner Zhao, Professor, comments: “Its elucidation of the meaning of the goodness of human nature is penetrating and thorough. This is a contribution to the understanding of Mencius.”
Associate Examiner Chen, Department Magistrate, comments: “In likening human nature to water, Mencius used what Gaozi understood to refute him. This essay develops the point with precision and penetration—something exceedingly rare among the examination essays.”
Examiner Sun, Left Companion to the Heir Apparent, comments: “Dignified, elegant, lucid, and pure; unlike the other compositions.”
Examiner Wang, Left Admonisher to the Heir Apparent, comments: “Its explanation of the goodness of human nature is apt and direct.”

The great worthy takes up the analogy to illuminate the goodness of human nature and establishes conclusively that no human nature is without goodness. How profound is the original goodness of human nature! When we observe that water necessarily flows downward, is not the goodness of human nature also…

title: 隆慶元年應天府鄉試錄
text:
□乎告子以水喻性孟子就而折之曰夫水無
分於東西者其勢也而必分於上下者其性也
故知水之性則知人之性矣吾謂人性之善者
正以猶夫水之下耳蓋原其降衷之初則天之
所繼我者惟善而已至純而無雜也猶夫水曰
潤下其流而不息者性之自得耳夫孰決之而
後行哉本其懿德之好則心之所同然者此善
而已至順而無強也猶夫水之就下其沛然莫
禦者性之自適耳夫孰挽之而可上哉使天下
===
或有不下之水則人亦容有不善之性矣今合
二者觀之均是人則均是善而純粹以精者天
下之性舉相似焉聖人固此善也凡民亦此善
也蓋性命於天本有善而無惡謂之曰人未有
不本乎天者也而豈有不善者哉均是水則均
是下而盈科以進者天下之水舉相似焉河海
固此下也川澮亦此下也蓋水因乎地本宜下
而不宜上謂之曰水未有不行乎地者也而豈
有不下者哉夫知水之無不下則知性之無不
punctuated: □乎？告子以水喻性，孟子就而折之曰：「夫水無分於東西者，其勢也；而必分於上下者，其性也。故知水之性，則知人之性矣。吾謂人性之善者，正以猶夫水之下耳。蓋原其降衷之初，則天之所繼我者惟善而已，至純而無雜也。猶夫水曰潤下，其流而不息者，性之自得耳，夫孰決之而後行哉？本其懿德之好，則心之所同然者此善而已，至順而無強也。猶夫水之就下，其沛然莫禦者，性之自適耳，夫孰挽之而可上哉？使天下或有不下之水，則人亦容有不善之性矣。今合二者觀之，均是人，則均是善，而純粹以精者，天下之性舉相似焉。聖人固此善也，凡民亦此善也。蓋性命於天，本有善而無惡，謂之曰人，未有不本乎天者也，而豈有不善者哉？均是水，則均是下，而盈科以進者，天下之水舉相似焉。河海固此下也，川澮亦此下也。蓋水因乎地，本宜下而不宜上，謂之曰水，未有不行乎地者也，而豈有不下者哉？夫知水之無不下，則知性之無不
translation_en:
…[illegible] [?]? Gaozi used water as an analogy for human nature, and Mengzi took up that analogy to refute him, saying: “That water makes no distinction between east and west is a matter of its circumstances; that it necessarily distinguishes between up and down is a matter of its nature. Thus, knowing the nature of water, one knows human nature. When I speak of the goodness of human nature, I mean precisely that it resembles water’s flowing downward. If we trace back to the beginning, when Heaven bestowed our inner constitution, what Heaven imparted to us was goodness alone, utterly pure and unmixed. It is like the saying that water ‘moistens and descends’: its ceaseless flowing is simply its nature finding fulfillment. Who must first open a channel for it before it will flow? If we consider our fundamental love of admirable virtue, what all hearts alike approve is simply this goodness, utterly natural and unforced. It is like water’s seeking the low ground: its abundant, irresistible flow is simply its nature following its own inclination. Who could pull it upward?

“If there were water anywhere under Heaven that did not flow downward, then one might allow that there were human natures that were not good. Now consider the two together. All alike are human, and therefore all alike are good; in their purity and refinement, the natures of all people under Heaven resemble one another. Sages certainly possess this goodness, and ordinary people possess this same goodness. For nature is ordained by Heaven and originally contains goodness without evil. Of all who are called human, none does not have their origin in Heaven: how, then, could any be without goodness? All alike are water, and therefore all alike flow downward; in filling hollows before advancing, all the waters under Heaven resemble one another. The Yellow River and the seas certainly descend in this way, and streams and channels descend in this same way. For water follows the terrain and is inherently suited to descend, not to ascend. Of all that is called water, none does not flow along the earth: how, then, could any fail to descend? Once one knows that no water fails to descend, one knows that no human nature fails to…

title: 隆慶元年應天府鄉試錄
text:
善斯二者之取類固甚明也而告子乃謂無分
於善不善豈知性之定體固有不可易者哉大
抵水性本下充其下不放乎海不止也人性本
善充其善不至於聖不止也書敘禹治水惟導
之一言謂順其性也順水之性則九河皆可使
至於海率人之性則人皆可以爲堯舜萬世而
下知人之性有善無不善自孟子始故曰孟子
功之在禹下
易
九五飛龍在天利見大人
===
周汝礪
同考試官教諭楊　批〔命意精深措詞俊雅〕
非茂學有〔到佳士佳士〕
同考試官推官沈　批〔發利見意明切宛然〕
盛世氣象錄之
考試官左中允孫　批〔以時字發爻義得肯〕
考試官左諭德王　批〔雄古大作〕
聖人在天子之位而天下仰治者賴焉蓋天子
punctuated:
善，斯二者之取類固甚明也。而告子乃謂無分於善不善，豈知性之定體固有不可易者哉？大抵水性本下，充其下，不放乎海不止也；人性本善，充其善，不至於聖不止也。《書》敘禹治水，惟導之一言，謂順其性也。順水之性，則九河皆可使至於海；率人之性，則人皆可以爲堯舜。萬世而下，知人之性有善無不善，自孟子始，故曰孟子功之在禹下。
易
九五，飛龍在天，利見大人。
周汝礪
同考試官教諭楊，批〔命意精深，措詞俊雅〕非茂學有〔到，佳士，佳士〕。
同考試官推官沈，批〔發利見意明切，宛然〕盛世氣象，錄之。
考試官左中允孫，批〔以時字發爻義，得肯〕。
考試官左諭德王，批〔雄古大作〕。
聖人在天子之位，而天下仰治者賴焉。蓋天子
translation_en:
…good: the analogy between these two is indeed very clear. Yet Gaozi says that human nature makes no distinction between good and not good. How could he understand that nature has a fixed constitution that cannot be altered? In general, water’s nature is originally to flow downward; fully developing this downward tendency, it does not stop until it reaches the sea. Human nature is originally good; fully developing this goodness, it does not stop until it reaches sagehood. In recounting Yu’s control of the waters, the Book of Documents uses the single word “guide,” meaning to follow their nature. By following water’s nature, all nine rivers can be made to reach the sea; by following human nature, everyone can become a Yao or a Shun. For all the ages to come, the understanding that human nature possesses goodness and nothing that is not good began with Mengzi. Thus it is said that Mengzi’s achievement ranks below Yu’s.
Book of Changes
Nine in the fifth place: “A flying dragon in heaven. It is beneficial to see the great man.”
Zhou Ruli
Associate Examiner Yang, Instructor, comments: “The conception is refined and profound; the phrasing is elegant and distinguished. Without extensive learning, [one could not attain this?]—an excellent scholar, an excellent scholar!” [?]
Associate Examiner Shen, Judge, comments: “It develops the meaning of ‘beneficial to see’ clearly and precisely, vividly conveying the atmosphere of a flourishing age. Accept it.”
Examiner Sun, Left Companion to the Heir Apparent, comments: “By using the word ‘timing’ to elucidate the meaning of the line, it grasps the essential point.”
Examiner Wang, Left Admonisher to the Heir Apparent, comments: “A grand composition, powerful and antique in style.”
When a sage occupies the position of Son of Heaven, all under Heaven who look up to him for good government find their support in him. For the Son of Heaven…

title: 隆慶元年應天府鄉試錄
text:
者天下所觀也聖人出而人皆仰之非乾九五
其孰能當此哉且夫德之在人天所與也大莫
大於聖人位以行乎德亦天所與也尊莫尊於
天子兼此二者則爲在上之大人而未之數見
焉時之爲也其唯乾爻乎何也時固有聖不得
位者矣乾之九聖德也而居於五焉亦有君不
修德者矣乾之五君位也而以九居焉統禮樂
征伐之權一日萬幾惟健以行之妙神化之用
於天下操慶賞刑威之柄羣臣百姓惟徊以主
===
之啓風雲之會於域中擬諸其象不猶龍之飛
而在天者乎此何時也大人首出萬物所快覩
也占遇之者仕爲人臣固大義之無所逃也而
有君如此今一見之則立聖人之朝以對揚天
子之命巍乎乘龍御天之功將於是樂觀其成
矣何不利之有哉生爲斯民固大統之不能外
也而有君如此今一見之則近天子之光以幸
爲聖人之氓沛乎雲行雨施之澤將於是親被
其休矣何不利之有哉夫觀象於九五乾之顯
punctuated: 者，天下所觀也。聖人出而人皆仰之，非乾九五，其孰能當此哉？且夫德之在人，天所與也，大莫大於聖人；位以行乎德，亦天所與也，尊莫尊於天子。兼此二者，則爲在上之大人，而未之數見焉，時之爲也。其唯乾爻乎？何也？時固有聖不得位者矣。乾之九，聖德也，而居於五焉；亦有君不修德者矣。乾之五，君位也，而以九居焉。統禮樂征伐之權，一日萬幾，惟健以行之，妙神化之用於天下；操慶賞刑威之柄，羣臣百姓，惟徊以主之，啓風雲之會於域中。擬諸其象，不猶龍之飛而在天者乎？此何時也？大人首出，萬物所快覩也。占遇之者，仕爲人臣，固大義之無所逃也，而有君如此，今一見之，則立聖人之朝，以對揚天子之命，巍乎乘龍御天之功，將於是樂觀其成矣，何不利之有哉？生爲斯民，固大統之不能外也，而有君如此，今一見之，則近天子之光，以幸爲聖人之氓，沛乎雲行雨施之澤，將於是親被其休矣，何不利之有哉？夫觀象於九五，乾之顯
translation_en:
…is the one to whom all under Heaven look. When a sage comes forth, everyone looks up to him. If not the Nine in the Fifth Place of Qian, who could answer to this? Virtue in human beings is bestowed by Heaven, and none is greater in virtue than the sage; the position through which virtue is put into practice is likewise bestowed by Heaven, and none is more exalted in position than the Son of Heaven. Whoever combines these two is the great man above, yet such a man is seldom seen: this depends upon the time. Surely this is what the line of Qian signifies! Why? There have certainly been times when a sage did not obtain the proper position. The nine of Qian represents sagely virtue, and here it occupies the fifth place. There have also been rulers who did not cultivate virtue. The fifth place of Qian is the ruler’s position, and here a nine occupies it. He commands authority over rites, music, punitive expeditions, and warfare; amid the myriad affairs of each day, he acts with vigor, bringing the wondrous efficacy of spiritual transformation to all under Heaven. He holds the power of rewards and honors, punishments and awe; he presides over his ministers and the common people with solicitude [?], bringing about a meeting of wind and cloud within the realm. Compared with the image of this line, is he not like a dragon flying in Heaven? What a time this is! The great man comes forth at the head of all, and all beings delight to behold him.

For one who encounters this line in divination and serves as a minister, the great duty of allegiance is certainly inescapable. With such a ruler, once he gains an audience, he stands in the sage’s court to receive and extol the Son of Heaven’s commands. He will then joyfully witness the accomplishment of that lofty achievement of riding the dragon and governing Heaven. How could this fail to be favorable? For one born among the common people, there is certainly no standing outside the overarching political order. With such a ruler, once he beholds him, he draws near to the radiance of the Son of Heaven, fortunate to be a subject of the sage. He will then personally receive the blessings of that abundant bounty, like clouds moving and rain falling. How could this fail to be favorable? Now, in contemplating the image of the Nine in the Fifth Place, Qian’s manifest…

title: 隆慶元年應天府鄉試錄
text:
龍至隆也而諸爻之比類於龍德者咸統於尊
玩占於九五乾之美利至廣也而他卦之取義
於利見者盡出其下矣周公繫易至此其深慶
矣夫抑周公之時何時也文武之德主治於上
而身任家相之責教化大行以能保子孫臣庶
其利溥哉遡而上之時雍風動平成輯寧之世
聖君代作後先符合孰非所嘉樂而思兼之者
乎然則著之乾爻蓋將以興堯舜之道三王之
功也意深遠矣
===
擬之而後言議之而後動擬議以成其變
化鳴鶴在陰其子和之我有好爵吾與
爾靡之子曰君子居其室出其言善則
千里之外應之況其邇者乎居其室出
其言不善則千里之外違之況其邇者
乎言出乎身加乎民行發乎邇見乎遠
言行君子之樞機樞機之發榮辱之主
也言行君子之所以動天地也可不慎
乎
punctuated:
龍至隆也，而諸爻之比類於龍德者咸統於尊。玩占於九五，乾之美利至廣也，而他卦之取義於利見者盡出其下矣。周公繫易至此，其深慶矣夫！抑周公之時何時也？文武之德主治於上，而身任家相之責，教化大行，以能保子孫臣庶，其利溥哉！遡而上之，時雍風動、平成輯寧之世，聖君代作，後先符合，孰非所嘉樂而思兼之者乎？然則著之乾爻，蓋將以興堯舜之道、三王之功也，意深遠矣。

擬之而後言，議之而後動，擬議以成其變化。「鳴鶴在陰，其子和之。我有好爵，吾與爾靡之。」子曰：「君子居其室，出其言善，則千里之外應之，況其邇者乎？居其室，出其言不善，則千里之外違之，況其邇者乎？言出乎身，加乎民；行發乎邇，見乎遠。言行，君子之樞機；樞機之發，榮辱之主也。言行，君子之所以動天地也，可不慎乎？」
translation_en:
…the dragon reaches the utmost eminence, and all the other lines that draw analogies with the dragon’s virtue are united under this honored position. Contemplating the prognostication for the nine in the fifth place, one sees that the excellent benefits of Qian extend most broadly; all other hexagrams that derive their meaning from the phrase “it is beneficial to see” stand beneath it. When the Duke of Zhou appended his words to the Changes at this point, how profoundly he must have rejoiced! Yet what sort of age was the Duke of Zhou’s? The virtue of Kings Wen and Wu presided over government above, while he himself bore responsibility as minister of the royal house. Moral instruction spread widely, securing the welfare of descendants, ministers, and common people. How universal its benefits! Looking further back to ages of harmonious concord and transforming influence, when the land was brought to order and all enjoyed peace, sage rulers arose in succession, those who came later according with those before them. Which of these achievements would he not have admired and delighted in, wishing to unite them all? Thus, in setting these words down in the lines of Qian, he surely intended to revive the Way of Yao and Shun and the achievements of the Three Kings. His meaning was profound and far-reaching indeed.

“One models one’s words before speaking and deliberates before acting; through such modeling and deliberation one brings transformations to completion. ‘A calling crane is in the shade; its young answers it. I have a fine cup of wine; I will share it with you.’ The Master said: ‘The gentleman dwells in his chamber. If the words he speaks are good, people a thousand li away respond to him—how much more those nearby! If, while dwelling in his chamber, the words he speaks are not good, people a thousand li away oppose him—how much more those nearby! Words issue from oneself and affect the people; actions begin close at hand and become apparent far away. Words and actions are the gentleman’s door pivot and crossbow trigger. Their operation determines honor or disgrace. Through words and actions the gentleman moves Heaven and Earth. Can he fail to be careful?’”

title: 隆慶元年應天府鄉試錄
text:
胡宥
同考試官教諭楊　批〔長題詞能約意且整然有法易義之最佳者宜錄之以式多士〕
同考試官推官沈　批〔善收拾善提掇而語意峻潔條理精密足占造養〕
考試官左中允孫　批〔簡而有法〕
考試官左諭德王　批〔是善作長題者〕
君子之言動學易即乎爻而當知所謹矣夫易
之理在人而言動其著也明於乎爻之義可不
===
謹與且聖人作易本稽實以待虛君子用易在
隨事而通感故自交卦生爻之後而寓辭占象
變之中有言焉言可爲則也必擬而求之以資
其所發言者有動焉動可與謀也必議而求之
以效其所順動者非易之言不敢言即夫變易
告人之旨而善通之隨宜妙應語言無非教矣
非易之動不敢動即夫變通趨時之權而善用
之順事推行踐履皆是易矣擬議維何中孚九
二曰鳴鶴在陰其子和之我有好爵吾與爾靡
punctuated:
胡宥

同考試官教諭楊，批〔長題詞能約意且整然有法易義之最佳者宜錄之以式多士〕。
同考試官推官沈，批〔善收拾善提掇而語意峻潔條理精密足占造養〕。
考試官左中允孫，批〔簡而有法〕。
考試官左諭德王，批〔是善作長題者〕。

君子之言動，學易即乎爻而當知所謹矣。夫易之理在人，而言動其著也。明於乎爻之義，可不謹與？且聖人作易，本稽實以待虛；君子用易，在隨事而通感。故自交卦生爻之後，而寓辭占象變之中，有言焉，言可爲則也，必擬而求之，以資其所發言者；有動焉，動可與謀也，必議而求之，以效其所順動者。非易之言不敢言，即夫變易告人之旨而善通之，隨宜妙應，語言無非教矣；非易之動不敢動，即夫變通趨時之權而善用之，順事推行，踐履皆是易矣。擬議維何？中孚九二曰：「鳴鶴在陰，其子和之。我有好爵，吾與爾靡
translation_en:
Hu You 胡宥

Associate Examiner Yang, Instructor, comments: “For a long topic, the wording is concise and the ideas orderly and methodical. This is among the finest essays on the meaning of the Changes and should be recorded as a model for the candidates.”
Associate Examiner Shen, Prefectural Judge, comments: “Skillful in drawing things together and bringing out the essentials, with incisive, clean expression and precise organization: ample evidence of his attainment and cultivation.”
Examiner Sun, Left Companion to the Heir Apparent, comments: “Concise and methodical.”
Examiner Wang, Left Admonisher, comments: “Here is someone skilled at writing on a long topic.”

As for the gentleman’s words and actions, by studying the Book of Changes and attending to its lines, he should come to know where caution is required. The principles of the Changes reside in human beings, and words and actions are their visible manifestations. Understanding the meaning of its lines [?], can one fail to be cautious? Moreover, when the sages composed the Changes, they examined actual circumstances to anticipate what had yet to take shape; when the gentleman uses the Changes, he responds to particular affairs and achieves sympathetic communication. Thus, once the hexagrams interact and generate lines, within their statements, prognostications, images, and transformations there are words that can serve as standards. He must compare and seek their meaning to inform the words he utters. There are also movements that can aid deliberation. He must discuss and seek their meaning to guide the actions he appropriately undertakes. He dares utter no words that do not accord with the Changes: taking up and thoroughly comprehending the purport by which changing configurations instruct people, he responds aptly to circumstances, so that all his words offer instruction. He dares undertake no action that does not accord with the Changes: taking up and skillfully employing the discretionary judgment that adapts to change and accords with the times, he proceeds as affairs require, so that all his conduct embodies the Changes. What does such comparison and deliberation involve? The nine in the second place of Zhongfu, Inner Sincerity, says: “A calling crane is in the shade; its young answers it. I have a fine goblet of wine; with you I will share …

title: 隆慶元年應天府鄉試錄
text:
之此其義何取於聲應爾我間也而因可識吉
動感通之大矣君子居室至邇也出一言而期
之應不可若是其幾千里之外至遠也從其善
而莫之違又復何限於近其不善者異是矣夫
言非外出也自身以加民行猶之言也由邇以
及遠故善否纔一念之微如樞斯闢如機斯張
則不在初而從違決千里之外從之則榮違之
則辱惟其所召豈人力也哉天聽自我民聽一
言善而天地昭格焉不善不可言也天視自我
===
民視一動善而天地鑒歆焉不善不可行也夫
民心至神而天道不遠如此君子可不慎所感
之首哉大傳首舉爲擬議法他若語默出處皆
言動也可例推矣雖然謂擬議者必占之易乎
變化云爲易在吾心願此感通之義聖人於中
乎發之中之爲言心也乎誠也天地之道一誠
盡之況於人乎苟爲不誠而徒期應於言動間
日予善矣而顧予違也不占而已矣
書
punctuated:
之。此其義何取於聲應爾我間也？而因可識吉動感通之大矣。君子居室，至邇也；出一言而期之應，不可若是其幾。千里之外，至遠也；從其善而莫之違，又復何限於近？其不善者異是矣。夫言非外出也，自身以加民；行猶之言也，由邇以及遠。故善否纔一念之微，如樞斯闢，如機斯張，則不在初而從違決千里之外。從之則榮，違之則辱，惟其所召，豈人力也哉？天聽自我民聽，一言善而天地昭格焉，不善不可言也；天視自我民視，一動善而天地鑒歆焉，不善不可行也。夫民心至神，而天道不遠如此，君子可不慎所感之首哉？大傳首舉爲擬議法，他若語默出處，皆言動也，可例推矣。雖然，謂擬議者必占之易乎？變化云爲，易在吾心。願此感通之義，聖人於中乎發之。中之爲言，心也乎？誠也。天地之道，一誠盡之，況於人乎？苟爲不誠，而徒期應於言動間，日予善矣，而顧予違也，不占而已矣。

書
translation_en:
…share it with you. Why does this passage draw its meaning from the answering of one voice by another, between you and me? Through this one can recognize the great power of auspicious action to evoke responses and establish communion [?]. A gentleman dwelling in his chamber is in the nearest of places; yet, when he utters a word and anticipates its response, that response cannot be reckoned so narrowly [?]. A thousand li away is a very distant place; yet if people follow his goodness and none oppose it, why should its reach be confined to those nearby? With what is not good, the outcome is different.

Words do not come from outside: they proceed from oneself and extend to the people. Conduct is like speech: it proceeds from the near and reaches the distant. Thus goodness or its opposite lies initially in the subtle stirring of a single thought. Like a pivot opening a door or a trigger releasing a bow, its effect does not remain at its origin: whether people follow or oppose it is determined a thousand li away. Their following brings honor; their opposition brings disgrace. Each is simply what one has called forth. Could human force bring this about? “Heaven hears through the hearing of our people”: when a single utterance is good, Heaven and Earth manifestly respond to it; what is not good must therefore not be spoken. “Heaven sees through the sight of our people”: when a single action is good, Heaven and Earth behold and welcome it; what is not good must therefore not be done.

The people's hearts are supremely numinous, and the Way of Heaven is thus never far away. Can the gentleman fail to take care over the first impulse that evokes a response? The Great Commentary first adduces this as a rule for deliberation. Other matters, such as speaking or remaining silent, entering service or withdrawing, all belong to speech and action, and may be inferred by analogy. Nevertheless, does deliberation necessarily mean consulting the Changes through divination? In transformations, speech, and action, the Changes is within my own heart. As for this principle of evoking responses and establishing communion [?], the sage brings it forth from within. Does “within” mean the heart? It means sincerity. The Way of Heaven and Earth is comprehended entirely in sincerity alone; how much more is this true of human beings! If one is insincere and merely expects a response to one's words and deeds, daily declaring, “I am good,” while people instead oppose one [?], there is simply no need to divine.

姚純臣

===
聖君推言克艱之效皆致治之全功也夫俱人
致賢而天下舉安其於治效大矣所以致此者
豈易能哉此帝舜感禹謨而推廣之也意曰君
臣者治化之原也然患不能克艱耳誠盡其道
焉則其效豈小補哉夫治以求言為急常患其
伏而未盡達也今則眾思畢集而獻納有嘉
謨嘉猷之入告非直在朝者然也風聲所樹人
懷自獻之誠知無不言言無不盡四海之內皆
將輕千里而告之善矣寧復以言為諱哉治以
punctuated:
嘉言罔攸伏，野無遺賢，萬邦咸寧。
姚純臣
同考試官教諭蔣　批〔見理明透，措辭醇雅。〕〔盛世致治之隆，宛然在目，殆精於經學者耶？取之〕〔以式多士。〕

聖君推言克艱之效，皆致治之全功也。夫俱人致賢而天下舉安，其於治效大矣。所以致此者，豈易能哉？此帝舜感禹謨而推廣之也。意曰：君臣者，治化之原也，然患不能克艱耳。誠盡其道焉，則其效豈小補哉？夫治以求言為急，常患其伏而未盡達也。今則眾思畢集，而獻納有嘉謨嘉猷之入告，非直在朝者然也。風聲所樹，人懷自獻之誠，知無不言，言無不盡。四海之內，皆將輕千里而告之善矣，寧復以言為諱哉？治以
translation_en:
“No good counsel remains concealed; no worthy man is left overlooked in the countryside; all the myriad states are at peace.”
Yao Chunchen
Associate Examiner Jiang, an Instructor, comments: “His understanding of principle is clear and penetrating, and his phrasing refined and elegant. The height of good government in a flourishing age appears vividly before our eyes. Surely he is deeply versed in classical learning? Select this essay as a model for the candidates.”
Associate Examiner Yang, a Department Magistrate, comments: “The topic elaborates upon the magnitude of the results, thereby revealing precisely where the difficulties have been overcome. This essay is uniquely able to elucidate this point, and its sentences are also lucid and apt. It merits inclusion.”
Examiner Sun, Left Companion to the Heir Apparent, comments: “He skillfully portrays the atmosphere of flourishing government.”
Examiner Wang, Left Admonisher to the Heir Apparent, comments: “His exposition of principle is clear and lucid. Select it.”

The sage ruler elaborates upon the effects of overcoming difficulties: all constitute the complete achievement of good government. When people are brought together and worthy men attracted [?], and the whole world enjoys peace, the results for government are great indeed. Could bringing this about be easy? Here Emperor Shun, moved by Yu’s counsels, expands upon them. His meaning is this: ruler and ministers are the source of orderly government and moral transformation; the concern is simply that they may fail to overcome the difficulties. If they truly fulfill their proper way, how could the results amount to merely a minor contribution?
In governing, seeking counsel is an urgent priority. The constant concern is that counsel may remain concealed and fail to reach the ruler in its entirety. Now, however, everyone’s thoughts are gathered together, and worthy plans and sound counsels are submitted as advice. Nor is this confined to those at court. Wherever the influence of exemplary rule reaches, people sincerely wish to offer what they have. They withhold nothing they know and express fully whatever they say. Throughout the land within the Four Seas, all will think little of traveling a thousand li to offer good counsel. How could speaking out still be regarded as taboo? In governing, one takes …

title: 隆慶元年應天府鄉試錄
text:
用賢爲務常患其遺而未盡舉也今則衆正彙
征而登庸有地三德六德之咸事非直在位者
然也表極所端人懷嚮用之志見無不舉舉無
不先天下之士皆悅而願立于其朝矣寧復以
隱爲高哉治以安民爲功常患萬邦之未盡寧
也今則明良道合而治化覃敷登黎百姓之樂
安非直一方爲然也太平無虞人蒙至治之澤
咸若于政咸敏于德萬邦之民無一夫不獲其
所矣寧復其咨于下哉夫言罔伏則一總章之
===
日也賢罔遺則一明揚之始也萬邦寧則一時
雍之盛也效之所臻固不止於政乂民化而所
以保文命之敷者益無終窮矣君臣相與之際
可不戒哉抑考有虞之治克艱之效皆舜之能
事也然且不以自居至皐陶陳謨雖帝堯猶謂
其難焉蓋不以治爲已足者君之克艱也不以
君之治爲已足者臣之克艱也惟其心之益虛
此治之所以益盛歟彼訑訑之聲拒人千里而
倡豐亨豫大之說以自多者無惑乎治之不古
punctuated: 用賢爲務，常患其遺而未盡舉也。今則衆正彙征，而登庸有地，三德六德之咸事，非直在位者然也。表極所端，人懷嚮用之志，見無不舉，舉無不先，天下之士皆悅而願立于其朝矣，寧復以隱爲高哉？治以安民爲功，常患萬邦之未盡寧也。今則明良道合，而治化覃敷，登黎百姓之樂安，非直一方爲然也。太平無虞，人蒙至治之澤，咸若于政，咸敏于德，萬邦之民無一夫不獲其所矣，寧復其咨于下哉？夫言罔伏，則一總章之日也；賢罔遺，則一明揚之始也；萬邦寧，則一時雍之盛也。效之所臻，固不止於政乂民化，而所以保文命之敷者，益無終窮矣。君臣相與之際，可不戒哉？抑考有虞之治，克艱之效，皆舜之能事也。然且不以自居，至皐陶陳謨，雖帝堯猶謂其難焉。蓋不以治爲已足者，君之克艱也；不以君之治爲已足者，臣之克艱也。惟其心之益虛，此治之所以益盛歟？彼訑訑之聲，拒人千里，而倡豐亨豫大之說以自多者，無惑乎治之不古
translation_en:
…employing worthy men is an essential task, and the constant concern is that some may be overlooked and not all brought forward. Now, however, upright men advance together and find places in office. Those possessing three virtues or six virtues all serve, and this is not confined to those already holding positions. With the exemplary standard correctly established, people aspire to be employed. No worthy man encountered goes unrecommended, and each recommendation is advanced with urgency. The scholars of the realm all rejoice and wish to stand at his court. How could they still regard withdrawal from service as lofty?

Government takes bringing peace to the people as its achievement, and the constant concern is that the myriad states may not all be at peace. Now, however, an enlightened ruler and worthy ministers are united in the Way, and good government and moral transformation spread far and wide. The common people [?] enjoy peace, and this is not confined to one region. In an age of great peace, free from anxiety, people receive the blessings of consummate government. All comply with its administration; all diligently pursue virtue. Among the people of the myriad states, not one fails to find his proper place. How could there still be lamentation among those below?

When no counsel remains concealed, it is another day of the Hall of Comprehensive Illumination [?]; when no worthy man is overlooked, it is a fresh beginning of discerning and promoting the worthy; when the myriad states are at peace, it is another flourishing age of universal harmony. The effects attained certainly extend beyond orderly administration and the moral transformation of the people: the means of ensuring the continued spread of civilizing instruction become ever more inexhaustible. Can ruler and ministers fail to be vigilant in their dealings with one another?

Moreover, if we examine the government of Youyu, the achievements resulting from taking its difficulties seriously were all accomplishments of Shun. Yet he did not claim them for himself. When Gao Yao presented his counsels, even Emperor Yao was said to have found the task difficult. For a ruler, taking its difficulties seriously means never considering his government already sufficient; for a minister, it means never considering his ruler’s government already sufficient. Is it not precisely because their minds become ever more receptive that their government flourishes ever more greatly? As for those whose complacent voices repel others a thousand li away, and who vaunt themselves by proclaiming abundance, success, ease, and grandeur, it is no wonder that their government fails to match antiquity…

title: 隆慶元年應天府鄉試錄
text:
天也
我聞曰昔在殷王中宗嚴恭寅畏天命自
度治民祗懼不敢荒寧肆中宗之享國
七十有五年
吴遷聰

公告君之大旨此作得之
===

愛之意
商王敬德通于天人宜獲福之求也夫敬者人
君所以奉天而治由此出也商王享國長求其
敬德不衰之徵與周公欲成王之無逸而以有
商繼體之君告之曰人君之有國也天命之所
歸人心之所戴也謹之罔不在初而其保天命
punctuated:
天也。

我聞曰：「昔在殷王中宗，嚴恭寅畏，天命自度，治民祗懼，不敢荒寧，肆中宗之享國七十有五年。」

吴遷聰
