商王敬德通于天人，宜獲福之求也。夫敬者，人君所以奉天，而治由此出也。商王享國長，求其敬德不衰之徵與？周公欲成王之無逸，而以有商繼體之君告之曰：「人君之有國也，天命之所歸，人心之所戴也。謹之罔不在初，而其保天命
translation_en:
…Heaven [?].

“I have heard it said: ‘Formerly, Zhongzong, king of Yin, was solemn and respectful, reverent and fearful. He measured himself against Heaven’s mandate and governed the people with reverent apprehension, never daring to indulge in idle ease. Thus Zhongzong held the throne for seventy-five years.’”

Wu Qiancong

Associate Examiner Jiang, an Instructor, comments: “The reasoning is clear and the language fluent; he excels at exposition. His elucidation of the meaning of ‘reverence’ is exceptionally precise and penetrating. Such learning in the Classics is indeed rare. This essay should rank first in this examining section.”

Associate Examiner Yang, a Department Magistrate, comments: “Through reverence one naturally becomes capable of avoiding idle ease: this is the principal message of the Duke of Zhou’s admonition to his ruler. This composition grasps it.”

Examiner Sun, Left Companion to the Heir Apparent, comments: “The exposition of reverence as the means of avoiding idle ease is clear.”

Examiner Wang, Left Adviser to the Heir Apparent, comments: “The explanation of ‘reverence’ is thorough and penetrating, deeply grasping the Duke of Zhou’s loyal affection.”

The Shang king’s reverent virtue reached both Heaven and humankind; fittingly, he received enduring blessings [?]. Reverence is the means by which a ruler serves Heaven, and good government proceeds from it. The Shang king held the throne for a long time: may we seek in this evidence that his reverent virtue never declined? The Duke of Zhou wished King Cheng to avoid idle ease, and therefore instructed him by citing a king who had succeeded to the Shang throne, saying: “When a ruler possesses a state, it is because Heaven’s mandate has come to rest upon him and the people’s hearts uphold him. None fails to exercise care at the beginning; yet, as for preserving Heaven’s mandate…

title: 隆慶元年應天府鄉試錄
text:
繫人心也約之惟存乎敬我所謂無逸者於商
王中宗有聞矣外貌無斯須之不敬何其嚴也
而常守之以謙抑又甚恭焉中心無斯須之不
敬何其寅也而常謹之以戒懼又甚畏焉是蓋
不以天位之舍爲要惟以天命之理自度內不
逸於心儼上帝之臨也外不逸於身凜在帝
之左右也誠有命以爲防而事天守身毋不敬
焉者矣既以天之命我者自持不以我之治人
者可忽懼民艱未畛何敢以怠荒乖之懼民務
===
未修何敢以安寧處之誠有理以貞度而修已
治人毋不敬焉者矣中宗克盡無逸之實如此
敬無間於天人固弗謹此而失彼敬不殊於久
近要非勤始而怠終故考其時則商道中興也
坐享太平已底治功之盛而紀其年則七十有
五也多歷年所益引國祚之長謂非天命來保
人心未繫者乎此可見敬也者君德所以成始
而成終也不敬則荒寧荒寧則逸其亦異乎我
所聞矣抑考益戒舜曰罔遊于逸而舜授禹曰
punctuated: 繫人心也，約之惟存乎敬。我所謂無逸者，於商王中宗有聞矣。外貌無斯須之不敬，何其嚴也！而常守之以謙抑，又甚恭焉。中心無斯須之不敬，何其寅也！而常謹之以戒懼，又甚畏焉。是蓋不以天位之舍爲要，惟以天命之理自度。內不逸於心，儼上帝之臨也；外不逸於身，凜在帝之左右也。誠有命以爲防，而事天守身，毋不敬焉者矣。既以天之命我者自持，不以我之治人者可忽。懼民艱未畛，何敢以怠荒乖之？懼民務未修，何敢以安寧處之？誠有理以貞度，而修已治人，毋不敬焉者矣。中宗克盡無逸之實如此，敬無間於天人，固弗謹此而失彼；敬不殊於久近，要非勤始而怠終。故考其時，則商道中興也，坐享太平，已底治功之盛；而紀其年，則七十有五也，多歷年所，益引國祚之長。謂非天命來保、人心未繫者乎？此可見敬也者，君德所以成始而成終也。不敬則荒寧，荒寧則逸，其亦異乎我所聞矣。」抑考益戒舜曰：「罔遊于逸。」而舜授禹曰：
translation_en: …and securing the people’s allegiance, in essence, depend solely upon reverence. Of what I call freedom from ease, I have heard an example in Zhongzong, king of Shang. In his outward bearing, he was never without reverence for even a moment: how solemn he was! Yet he always maintained this through humility and restraint, and was exceedingly deferential. Within his heart, he was never without reverence for even a moment: how earnest he was! Yet he always guarded this through vigilance and apprehension, and was exceedingly fearful. This was because he did not regard occupancy of Heaven’s throne [?] as the essential thing, but measured himself solely by the principles of Heaven’s mandate. Inwardly, he allowed no ease in his heart, solemnly aware that the Lord on High looked down upon him; outwardly, he allowed no ease in his person, trembling as though standing beside the Lord. Truly, he took the mandate as a safeguard and was reverent in everything, serving Heaven and guarding his own conduct. Having upheld himself by what Heaven had commanded of him, he did not suppose that his governance of others could be neglected. Fearing that the people’s hardships were not yet relieved [?], how could he dare, through indolence and neglect, to fail them? Fearing that the people’s affairs were not yet put in order, how could he dare to rest at ease? Truly, he used principle to make his standards correct, and was reverent in everything, cultivating himself and governing others. Such was Zhongzong’s full realization of freedom from ease. His reverence admitted no division between Heaven and humankind: assuredly, he did not attend carefully to one while neglecting the other. His reverence did not differ over long or short periods: certainly, he was not diligent at the beginning and negligent at the end. Thus, when we examine his age, we find that the way of Shang flourished anew: he enjoyed great peace and had already attained the height of achievement in government. When we count the years of his reign, they number seventy-five: through those many years, he further prolonged the dynasty’s allotted span. Could one say that Heaven’s mandate did not come to protect him, and that the people’s hearts were not bound to him [?]? From this we can see that reverence is what enables a ruler’s virtue to accomplish both its beginning and its completion. Without reverence comes indulgence in idle ease; from indulgence in idle ease comes indolence. That would indeed be different from what I have heard.” Furthermore, examining the past, we find that Yi admonished Shun, saying, “Do not wander into ease.” And when Shun transmitted rule to Yu, he said: …

title: 隆慶元年應天府鄉試錄
text:
敬修其可願敬與逸對故逸之不可以有也周
公勉成王至矣然敬之實必於治人徵之修已
而百姓安篤恭而天下平二帝三王胥此道也
不然侮慢自賢速戾多矣而狎侮小人其於天
命去留何如耶爲人上者柰何不敬
詩
天生烝民有物有則民之秉彛好是懿德
天監有周昭假于下保茲天子生仲山
甫
唐鶴徵
同考試官教授梁　批〔詞溫粹而意雋永宜錄以式〕
同考試官教授趙　批〔天生賢以佐一代中興之盛此作發之殆盡佳士也錄之〕
同考試官知州陳　批〔發出周家中興氣象且詞旨雋永可嘉〕
考試官左中允孫　批〔溫雅可誦〕
考試官左諭德王　批〔能發天生賢之意〕
punctuated:
「敬修其可願。」敬與逸對，故逸之不可以有也，周公勉成王至矣。然敬之實，必於治人徵之。修已而百姓安，篤恭而天下平，二帝三王胥此道也。不然，侮慢自賢，速戾多矣；而狎侮小人，其於天命去留何如耶？爲人上者，柰何不敬？
詩
天生烝民，有物有則。民之秉彛，好是懿德。天監有周，昭假于下。保茲天子，生仲山甫。
唐鶴徵
同考試官教授梁，批〔詞溫粹而意雋永，宜錄以式。〕
同考試官教授趙，批〔天生賢以佐一代中興之盛，此作發之殆盡。佳士也，錄之。〕
同考試官知州陳，批〔發出周家中興氣象，且詞旨雋永，可嘉。〕
考試官左中允孫，批〔溫雅可誦。〕
考試官左諭德王，批〔能發天生賢之意。〕
translation_en:
…“Reverently cultivate what is worthy of desire.” Reverence stands opposed to ease; thus the Duke of Zhou was most earnest in urging King Cheng to shun ease. Yet the substance of reverence must be demonstrated in governing the people. Cultivate oneself, and the common people are at peace; be steadfastly reverent, and all under Heaven is tranquil. The Two Emperors and Three Kings all followed this Way. Otherwise, arrogance, disdain, and conceit bring many calamities upon oneself. If a ruler treats the common people with contemptuous familiarity, what will become of Heaven’s Mandate—will it remain or depart? How can those who stand above others fail to be reverent?
Book of Odes
Heaven gives birth to the multitude of people; for every thing there is a rule. The people hold fast to their constant nature and love this admirable virtue. Heaven watches over Zhou; its radiance reaches down below. To protect this Son of Heaven, it gave birth to Zhong Shanfu.
Tang Hezheng
Associate Examiner Liang, Professor, comments: “The language is gentle and refined, and the meaning has lasting savor. It should be selected as a model.”
Associate Examiner Zhao, Professor, comments: “Heaven brings forth worthy men to assist the flourishing restoration of a dynasty. This composition develops that idea almost exhaustively. A fine scholar: select his work.”
Associate Examiner Chen, Prefect, comments: “It brings out the spirit of the Zhou dynasty’s restoration, and its language and meaning have lasting savor. Commendable.”
Examiner Sun, Left Companion to the Heir Apparent, comments: “Gentle and elegant, well worth reciting.”
Examiner Wang, Left Admonisher to the Heir Apparent, comments: “It succeeds in bringing out the idea that Heaven gives birth to worthy men.”

title: 隆慶元年應天府鄉試錄
text:
詩人原天命之善而因表其生賢之意焉蓋天
命之性本皆善也况山甫之生出於天之佑命
者則豈猶夫人而已哉昔王命仲山甫築城于
齊尹吉甫作詩以送之蓋謂賢才之生不偶然
也吾嘗求端於天而知山甫之異于人矣何則
天之生斯民也氣以成形而理亦賦焉物則之
良徵諸庶民有同秉者是以民之秉此彛也情
之所感而善斯形焉懿德之好達之天下有同
然者夫知天下無不善之情則知天下無不善
===
之性此所以論於凡民者然耳而况天之照臨
於上有貞觀焉不可得而誣也謂我周之感格
於下有明德焉乃其所簡在也故天心仁愛吾
君以爲中興之令主則所以扶持而安全者必
將使其得賢以自輔也于是間氣鍾而山甫生
焉眷之篤斯畀之隆殆與文之四友而媲德矣
物則之良夫豈常人之可及哉帝命寵綏我后
以爲昭代之賢王則所以撥亂而興衰者必不
使其有君而無臣也于是良弼賚而山甫出焉
punctuated:
詩人原天命之善，而因表其生賢之意焉。蓋天命之性本皆善也，况山甫之生出於天之佑命者，則豈猶夫人而已哉！昔王命仲山甫築城于齊，尹吉甫作詩以送之，蓋謂賢才之生不偶然也。吾嘗求端於天，而知山甫之異于人矣。何則？天之生斯民也，氣以成形，而理亦賦焉。物則之良，徵諸庶民，有同秉者。是以民之秉此彛也，情之所感，而善斯形焉。懿德之好，達之天下，有同然者。夫知天下無不善之情，則知天下無不善之性，此所以論於凡民者然耳。

而况天之照臨於上，有貞觀焉，不可得而誣也。謂我周之感格於下，有明德焉，乃其所簡在也。故天心仁愛吾君，以爲中興之令主，則所以扶持而安全者，必將使其得賢以自輔也。于是間氣鍾而山甫生焉。眷之篤，斯畀之隆，殆與文之四友而媲德矣。物則之良，夫豈常人之可及哉！帝命寵綏我后，以爲昭代之賢王，則所以撥亂而興衰者，必不使其有君而無臣也。于是良弼賚而山甫出焉。
translation_en:
The poet traces goodness to Heaven’s mandate and thereby reveals Heaven’s intention in bringing forth worthy men. The nature conferred by Heaven is fundamentally good in all people. How much more, then, must Shanfu, whose birth arose from Heaven’s protective mandate, have been more than an ordinary man! Formerly, the king commanded Zhong Shanfu to build a city wall in Qi, and Yin Jifu composed a poem to send him on his way, holding that the birth of a worthy man of talent was no chance occurrence. I have sought its origin in Heaven and thus come to understand how Shanfu differed from other men. Why is this? When Heaven brings forth the people, vital force gives them bodily form, while principle is also bestowed upon them. The goodness of the norms inherent in things may be verified among the common people: all alike possess it. Thus, because the people hold these constant norms, goodness manifests itself when their feelings are stirred. A love of admirable virtue is shared throughout the world. To know that the feelings of all under Heaven are good is to know that their natures are good. Yet this is merely what may be said of ordinary people.

How much more, then, must be said of Heaven, which shines down from above! Its constant scrutiny cannot be deceived. Our Zhou, moving Heaven from below, possesses luminous virtue and is therefore the object of its choice. Thus Heaven, in its benevolence, loves our ruler and makes him an excellent lord of restoration. To sustain and safeguard him, it must ensure that he obtains worthy men to assist him. Thus an exceptional concentration of vital force gathered, and Shanfu was born. So profound was Heaven’s care that its gift was correspondingly great: in virtue he could well rival King Wen’s four companions. How could ordinary men attain such goodness in the norms inherent in things! The mandate of the Lord on High favors and brings peace to our sovereign, making him a worthy king of an illustrious age. In providing the means to quell disorder and revive what has declined, Heaven surely would not allow there to be a ruler without a minister. Thus an excellent assistant was bestowed, and Shanfu came forth.…

title: 隆慶元年應天府鄉試錄
text:
任之重斯賦之全殆與興武之九人而繼美矣懿
德之備夫豈凡民之可班哉是則觀天之生民
可以見性善之同焉觀天之生賢可以見周祜
之篤焉吉甫爲詩其知道乎大抵有一代之君
必有一代之臣斯二者交相成也宣王側身修
行上格乎天故天錫賢才以爲之佐山甫不恃
其在天者而式古訓力威儀以益懋於學故能
明哲保身忠勤事上以成佐命之功周道之中
興其在是歟
===
載見辟王曰求厥章龍旂陽陽和鈴央央
鞗革有鶬休有烈光率見昭考以孝以
享以介眉壽永言保之思皇多祜烈文
辟公綏以多福俾緝熙于純嘏
施近臣
同考試官教授梁　批　氣格雄健詞理精到
擅場之作
同考試官教授趙　批　會發周室君臣忠孝
之德且詞意溫厚深得頌體者
punctuated:
任之重，斯賦之全，殆與興武之九人而繼美矣。懿德之備，夫豈凡民之可班哉？是則觀天之生民，可以見性善之同焉；觀天之生賢，可以見周祜之篤焉。吉甫爲詩，其知道乎！大抵有一代之君，必有一代之臣，斯二者交相成也。宣王側身修行，上格乎天，故天錫賢才以爲之佐。山甫不恃其在天者，而式古訓，力威儀，以益懋於學，故能明哲保身，忠勤事上，以成佐命之功。周道之中興，其在是歟？

載見辟王，曰求厥章。龍旂陽陽，和鈴央央。鞗革有鶬，休有烈光。率見昭考，以孝以享，以介眉壽。永言保之，思皇多祜。烈文辟公，綏以多福，俾緝熙于純嘏。

施近臣

同考試官教授梁批：氣格雄健，詞理精到，擅場之作。

同考試官教授趙批：會發周室君臣忠孝之德，且詞意溫厚，深得頌體者。
translation_en:
…The weight of the charge entrusted to him called for the completeness of his endowment; he could surely carry forward the excellence of the nine men who helped King Wu rise. In the fullness of his admirable virtue, how could ordinary people rank alongside him? Thus, by observing Heaven’s creation of the people, we can perceive the goodness of nature that all share; by observing Heaven’s creation of worthy men, we can perceive the abundance of its blessings upon Zhou. Jifu, in composing his poem, surely understood the Way! In general, wherever there is a ruler worthy of his age, there must also be ministers worthy of that age: the two bring one another to fulfillment. King Xuan humbled himself and cultivated his conduct, thereby reaching Heaven above; Heaven therefore bestowed worthy men to assist him. Shanfu did not rely solely upon what Heaven had endowed him with, but took ancient teachings as his model and worked diligently at dignified bearing, applying himself ever more earnestly to learning. Thus he could preserve himself through clear understanding and wisdom, serve his sovereign loyally and diligently, and accomplish the work of assisting the royal mandate. Was this not the source of the restoration of Zhou’s Way?

They come to appear before their sovereign king,
Seeking his rules and ordinances.
Dragon banners flutter brightly;
Chariot bells ring in harmony.
Bridle straps bear gleaming metal fittings;
Their splendor shines brilliantly.
He leads them to appear before his illustrious deceased father,
To offer filial service and sacrifice,
And thereby obtain long life.
May he preserve this forever—
Ah, abundant and magnificent blessings!
Glorious and accomplished lords,
Bring him repose through many blessings,
And enable him to continue in brightness amid the fullness of good fortune.

Shi Jinchen.

Associate Examiner Liang, Instructor, comments: “Vigorous in spirit and style, precise and accomplished in expression and reasoning: a work that surpasses the field.”

Associate Examiner Zhao, Instructor, comments: “It comprehensively brings out the virtues of loyalty and filial piety among the ruler and ministers of the house of Zhou. Its language and sentiments are also gentle and generous, profoundly capturing the form of the hymn.”

title: 隆慶元年應天府鄉試錄
text:
同考試官知州陳　批〔詞不費而意自足佳〕
作也
考試官左中允孫　批〔說仁孝意好且以來朝見〕
〔廟作二大比立格正大可録〕
考試官左諭德王　批〔體格純正詩義之優者〕
周王美諸侯來朝以助祭而因歸其錫福之功
焉夫朝而助祭諸侯之常職也王者乃以錫福
之功歸之不可以見仁孝之至乎此諸侯助祭
于武王廟之詩蓋謂先王以觀禮同邦國以祀
===
禮萃人心予今有以得此於諸侯矣方其載見
也以爲天王紀法之宗也人臣紀法之守也於
是稟受乎王章而來朝之儀修焉以龍旂則陽
陽精白之誠昭於物采矣以和鈴則央央以鞗
革則有鶬德音之秩宜於輿衛矣一時見聞之
盛不有以顯邦家之光乎迨其既見也以爲土
地昭考所封也人心昭考所屬也於是率之以
廟見而助祭之禮舉焉以虔對越而克盡其恭
合天下以昭孝矣以薦廣牡而外盡其物合天
punctuated:
同考試官知州陳批〔詞不費而意自足，佳〕作也。
同考試官教授孫批〔說仁孝意好，且以來朝見〕〔廟作二大比，立格正大，可録〕
考試官左諭德王批〔體格純正，詩義之優者〕
周王美諸侯來朝以助祭，而因歸其錫福之功焉。夫朝而助祭，諸侯之常職也。王者乃以錫福之功歸之，不可以見仁孝之至乎？此諸侯助祭于武王廟之詩，蓋謂先王以觀禮同邦國，以祀禮萃人心，予今有以得此於諸侯矣。方其載見也，以爲天王紀法之宗也，人臣紀法之守也，於是稟受乎王章，而來朝之儀修焉。以龍旂則陽陽，精白之誠昭於物采矣；以和鈴則央央，以鞗革則有鶬，德音之秩宜於輿衛矣。一時見聞之盛，不有以顯邦家之光乎？迨其既見也，以爲土地昭考所封也，人心昭考所屬也，於是率之以廟見，而助祭之禮舉焉。以虔對越而克盡其恭，合天下以昭孝矣；以薦廣牡而外盡其物，合天
translation_en:
Associate Examiner Chen, Department Magistrate, comments: 〔The language is economical, yet the meaning is complete: an excellent〕 composition.
Examiner Sun, Left Mentor, comments: 〔The treatment of benevolence and filial piety is good. Moreover, attendance at court and presentation in〕〔the ancestral temple form two major parallel sections. The composition is upright and grand in conception, and merits inclusion.〕
Examiner Wang, Left Admonisher, comments: 〔Pure and correct in form and style: an outstanding interpretation of the Poetry.〕
The king of Zhou praises the feudal lords for coming to court to assist at the sacrifices, and consequently credits them with bringing blessings upon him. Now, attending court and assisting at sacrifices are the ordinary duties of the feudal lords. Yet the king credits them with bringing blessings upon him: does this not reveal the utmost benevolence and filial piety? This is a poem about the feudal lords assisting at sacrifices in the temple of King Wu. Its meaning is approximately this: “The former kings united the states through the observance of ceremonial rites and gathered people’s hearts through sacrificial rites. Now, through the feudal lords, I have attained this.”
When they first appeared in audience, they considered the Son of Heaven the fountainhead of regulations and laws, and ministers their custodians. Thus they respectfully received the royal statutes and duly performed the ceremonies of attendance at court. Their dragon banners were resplendent: their utterly pure sincerity shone through the colors of their ceremonial insignia. Their carriage bells rang harmoniously, and their leather reins bore gleaming ornaments: the ordered expression of their virtue befitted their carriages and escorts. Did not the magnificence of everything seen and heard on that occasion display the glory of the royal house and realm?
Once they had appeared in audience, the king reflected that their lands had been granted by his illustrious deceased father, and that the people’s hearts had been entrusted to them by that father. He therefore led them to present themselves in the ancestral temple, where the rites of assisting at sacrifice were performed. Through reverently attending upon the spirit, they fully expressed their respect, joining all under Heaven in manifesting filial piety. Through presenting large bulls, they furnished the full complement of outward offerings, joining all under Heaven …

title: 隆慶元年應天府鄉試錄
text:
下以爲享矣一時萃渙之誠不有以致皇考之
假乎由是介之眉壽以來其承祀之基申之多
祜以隆其保艾之慶是豈我之能自致哉蓋由
烈文辟公盡感格之誠而綏我以多福之備故
俾予一人其敢忘所自哉夫成王基命宥密昭假
於先王素矣而世廟之鑿循讓而不敢居焉非
其仁孝之獨至乎抑天子有事於宗廟諸侯各
以其職來祭禮也而人心之所屬天命之去留
===
寔繫焉是故周王重之清廟之歌惟顯相多士
之美而此詩及烈文皆歸功於諸侯上下之情
交相忠愛所以培植固結乎此耳後世苑擲與
歌包茅責貢周道衰矣而天命人心猶附屬焉
非文武成康之德未泯歟
春秋
春公觀魚于棠〔隱公〕五年夏公如齊觀社
莊公二十有三年
punctuated:
下以爲享矣。一時萃渙之誠，不有以致皇考之假乎？由是介之眉壽，以來其承祀之基；申之多祜，以隆其保艾之慶。是豈我之能自致哉？蓋由烈文辟公盡感格之誠，而綏我以多福之備，故俾予一人，其敢忘所自哉？夫成王基命宥密，昭假於先王素矣，而世廟之鑿，循讓而不敢居焉，非其仁孝之獨至乎？抑天子有事於宗廟，諸侯各以其職來祭，禮也，而人心之所屬、天命之去留，寔繫焉。是故周王重之，《清廟》之歌惟顯相多士之美，而此詩及《烈文》皆歸功於諸侯。上下之情交相忠愛，所以培植固結乎此耳。後世苑擲與歌，包茅責貢，周道衰矣，而天命人心猶附屬焉，非文武成康之德未泯歟？

春秋

春，公觀魚于棠。〔隱公〕五年。夏，公如齊觀社。莊公二十有三年。
translation_en:
…all under Heaven are united in making the offering. Could the sincerity of this gathering in worship fail to bring the august deceased father’s presence? Thus he grants long life, securing the foundation for continuing the sacrifices, and bestows abundant blessings, magnifying the favor of protection and nurture. Could I possibly have achieved this myself? It is because the illustrious and accomplished lords have exerted their utmost sincerity to move the spirits and bring their presence, thereby securing for me blessings in their fullness. Since they have thus benefited me, the One Man, how could I dare forget their source?

King Cheng established his mandate with generous depth and quiet diligence, and had long approached the former kings in radiant reverence. Yet, regarding the ancestral temple’s construction [?], he deferred modestly and dared not claim the credit. Was this not the utmost expression of his benevolence and filial devotion? Moreover, when the Son of Heaven performs rites in the ancestral temple, the regional lords come to sacrifice, each according to his duties: this is ritual propriety. Yet upon it also depend the allegiance of the people’s hearts and whether Heaven’s Mandate remains or departs. For this reason the kings of Zhou attached great importance to it. The song “The Pure Temple” (Qing miao) celebrates only the excellence of the distinguished assistants and the many officers, while this poem and “Illustrious and Accomplished” (Lie wen) both attribute the achievement to the regional lords. Those above and below reciprocated one another’s loyalty and affection; through this they nurtured and firmly consolidated their bonds.

In later ages, there were “garden, casting away, and song” [?], and demands for tribute of bundled thatching grass. The Way of Zhou had declined, yet Heaven’s Mandate and the people’s hearts still adhered to it. Was this not because the virtue of Kings Wen, Wu, Cheng, and Kang had not yet faded?

Spring and Autumn Annals

“In spring, the duke watched the fishing at Tang.” 〔Duke Yin〕 Fifth year.

“In summer, the duke went to Qi to observe the sacrifice at the altar of the soil.” Twenty-third year of Duke Zhuang.

title: 隆慶元年應天府鄉試錄
text:
同考試官知縣王　批〔簡而文嚴而有體春秋義若此者不多見也〕
考試官左諭德王　批〔文整而徤〕
考試官左中允孫　批〔得謹嚴體〕
内君舉動之非禮法者春秋兩致譏焉夫舉動
人君之大節不以禮法自處不可也隱之觀魚
莊之觀社均爲春秋所譏因以此且夫觀魚于
棠隱以略地行而春秋譏之者何蓋君人之廵
行當必以王事民事爲重也外此則慢政逸遊
===
爾棠之魚非公所當觀也歷年享國未爲能君
今又遠出以觀魚焉不思一人之身表率臣民
者也動不於禮其何以彰之軌物乎于時僖伯
之諫謂納民於亂政者公知其非而不能以自
克也名爲略地而往實則陳魚而觀公於是爲
遂非爲縱欲矣君子曰棠魚之觀易而述職省
耕可也宜特書觀魚以譏之觀社于齊莊以會
祀往而春秋譏之者何蓋君人之會祀當必有
受命受事之辨也紊此則非法輕舉爾齊之社
punctuated:
同考試官知縣王批〔簡而文，嚴而有體，春秋義若此者不多見也。〕
考試官左諭德王批〔文整而徤。〕
考試官左中允孫批〔得謹嚴體。〕
内君舉動之非禮法者，《春秋》兩致譏焉。夫舉動，人君之大節，不以禮法自處，不可也。隱之觀魚，莊之觀社，均爲《春秋》所譏，因以此。且夫觀魚于棠，隱以略地行，而《春秋》譏之者何？蓋君人之廵行，當必以王事民事爲重也。外此則慢政逸遊爾。棠之魚，非公所當觀也。歷年享國，未爲能君，今又遠出以觀魚焉。不思一人之身，表率臣民者也，動不於禮，其何以彰之軌物乎？于時僖伯之諫，謂納民於亂政者，公知其非，而不能以自克也。名爲略地而往，實則陳魚而觀，公於是爲遂非，爲縱欲矣。君子曰：棠魚之觀，易而述職省耕可也。宜特書觀魚以譏之。觀社于齊，莊以會祀往，而《春秋》譏之者何？蓋君人之會祀，當必有受命受事之辨也。紊此則非法輕舉爾。齊之社
translation_en:
Associate Examiner Wang, District Magistrate, comments: 〔Concise yet elegant, rigorous and properly structured. Interpretations of the Spring and Autumn Annals such as this are rarely seen.〕
Examiner Wang, Left Mentor, comments: 〔The composition is orderly and vigorous.〕
Examiner Sun, Left Admonisher, comments: 〔It achieves a scrupulous and rigorous style.〕
The Spring and Autumn Annals twice censures actions by the ruler of its own state that contravene ritual propriety and established norms. A ruler’s actions are a matter of great consequence: he must conduct himself according to ritual propriety and established norms. Duke Yin’s viewing of fish and Duke Zhuang’s viewing of the sacrifice to the soil altar are both censured by the Spring and Autumn Annals for this reason [?]. Now, when Duke Yin went to view fish at Tang, he travelled under the pretext of inspecting the territory. Why, then, does the Spring and Autumn Annals censure him? A ruler’s tours must give priority to royal business and the affairs of the people. Anything beyond these is merely neglect of government and idle pleasure-seeking.
The fish at Tang were not something the duke ought to have gone to see. Though he had ruled the state for years, he had yet to prove himself a capable ruler; now he again travelled far afield to view fish. He failed to reflect that his own person served as an example to his ministers and people. If his actions did not accord with ritual propriety, how could he make manifest the standards of proper conduct? At the time, Xibo remonstrated that this would draw the people into disorderly government. The duke knew that his conduct was wrong, yet could not restrain himself. Nominally he went to inspect the territory; in fact, he had fish displayed for his viewing. Thus the duke persisted in wrongdoing and indulged his desires. The gentleman says: he could properly have replaced his viewing of fish at Tang with a visit to report on his duties to the king and an inspection of farming. It was fitting that the Annals expressly recorded “viewing fish” to censure him.
When Duke Zhuang went to Qi to view the sacrifice to the soil altar, he went to participate in the rites. Why, then, does the Spring and Autumn Annals censure him? A ruler’s participation in sacrifices must observe the distinction between receiving a command and accepting an assigned service. To confuse these is merely to act rashly in violation of established norms. The soil altar of Qi…

title: 隆慶元年應天府鄉試錄
text:
非我所當會也因社觀民已非故業今又輕出
而往觀焉不思一時之爲垂法後來者也舉而
非法其何以著之儀刑乎于時曹劌之諫謂示
後以何觀者公聞其非而不能以不往也以周
公之胄供齊國之末事公於是爲輕舉爲妄
說矣君子曰齊社之觀易而于周受命可也宜
直書如齊觀社以譏之是知一舉動而非禮法
二君之過也謂遊觀細故耳春秋必書後世有
遺譏焉可不慎歟抑論僖伯之忠隱能知之有
===
加禮於其身後而不能用其言於身前可慨也
莊也制命於母乃父讐之忍忘而又請婚姻焉
悖亦甚矣丹楹刻桷御孫指爲大惡而劌以非
法諍若小失然吁隱能知其臣而莊不能知乃
拒諫則等爾然則劌其猶在公子彄之後乎
初稅畝〔宣公十有五年三月作丘甲成公〕
元年春用田賦〔哀公十有二年〕
同考試官知縣王　批　〔格整而義盡經文之〕
夕復乾
punctuated:
非我所當會也。因社觀民，已非故業；今又輕出而往觀焉，不思一時之爲，垂法後來者也。舉而非法，其何以著之儀刑乎？于時曹劌之諫，謂示後以何觀者，公聞其非而不能以不往也。以周公之胄，供齊國之末事，公於是爲輕舉、爲妄說矣。君子曰：「齊社之觀，易而于周受命可也。」宜直書「如齊觀社」以譏之。是知一舉動而非禮法，二君之過也。謂遊觀細故耳，春秋必書，後世有遺譏焉，可不慎歟？抑論僖伯之忠，隱能知之，有加禮於其身後，而不能用其言於身前，可慨也！莊也制命於母，乃父讐之忍忘，而又請婚姻焉，悖亦甚矣！丹楹刻桷，御孫指爲大惡，而劌以非法諍，若小失然。吁！隱能知其臣，而莊不能知，乃拒諫則等爾。然則劌其猶在公子彄之後乎？
初稅畝〔宣公十有五年三月作丘甲成公〕元年春，用田賦〔哀公十有二年〕。
同考試官知縣王批：〔格整而義盡，經文之〕夕復乾
translation_en:
…is not a ceremony we ought to attend. Observing the people on the occasion of the sacrifice to the soil was already outside his established duties; now he recklessly went abroad to watch it, without considering that his actions at that moment would set a standard for posterity. If his conduct departed from proper rules, how could he make it an exemplary model? Cao Gui’s remonstrance at the time asked what spectacle he would thereby present to later generations. The duke heard that his conduct was wrong, yet could not refrain from going. As a descendant of the Duke of Zhou, he attended to a minor affair of the state of Qi: thus the duke acted rashly and indulged in misguided pleasure. The gentleman says: “Instead of watching Qi’s sacrifice to the soil, he could properly have gone to Zhou to receive commands.” It was fitting to record directly, “He went to Qi to watch the sacrifice to the soil,” thereby censuring him. Thus we see that undertaking an action contrary to ritual and proper rules was the fault of both rulers. One might call sightseeing a trifling matter, yet the Spring and Autumn Annals invariably records it, leaving censure for later generations. Could one fail to be cautious? Moreover, considering Xibo’s loyalty, Duke Yin could recognize it and accorded him additional honors after his death, yet could not act upon his words while he lived. This is lamentable! Duke Zhuang took his directions from his mother, brought himself to forget the enmity owed to his father’s killer, and even sought a marriage alliance with that state. His perversity was extreme! Yusun identified painting the pillars red and carving the rafters as a great wrong, whereas Gui remonstrated against conduct contrary to proper rules as though it were a minor fault. Alas! Yin could appreciate his minister, while Zhuang could not; yet in rejecting remonstrance they were alike. Was Gui, then, still inferior to Prince Kou?
“The first levy of a tax on fields.” 〔The fifteenth year of Duke Xuan; third month, “instituted the military levy by qiu”; Duke Cheng〕 “First year, spring”; “applied the field levy.” 〔The twelfth year of Duke Ai〕 [The placement of the dates and quotations in the transcription is doubtful.]

title: 隆慶元年應天府鄉試錄
text:
可式者
考試官左中允孫批主三傳意叙斷良是
考試官左諭德王批語有斷制可取
内君屢變取民之制春秋各指其失也甚矣民
不可過取也先王之法魯其三變矣春秋書之
曰初曰作曰用詞不一而所以示貶者則三致
意云昔先王之爲田制也有助有徹取之于民
皆什一其分爾我宣變之爲稅畝則廢公田而
履畝踰成法而倍入矣誠何心也謂資民以富
===
國雖取之不爲虐豈知損下卽以損上欲厚於
公獨不恤其私乎曰初者初失其故示不可以
有初也先王之爲兵制也或丘或甸寓之於農
僅五七其人爾我成變之爲丘甲則備一甲於
一丘合百人於一甸矣誠何心也謂益兵以禦
敵雖加之不爲過豈知役兵卽以役民欲實於
外寧不虛其中乎曰作者作法於貪示不可以
有作也至田以出粟賦以出車先王弛力薄征
之制未之有改也我哀變之爲田賦則軍旅之

punctuated:
可式者。
考試官左中允孫批：主三傳意，叙斷良是。
考試官左諭德王批：語有斷制，可取。
内君屢變取民之制，春秋各指其失也。甚矣，民不可過取也！先王之法，魯其三變矣。春秋書之，曰初，曰作，曰用，詞不一，而所以示貶者則三致意云。
昔先王之爲田制也，有助有徹，取之于民皆什一其分爾。我宣變之爲稅畝，則廢公田而履畝，踰成法而倍入矣。誠何心也？謂資民以富國，雖取之不爲虐，豈知損下卽以損上？欲厚於公，獨不恤其私乎？曰初者，初失其故，示不可以有初也。
先王之爲兵制也，或丘或甸，寓之於農，僅五七其人爾。我成變之爲丘甲，則備一甲於一丘，合百人於一甸矣。誠何心也？謂益兵以禦敵，雖加之不爲過，豈知役兵卽以役民？欲實於外，寧不虛其中乎？曰作者，作法於貪，示不可以有作也。
至田以出粟，賦以出車，先王弛力薄征之制，未之有改也。我哀變之爲田賦，則軍旅之

…that may serve as a model.
Examiner Sun, Left Companion to the Heir Apparent, comments: “It follows the meaning of the Three Commentaries; its exposition and judgments are indeed sound.”
Examiner Wang, Left Admonisher to the Heir Apparent, comments: “The language shows decisive judgment and is commendable.”
The rulers [?] repeatedly altered the system of levying resources from the people, and the Spring and Autumn Annals identifies the fault in each case. How grave a matter it is: one must not take excessively from the people! Lu altered the former kings’ laws three times. The Spring and Autumn Annals records these changes with the words “first,” “instituted,” and “employed.” Though the wording differs, it conveys censure with particular emphasis in all three cases.
When the former kings established the land system, there were the zhu system of communal labor and the che system of shared assessment; what they took from the people amounted only to a tenth of their allotted share. Our Duke Xuan changed this to taxation by the mu: he abolished the public fields and assessed the acreage, exceeding the established rule and doubling revenue. What was his intention? He supposed that drawing upon the people to enrich the state was no oppression, even though it meant taking from them. How could he fail to understand that diminishing those below thereby diminishes those above? In seeking abundance for the public treasury, could he alone disregard the people’s private means? The word “first” marks the first departure from the old practice and shows that such a beginning must not be made.
When the former kings established the military system, they organized it by qiu or dian territorial units, embedding military service in agriculture and requiring only five or seven men. Our Duke Cheng changed this to the levy of armor by the qiu: each qiu had to provide a full armored contingent, bringing the total to a hundred men per dian. What was his intention? He supposed that increasing troop strength to resist the enemy was no excess, even though it increased the levy. How could he fail to understand that putting soldiers into service means putting the people into service? In seeking strength abroad, would he not empty the country within? The word “instituted” means that he instituted a rule out of greed and shows that such an institution must not be made.
As for land yielding grain and military levies providing chariots, the former kings’ system of easing labor demands and keeping exactions light had not been altered. Our Duke Ai changed this to a military levy on the land, so that the army’s…

title: 隆慶元年應天府鄉試錄
text:
征在田商賈之賦皆農矣誠何心也謂年饑用
匱猶望於取二之外也豈知百姓不足之憂已
形諸有若之對而三家聚斂之謀頗勝於周公
之法耶曰用者用褎困農示不可以有用也要
之法可無變也民不可不恤也法變而國是日
非宣猶之成成猶之哀矣民貧而國勢浸弱哀
之弊基于成成之弊基于宣矣魯之不競坐此
春秋烏得而諱之耶嘗考書曰鑒于成憲其永
無愆詩曰誰生厲階至今爲梗魯宣不得辭其
===
責矣然宣之意主在加稅而成哀乃在益兵則
孰使之然耶當時諸侯益兵自齊桓內政始而
晉惠州兵次之以故丘甲田賦不書初貶魯而
罪齊晉之旨寓矣胡氏有言文見於此起義在
彼明春秋者辨之
禮記
頌而無諂諫而無驕
曹樓
同考試官知縣趙　批〔措語精邃命意剴切〕
punctuated:
征在田，商賈之賦皆農矣。誠何心也？謂年饑用匱，猶望於取二之外也。豈知百姓不足之憂，已形諸有若之對，而三家聚斂之謀，頗勝於周公之法耶？曰：「用者，用褎困農，示不可以有用也。」要之，法可無變也，民不可不恤也。法變而國是日非，宣猶之成，成猶之哀矣；民貧而國勢浸弱，哀之弊基于成，成之弊基于宣矣。魯之不競，坐此，春秋烏得而諱之耶？嘗考《書》曰：「鑒于成憲，其永無愆。」《詩》曰：「誰生厲階？至今爲梗。」魯宣不得辭其責矣。然宣之意主在加稅，而成、哀乃在益兵，則孰使之然耶？當時諸侯益兵，自齊桓內政始，而晉惠州兵次之。以故丘甲、田賦不書初，貶魯而罪齊、晉之旨寓矣。胡氏有言：「文見於此，起義在彼。」明春秋者辨之。

《禮記》
頌而無諂，諫而無驕。
曹樓
同考試官知縣趙　批〔措語精邃，命意剴切。〕
translation_en:
…the military levy fell upon the fields, and even the taxes of merchants and traders were borne by the farmers. What could his intention have been? He supposed that, with famine in the land and resources exhausted, he could still look for revenue beyond the two-tenths levy. How could he not realize that concern over the people's insufficiency had already found expression in You Ruo's reply, while the revenue-extracting schemes of the Three Houses had largely prevailed over the Duke of Zhou's institutions? The explanation is: “The word ‘employed’ indicates employing [something unclear] to impoverish farmers [?], showing that such employment was impermissible.”

In sum, the laws could have been left unchanged, but the people's welfare could not be disregarded. As the laws changed and the state's policies grew worse by the day, Duke Xuan became like Duke Cheng, and Duke Cheng like Duke Ai. As the people became impoverished and the state's strength gradually declined, the abuses under Duke Ai had their foundation in Duke Cheng's reign, and those under Duke Cheng in Duke Xuan's. Lu's weakness arose from this. How could the Spring and Autumn Annals conceal it? I have examined the statement in the Book of Documents: “Take established statutes as your mirror, and you will forever be without error.” The Book of Odes says: “Who created the steps to disaster, which remain an obstruction to this day?” Duke Xuan of Lu cannot escape responsibility.

Yet Duke Xuan's chief intention was to increase taxation, whereas Dukes Cheng and Ai sought to increase military strength. Who, then, brought this about? Among the regional lords of that time, military expansion began with Duke Huan of Qi's internal administration, followed by Duke Hui of Jin's establishment of troops by district. Thus, the entries concerning the armor levy by hill-unit and the field levy do not include the word ‘first’: implicit in their censure of Lu is an intention to condemn Qi and Jin. Master Hu said: “The wording appears here, but the interpretive principle originates there.” Those who understand the Spring and Autumn Annals will discern this.

Book of Rites
“Praise without flattery; remonstrate without arrogance.”
Cao Lou

title: 隆慶元年應天府鄉試錄
text:
將必事君而不失其正者
考試官左中允孫　批　〔忠愛之意藹然〕
考試官左諭德王　批　〔是能無諂無驕者〕
臣之進言於君者有將順之忠有匡救之忠蓋
臣以實心事君爲忠也不然非爲祿即爲名矣
亦何取於進言哉記少儀者之意豈不以爲臣
者之上交於君也進言各因乎事人人殊矣因
言可以知心而忠否別焉其致一也是故吾嘗
有見于須君者矣君位乎天地之中一人有道
===
四海無虞宗社靈長所基也不可以弗須也曰
行帝道而帝行王道而王誠須之矣君聞而善
之宜也然而深慶之餘不可無厚望之意或者
勤于初而有怠于後即須言啓之耳臣之懼也
而可讇乎讇何心也忠臣不若是也故須而無
讇斯可矣又嘗有見于諫君者矣君處乎臣民
之上一念有差庶事或舛國家安危所關也不
可以弗諫也曰過有所當改闕有所當補誠諫
之矣君聞而從之幸也然而謀國之際不可有
punctuated:
將必事君而不失其正者。

考試官左中允孫　批　〔忠愛之意藹然〕
考試官左諭德王　批　〔是能無諂無驕者〕

臣之進言於君者，有將順之忠，有匡救之忠。蓋臣以實心事君爲忠也，不然，非爲祿即爲名矣，亦何取於進言哉？記少儀者之意，豈不以爲臣者之上交於君也，進言各因乎事，人人殊矣；因言可以知心，而忠否別焉，其致一也。是故吾嘗有見于須君者矣。君位乎天地之中，一人有道，四海無虞，宗社靈長所基也，不可以弗須也。曰：「行帝道而帝，行王道而王。」誠須之矣，君聞而善之，宜也。然而深慶之餘，不可無厚望之意。或者勤于初而有怠于後，即須言啓之耳，臣之懼也，而可讇乎？讇何心也？忠臣不若是也。故須而無讇，斯可矣。又嘗有見于諫君者矣。君處乎臣民之上，一念有差，庶事或舛，國家安危所關也，不可以弗諫也。曰：「過有所當改，闕有所當補。」誠諫之矣，君聞而從之，幸也。然而謀國之際，不可有
translation_en:
…will surely serve their ruler without departing from what is right.

Examiner Sun, Left Companion to the Heir Apparent, comments: 〔The spirit of loyalty and loving concern is abundantly evident.〕
Examiner Wang, Left Admonisher to the Heir Apparent, comments: 〔Here is someone capable of being free of both flattery and arrogance.〕

When a minister offers counsel to his ruler, there is the loyalty that supports and furthers his good intentions, and there is the loyalty that corrects and remedies his faults. Loyalty consists in serving the ruler with a sincere heart. Otherwise, one seeks either emolument or fame: what value would there be in offering counsel? Surely the intention of the author of “Minor Rules of Propriety” was this: when ministers address their superior, the ruler, their counsel responds to particular circumstances and differs from person to person. Yet their words reveal their hearts and distinguish loyalty from its absence; in this, their purpose is one.

Thus I have observed those who praise their ruler. [The transcription repeatedly has 須, apparently standing for 頌, “praise” [?].] The ruler occupies the center of Heaven and Earth. If this one man possesses the Way, all within the Four Seas are free from anxiety: this is the foundation of the enduring blessings of the ancestral temples and the altars of soil and grain. One cannot refrain from praising him. To say, “Practice the Way of the ancient emperors and become an emperor; practice the Way of the ancient kings and become a king,” is indeed to praise him. It is fitting that the ruler should hear this and approve. Yet alongside profound rejoicing there must also be an abiding sense of high expectations. Should he be diligent at first but grow indolent later, it may be these very words of praise that encourage this. That is what a minister fears. How, then, could he flatter? What sort of heart does flattery reveal? A loyal minister is not like this. Thus praise without flattery is acceptable.

I have also observed those who remonstrate with their ruler. The ruler stands above his ministers and people. If a single thought goes astray, the many affairs of government may fall into disorder: the security or peril of the state depends upon this. One cannot refrain from remonstrating. To say, “There are faults that ought to be corrected and deficiencies that ought to be made good,” is indeed to remonstrate. It is fortunate if the ruler hears and follows this counsel. Yet when deliberating for the state, there must not be…

title: 隆慶元年應天府鄉試錄
text:
自爲之圖或者閒其政而未格其心卽諫言徒
焉耳臣之懼也而可驕乎驕何心也忠臣不若
是也故諫而無驕斯可矣要之須以成美諫以
救過其義各殊均之不能無也謂以要君驕以
自矜其失各殊均之不可有也人君聽言其亦
知所辨哉抑君臣之義大矣一命以上修職奉
公俾吾君增美而鮮過保治安于長永臣之心
也何以謂且驕爲耶自堂陛之分旣懸其勢易
謂而驕心生於好名故競爲矯拂之行過則歸
===
君功則自居其於忠愛之實何如哉故曰爲名
譽而爲害則其害必不誠爲利祿而效忠則其
忠必不盡噫此非獨進言者責也
夫孝置之而塞乎天地溥之而橫乎四海
施諸後世而無朝夕推而放諸東海而
準推而放諸西海而準推而放諸南海
而準推而放諸北海而準
李天植
同考試官知縣趙　批〔格致暇雅而意復融〕
punctuated:
自爲之圖。或者閒其政而未格其心，卽諫言徒焉耳，臣之懼也。而可驕乎？驕何心也？忠臣不若是也，故諫而無驕斯可矣。要之，須以成美，諫以救過，其義各殊，均之不能無也；謂以要君，驕以自矜，其失各殊，均之不可有也。人君聽言，其亦知所辨哉！抑君臣之義大矣！一命以上，修職奉公，俾吾君增美而鮮過，保治安于長永，臣之心也，何以謂且驕爲耶？自堂陛之分旣懸，其勢易謂，而驕心生於好名，故競爲矯拂之行，過則歸君，功則自居，其於忠愛之實何如哉？故曰：「爲名譽而爲害，則其害必不誠；爲利祿而效忠，則其忠必不盡。」噫！此非獨進言者責也。
夫孝，置之而塞乎天地，溥之而橫乎四海，施諸後世而無朝夕，推而放諸東海而準，推而放諸西海而準，推而放諸南海而準，推而放諸北海而準。
李天植
同考試官知縣趙　批〔格致暇雅，而意復融〕
translation_en:
…schemes for one's own advantage. Perhaps one checks his policies without rectifying his heart, so that remonstrance amounts to mere words: this is what I, his servant, fear. How, then, could one be arrogant? What disposition would such arrogance reveal? A loyal minister is not like this. Thus, one should remonstrate without arrogance. In essence, praise [?] serves to perfect what is good, and remonstrance to remedy faults. Their purposes differ, yet neither can be dispensed with. Flattery [?] serves to exact something from the ruler, and arrogance to exalt oneself. Their failings differ, yet neither can be tolerated. When a ruler listens to counsel, surely he should know how to distinguish them!
Moreover, great indeed are the obligations between ruler and minister! From the lowest appointed rank upward, officials should discharge their duties and serve the public, enabling our ruler to increase his virtues and diminish his faults, and preserving good government and peace forever. Such is a minister's intention. What use, then, are flattery [?] and arrogance? Since the distinction between the hall and its steps—the ruler and his ministers—is so pronounced, their relative positions readily encourage flattery [?], while arrogance arises from a fondness for reputation. Thus men compete in acts of defiance, attributing faults to the ruler while claiming achievements for themselves. How does this accord with genuine loyalty and devotion? Hence the saying: “If one does harm [?] for the sake of reputation, that harm [?] will surely lack sincerity; if one renders loyal service for profit and emolument, that loyalty will surely be incomplete.” Alas! Responsibility for this does not rest solely with those who offer counsel.
As for filial piety: set it forth, and it fills Heaven and Earth; spread it abroad, and it extends across the Four Seas. Apply it to later generations, and it knows neither morning nor evening. Extend it to the Eastern Sea, and it holds true; extend it to the Western Sea, and it holds true; extend it to the Southern Sea, and it holds true; extend it to the Northern Sea, and it holds true.
Li Tianzhi.
Associate Examiner Zhao, District Magistrate, comments: 〔The composition's manner is composed and elegant [?], and its meaning, moreover, flows…〕

title: 隆慶元年應天府鄉試錄
text:
暢讀之興孝之意躍然
考試官左中允孫　批〔以人心明孝道意味雋永〕
考試官左諭德王　批〔粹古之文〕
孝道通於無間即人心之同可見矣甚矣孝道
之大也天地之經而人是則焉其孰有外之者
哉曾子自得之學因述之以教人也意曰天下
之道有五父子之親居一孝以事親子道則然
耳是道也根諸性命之微著爲倫理之顯故置
之而塞乎天地焉天高地下合覆載之所有至
大而無垠上蟠下際極愛敬之充周亦大而無
外矣又溥之而橫乎四海焉四海至遠也孝之
道遠而必屆有不可以方所限者又施諸後世
而無朝夕焉後世至久也孝之道久而不已有
不可以朝夕計者夫若此盈宇宙間皆孝之寓
矣何其大也然而天地不可窮後世不可即自
其橫乎四海者言之天機之流動若或推而使
行人心之統同隨所放而必至故放之乎極東
海之地則準之者盡東海之人矣而西海猶之
punctuated:
暢，讀之，興孝之意躍然。
考試官左中允孫，批〔以人心明孝道，意味雋永〕。
考試官左諭德王，批〔粹古之文〕。
孝道通於無間，即人心之同可見矣。甚矣，孝道之大也！天地之經，而人是則焉，其孰有外之者哉？曾子自得之學，因述之以教人也。意曰：天下之道有五，父子之親居一。孝以事親，子道則然耳。是道也，根諸性命之微，著爲倫理之顯，故置之而塞乎天地焉。天高地下，合覆載之所有，至大而無垠；上蟠下際，極愛敬之充周，亦大而無外矣。又溥之而橫乎四海焉。四海至遠也，孝之道遠而必屆，有不可以方所限者。又施諸後世而無朝夕焉。後世至久也，孝之道久而不已，有不可以朝夕計者。夫若此，盈宇宙間皆孝之寓矣，何其大也！然而天地不可窮，後世不可即。自其橫乎四海者言之，天機之流動，若或推而使行；人心之統同，隨所放而必至。故放之乎極東海之地，則準之者盡東海之人矣，而西海猶之
translation_en:
…flowing freely. Reading it vividly awakens the impulse toward filial devotion.
Examiner Sun, Left Companion to the Heir Apparent, comments: 〔It elucidates the Way of filial piety through the human heart; its meaning is rich and enduring.〕
Examiner Wang, Left Admonisher to the Heir Apparent, comments: 〔Writing of pure antique quality.〕
That the Way of filial piety extends everywhere without interruption can be seen from what human hearts share. How great indeed is the Way of filial piety! It is the constant norm of Heaven and Earth, which human beings take as their rule: who could stand outside it? Zengzi expounded the learning he had personally grasped in order to teach others. His meaning was this: of the five relationships governing the world, affection between father and son is one. To serve one's parents with filial devotion is simply what the Way of a son requires. This Way is rooted in the subtle depths of our nature and Heaven-given endowment and manifests itself visibly in the order of human relationships. Thus, set in place, it fills Heaven and Earth. Heaven is high and Earth low; together, all that they cover and sustain is supremely vast and boundless. Reaching above and extending below, love and reverence, when fully expanded to pervade all things, are likewise so great that nothing lies outside them. Spread abroad, this Way extends across the Four Seas. The Four Seas are exceedingly distant, yet however far away, the Way of filial piety must reach them: it cannot be confined by location. Applied to later generations, it knows neither morning nor evening. Later generations stretch into the remotest future, yet however long the duration, the Way of filial piety never ceases: it cannot be measured by mornings and evenings. If this is so, everything filling the universe is a dwelling place of filial piety. How great it is! Yet Heaven and Earth cannot be exhaustively explored, nor can later generations be directly reached. Let us speak of its extension across the Four Seas. The natural workings of Heaven flow as though something were pushing them onward; because human hearts are united in what they share, wherever this Way is extended, it must arrive. Thus, if extended to the farthest lands of the Eastern Sea, all the people of the Eastern Sea find it their standard; and the Western Sea is likewise…

title: 隆慶元年應天府鄉試錄
text:
□也南海猶之西也北海猶之南也此彊彼□
地不同而人則同有非父母生之者乎內夏外
夷人不同而心必同有不知父子之親者乎天
經地義四海一家等也即人可以窮天地矣合
敬同愛刑于四海可也即今可以徵後世矣大
哉孝乎其三極之所以立而萬世之所以永者
乎抑曾子斯言言乎道耳未及其人也故復見
之經自天子至於庶人悉舉其義合而觀之交
相發矣夫孔子論弟子之職先孝其所答問若
===
游夏諸賢多矣然以孝名者不數而曾子之傳
乃發其蘊以教萬世惟其有之故能言之是豈
聲音笑貌爲哉故曰孝德之本也教之所由生
也
第貳場
論
聖神繼天立極
唐鶴徵
同考試官教授梁　批　天生堯舜以開萬世
punctuated:
□也，南海猶之西也，北海猶之南也。此彊彼□，地不同而人則同，有非父母生之者乎？內夏外夷，人不同而心必同，有不知父子之親者乎？天經地義，四海一家等也，即人可以窮天地矣；合敬同愛，刑于四海可也，即今可以徵後世矣。大哉，孝乎！其三極之所以立而萬世之所以永者乎！抑曾子斯言，言乎道耳，未及其人也。故復見之經，自天子至於庶人，悉舉其義，合而觀之，交相發矣。夫孔子論弟子之職，先孝，其所答問，若游夏諸賢多矣。然以孝名者不數，而曾子之傳乃發其蘊，以教萬世。惟其有之，故能言之，是豈聲音笑貌爲哉？故曰：「孝，德之本也，教之所由生也。」
第貳場
論
聖神繼天立極
唐鶴徵
同考試官教授梁，批：天生堯舜，以開萬世
translation_en:
…[illegible]; the southern sea is like the western, and the northern sea is like the southern. This territory and that [illegible] [?]: the lands differ, but their people are alike. Is there anyone not born of parents? Whether among the Xia within or the Yi beyond, people differ, but their hearts must be alike. Is there anyone who does not know the affection between father and son? As the constant principle of Heaven and the proper order of Earth, filial piety makes all within the four seas one family, equal in this respect. Through human beings one can thus comprehend Heaven and Earth. Shared reverence and common love can serve as a model throughout the four seas; through the present one can thus ascertain what will hold for later generations. How great is filial piety! Is it not that by which the three ultimate orders—Heaven, Earth, and humanity—are established, and by which ten thousand generations endure? Yet these words of Zengzi speak only of the Way, without yet addressing those who practice it. Thus it appears again in the Classic: from the Son of Heaven down to the common people, its meaning is fully set forth. Read together, these passages illuminate one another. When Confucius discussed the duties of the young, he placed filial piety first. Many worthy men, such as Ziyou and Zixia, received his answers to their questions. Yet few were renowned for filial piety, whereas the tradition transmitted by Zengzi disclosed its deeper meaning to teach ten thousand generations. Only because he possessed it could he speak of it. Could this be accomplished merely through tone of voice and a smiling countenance? Thus it is said: “Filial piety is the root of virtue and the source from which teaching arises.”

Second Session
Discourse
“The Sage and Spiritually Perceptive Rulers Continue Heaven’s Work and Establish the Supreme Standard”
Tang Hezheng

Comment by Associate Examiner Liang, Professor: Heaven brought forth Yao and Shun to inaugurate, for ten thousand generations …

title: 隆慶元年應天府鄉試錄
text:
道統之傳立萬世人極之準一一盡之此篇擬
極精奧而筆力雄健古雅淵宏脫去時格高薦
允宜
同考試官教授趙　批　題本正大作者頗多
浮泛此作獨深探本原發千古聖神傳心之要
且格高詞古學識兼到之士也宜錄以式
同考試官知州陳　批　此題論聖人得統於
天而立萬世之人極不外一中予獨推究本原
且布置有體裁議論有氣脉擅場之作也敬服
===
敬服
考試官左中允孫　批　說執中即是立極處語有
根據而抑揚開闔通篇一氣可成足稱論手矣
考試官左諭德王　批　說堯舜之心處雋永有味
宜冠多士
聖人肇斯道之傳而天下萬世之人極立焉謂
非得統於天不可也夫道在天下未嘗一日息
也其統之有宗其會之有元其繼而承之有自
也故絕而復續仆而旋起亘千萬年如一日夫
punctuated:
道統之傳，立萬世人極之準，一一盡之。此篇擬極精奧，而筆力雄健，古雅淵宏，脫去時格，高薦允宜。

同考試官教授趙批：題本正大，作者頗多浮泛，此作獨深探本原，發千古聖神傳心之要，且格高詞古，學識兼到之士也，宜錄以式。

同考試官知州陳批：此題論聖人得統於天，而立萬世之人極，不外一中。予獨推究本原，且布置有體裁，議論有氣脉，擅場之作也。敬服，敬服。

考試官左中允孫批：說執中即是立極處，語有根據，而抑揚開闔，通篇一氣可成，足稱論手矣。

考試官左諭德王批：說堯舜之心處，雋永有味，宜冠多士。

聖人肇斯道之傳，而天下萬世之人極立焉，謂非得統於天不可也。夫道在天下，未嘗一日息也。其統之有宗，其會之有元，其繼而承之有自也，故絕而復續，仆而旋起，亘千萬年如一日。夫
translation_en:
…the transmission of the succession to the Way, and the establishment of a standard for the supreme norm of humanity for all ages: each is treated exhaustively. This essay’s conception is exceptionally subtle and profound, and its writing vigorous and forceful, classically elegant, deep, and expansive. It rises above the fashionable style of the day; a high recommendation is entirely fitting.

Associate Examiner Zhao, Professor, comments: The topic itself is upright and grand, but many writers treat it superficially and vaguely. This work alone probes deeply into its origins and brings out the essential teaching transmitted from mind to mind by the sages and spiritual exemplars throughout the ages. Moreover, its style is elevated and its diction antique. This is a scholar accomplished in both learning and discernment. His work should be included as a model.

Associate Examiner Chen, Department Magistrate, comments: This topic discusses how the sages received the succession from Heaven and established the supreme norm of humanity for all ages; it comes down to the single principle of the Mean. “I alone” [?] investigate its origins thoroughly. Moreover, the arrangement has proper form, and the argument has vitality and continuity. This is a work that outshines the field. I admire it, I admire it.

Examiner Sun, Left Companion of the Heir Apparent, comments: The explanation that holding fast to the Mean is precisely what constitutes establishing the supreme norm is well grounded. Through its rises and falls, openings and closings, the entire essay forms one continuous flow. The author fully deserves to be called a master of the discourse.

Examiner Wang, Left Admonisher of the Heir Apparent, comments: The passage explaining the minds of Yao and Shun has enduring depth and savor. It deserves to rank first among the many candidates.

The sages initiated the transmission of this Way, and thereby the supreme norm of humanity was established for all under Heaven and for all ages. One cannot say that they did not receive the succession from Heaven. The Way has never ceased to exist in the world for even a single day. Its succession has a source; its convergence has an origin; its continuation and inheritance have a point of departure. Thus, when severed, it is renewed; when cast down, it soon rises again. Across thousands and tens of thousands of years, it remains as it was on a single day. Now, …

title: 隆慶元年應天府鄉試錄
text:
固聖賢承傳之緒可灼睹矣乃若原其始之所
肇端一元初分大道方隱聖人者崛起其間亦
何所繼且承哉而獨闡斯道之秘以開萬世之
傳斯非繼天而有作者乎故原道統之傳者必
遡於聖人原聖人之道統者必遡於天語天而
道之大原見矣子朱子序中庸而推本上古聖
神繼天立極可謂善原道者歟夫道統之說尚
矣孟子叙堯舜以至孔子韓愈氏叙堯舜以至
孟子皆言道肇於堯舜而未遡其原也至董子
===
則曰道之大原出於天而宋儒稱堯亦謂其得
統於天則子朱子之說也請申之夫窮天地亘
古今而常存不息者此道也道之窮天地亘古
今而傳之無弊者此中也中也者道之極也天
地所以位也日月所以明也四時所以行也人
倫所以叙也物則所以著也禮樂刑政所由以
生天下國家所由以理也其理各足於吾性而
其原則命於天不觀之易乎易卦肇自龍馬之
圖以五生數統五成數而虛五與十於中其名
punctuated:
固聖賢承傳之緒可灼睹矣。乃若原其始之所肇端，一元初分，大道方隱，聖人者崛起其間，亦何所繼且承哉？而獨闡斯道之秘，以開萬世之傳，斯非繼天而有作者乎？故原道統之傳者，必遡於聖人；原聖人之道統者，必遡於天。語天，而道之大原見矣。子朱子序《中庸》，而推本上古聖神繼天立極，可謂善原道者歟！夫道統之說尚矣。孟子叙堯舜以至孔子，韓愈氏叙堯舜以至孟子，皆言道肇於堯舜，而未遡其原也。至董子，則曰：「道之大原出於天。」而宋儒稱堯，亦謂其得統於天，則子朱子之說也。

請申之。夫窮天地、亘古今而常存不息者，此道也；道之窮天地、亘古今而傳之無弊者，此中也。中也者，道之極也。天地所以位也，日月所以明也，四時所以行也，人倫所以叙也，物則所以著也，禮樂刑政所由以生，天下國家所由以理也。其理各足於吾性，而其原則命於天。不觀之《易》乎？《易》卦肇自龍馬之圖，以五生數統五成數，而虛五與十於中，其名
translation_en:
…indeed, the thread of transmission carried on by sages and worthies can be clearly discerned. Yet if we trace back to its very inception, when the primordial unity first divided and the Great Way was still hidden, what was there for the sages who arose in that age to continue and inherit? They alone disclosed the mysteries of this Way, thereby initiating its transmission for myriad generations. Were they not, then, men who continued Heaven’s work and brought something into being? Thus, whoever traces the transmission of the succession to the Way must go back to the sages; whoever traces the sages’ succession to the Way must go back to Heaven. Once Heaven is spoken of, the great source of the Way becomes apparent. In his preface to the Doctrine of the Mean, our Master Zhu traced its origins to the sages and spiritual men of high antiquity, who continued Heaven’s work and established the ultimate standard. May he not be called adept at tracing the origins of the Way? The account of the succession to the Way is ancient indeed. Mengzi recounted the succession from Yao and Shun down to Kongzi, and Han Yu recounted it from Yao and Shun down to Mengzi. Both said that the Way began with Yao and Shun, but neither traced it to its source. Master Dong, however, said: “The great source of the Way comes forth from Heaven.” And when the Confucian scholars of the Song spoke of Yao, they likewise said that he received the succession from Heaven. This, then, is our Master Zhu’s account.

Allow me to elaborate. What extends throughout Heaven and Earth, spans antiquity and the present, and constantly endures without ceasing is this Way. That by which the Way extends throughout Heaven and Earth, spans antiquity and the present, and is transmitted without impairment is this Mean. The Mean is the ultimate standard of the Way. It is that by which Heaven and Earth take their places, the sun and moon shine, the four seasons proceed, human relationships are ordered, and the principles governing things become manifest. It is that from which rites, music, punishments, and government arise, and by which all under Heaven, states, and families are brought into order. These principles are each fully present in our nature, while their source lies in Heaven’s decree. Do we not see this in the Book of Changes? The hexagrams of the Changes originated in the diagram borne by the dragon-horse. Its five generating numbers govern its five completing numbers, while five and ten are left vacant at the center. Its name…

title: 隆慶元年應天府鄉試錄
text:
曰太極不觀之書乎箕疇肇自神龜之書以五
奇數統四偶數而實五於中其名曰皇極合易
與書觀之是極之云者天然自有之中至極而
無以加也加之毫末則太過太過非中矣亦無
以損也損之毫末則不及不及非中矣然其初
也呈於圖象已爾隱於卦畫已爾兆於混兮闢
兮之天含於未雕未斵之人不識不知已爾上
古之世伏羲神農黃帝氏代作非不由之而忘
於言者時之未至聖人不欲以鑿其眞也至堯
===
之時黎民有待于變則固已有偏黨失中過與
不及者矣堯蓋有憂之曰弗立之準天下曷趨
焉弗洩其秘萬世曷傳焉於是揭執中之旨而
授之舜非徒以授舜也所以授之天下萬世以
立斯道之極也有虞之末民生雖貯感物而動
人心危而道心微矣故舜之授禹復益以精一
之言非徒以授禹也所以授之天下萬世以開
心學之源也予讀二典至此有以仰窺堯舜至
公無我之心焉蓋中者堯舜所受於天之道也
punctuated: 曰太極。不觀之《書》乎？箕疇肇自神龜之書，以五奇數統四偶數，而實五於中，其名曰皇極。合《易》與《書》觀之，是極之云者，天然自有之中，至極而無以加也。加之毫末則太過，太過非中矣；亦無以損也，損之毫末則不及，不及非中矣。然其初也，呈於圖象已爾，隱於卦畫已爾，兆於混兮闢兮之天，含於未雕未斵之人，不識不知已爾。上古之世，伏羲、神農、黃帝氏代作，非不由之，而忘於言者，時之未至，聖人不欲以鑿其眞也。至堯之時，黎民有待于變，則固已有偏黨失中、過與不及者矣。堯蓋有憂之，曰：「弗立之準，天下曷趨焉？弗洩其秘，萬世曷傳焉？」於是揭執中之旨而授之舜，非徒以授舜也，所以授之天下萬世，以立斯道之極也。有虞之末，民生雖貯，感物而動，人心危而道心微矣。故舜之授禹，復益以精一之言，非徒以授禹也，所以授之天下萬世，以開心學之源也。予讀二典至此，有以仰窺堯舜至公無我之心焉。蓋中者，堯舜所受於天之道也。
translation_en:
…is called the Supreme Ultimate. Do we not also see this in the Book of Documents? The categories of Jizi originated in the writing borne by the divine tortoise: the five odd numbers govern the four even numbers, with five occupying the center. This is called the August Ultimate. Considering the Book of Changes and the Book of Documents together, what they call the “ultimate” is the mean naturally inherent in things, perfect in its utmost degree, to which nothing can be added. Add the slightest amount, and there is excess; excess is not the mean. Nor can anything be taken away: subtract the slightest amount, and there is deficiency; deficiency is not the mean. Yet from the beginning it was already thus when displayed in diagrams and images, and already thus when concealed in the lines of the hexagrams. It first showed itself in Heaven amid primordial chaos and the opening of the cosmos, and lay within human beings as yet uncarved and unhewn. Even without awareness or knowledge, it was already thus. In high antiquity, Fuxi, Shennong, and Huangdi arose in succession. It was not that they failed to follow it; they left it unspoken because the time had not yet come, and the sages did not wish to impair its authenticity by artificially working upon it.

By Yao’s time, the common people still awaited transformation, so there were already those who, through bias and faction, lost the mean and fell into excess or deficiency. Yao was presumably concerned about this and said: “If no standard is established for it, toward what will all under Heaven turn? If its mystery is not disclosed, how will it be transmitted through the ages?” He therefore proclaimed the principle of holding fast to the mean and entrusted it to Shun. This was not merely to entrust it to Shun, but to entrust it to all under Heaven and to all generations, thereby establishing the ultimate standard of this Way. Toward the end of the reign of Youyu, although the people’s livelihood was provisioned [?], they were stirred by contact with things: the human mind was precarious, and the mind of the Way was subtle. Thus, when Shun entrusted it to Yu, he further added the injunction to be discerning and single-minded. This was not merely to entrust it to Yu, but to entrust it to all under Heaven and to all generations, thereby opening the source of the learning of the mind. When I read the Two Canons to this point, I can reverently glimpse the supremely impartial and selfless minds of Yao and Shun. For the mean is the Way that Yao and Shun received from Heaven.

title: 隆慶元年應天府鄉試錄
text:
堯舜用是道以治唐虞之天下至是幾二千年及
汲於天下萬世之傳也或曰將以天下與人不
得不幷傳其治之之法是則然矣而堯舜之心
則不盡於是也其心蓋曰道行于身則澤被於
天下道傳於人則功施於萬世被於天下者有
盡施於萬世者無窮故吾用吾中以親睦九族
平章百姓協和萬邦豈若使萬世之家齊國治
而天下平也吾用吾中以在璿璣玉衡以封山
濬川以若于上下草木鳥獸豈若使萬世之天
===
地位而萬物育也吾用吾中而考中星以正日
置閏法以定時豈若使萬世之日月行而四時
序也吾用吾中以播百穀敷五教豈若使萬世
之民生厚而彝倫叙也吾用吾中以典三禮諧
八音明五刑豈若使萬世之禮樂明備而刑協
于中也吾用吾中以舉元凱誅四凶豈若使萬
世之君子進而小人退也於是揭而授之二聖
以傳之無窮庶幾萬世而下有堯舜者出焉則
今日之治猶可復見而道不至吾身而遂止也
punctuated: 堯舜用是道以治唐虞之天下，至是幾二千年，及汲於天下萬世之傳也。或曰：「將以天下與人，不得不幷傳其治之之法。」是則然矣，而堯舜之心則不盡於是也。其心蓋曰：「道行于身，則澤被於天下；道傳於人，則功施於萬世。被於天下者有盡，施於萬世者無窮。故吾用吾中以親睦九族，平章百姓，協和萬邦，豈若使萬世之家齊、國治而天下平也？吾用吾中以在璿璣玉衡，以封山濬川，以若于上下草木鳥獸，豈若使萬世之天地位而萬物育也？吾用吾中而考中星以正日，置閏法以定時，豈若使萬世之日月行而四時序也？吾用吾中以播百穀，敷五教，豈若使萬世之民生厚而彝倫叙也？吾用吾中以典三禮，諧八音，明五刑，豈若使萬世之禮樂明備而刑協于中也？吾用吾中以舉元凱，誅四凶，豈若使萬世之君子進而小人退也？」於是揭而授之二聖，以傳之無窮，庶幾萬世而下有堯舜者出焉，則今日之治猶可復見，而道不至吾身而遂止也。
translation_en:
Yao and Shun used this Way to govern the world under Tang and Yu. By this point, nearly two thousand years had passed, and they urgently concerned themselves with its transmission throughout the world for all generations [?; the transcription here is doubtful]. Some say: “When handing the realm over to another, one must also transmit the methods by which it is governed.” This is true, but Yao and Shun’s intentions were not exhausted by this consideration. Their thinking was, surely, as follows:

“When the Way is put into practice in one’s own person, its benefits extend throughout the world; when the Way is transmitted to others, its achievements reach ten thousand generations. What extends throughout the world has its limits; what reaches ten thousand generations is inexhaustible. Thus, I employ my mean to bring affection and harmony to the nine degrees of kinship, to distinguish and order the hundred clans, and to harmonize the myriad states. Yet how could this compare with ensuring that, for ten thousand generations, families are well ordered, states well governed, and the world at peace?

“I employ my mean to examine the jeweled celestial instrument and jade sighting tube, to mark out the mountains and dredge the rivers, and to accord with what is above and below, with plants and trees, birds and beasts. Yet how could this compare with ensuring that, for ten thousand generations, Heaven and Earth occupy their proper places and all things flourish? I employ my mean to observe the stars at culmination and thereby determine the days, and to establish rules for intercalation and thereby fix the seasons. Yet how could this compare with ensuring that, for ten thousand generations, the sun and moon follow their courses and the four seasons proceed in order?

“I employ my mean to sow the hundred grains and disseminate the five teachings. Yet how could this compare with ensuring that, for ten thousand generations, the people’s livelihood is abundant and the constant human relationships are properly ordered? I employ my mean to oversee the three rites, harmonize the eight classes of musical sounds, and make the five punishments clear. Yet how could this compare with ensuring that, for ten thousand generations, rites and music are fully articulated and complete, and punishments accord with the mean? I employ my mean to promote the Eight Yuan and Eight Kai and punish the Four Evildoers. Yet how could this compare with ensuring that, for ten thousand generations, exemplary men advance and petty men withdraw?”

Thus they made this teaching explicit and imparted it to the two sages, so that it might be transmitted without end. Their hope was that, ten thousand generations later, men like Yao and Shun would emerge; then the good government of their own day could once again be seen, and the Way would not come to an end with their own persons.

title: 隆慶元年應天府鄉試錄
text:
此堯舜之心也故孔子刪書斷自唐虞而詳其
授受之旨明上古之道於是始開萬世之人極
於是始立也是極也即易所謂太極書所謂皇
極者也建之則君道修否則蠡蟊之則天下治
否則亂如衡之於輕重然重者過之輕之者不
及也故衡誠縣不可欺以輕重如準之於高下
然高者過之下之者不及也故準誠設不可欺
以高下堯舜之道天下萬世之衡準也不可易
也夫堯舜之心無窮而其道又不可易如此是
===
故由堯舜以前繼天以立極者堯舜也由堯舜
以後繼堯舜以保極者猶夫堯舜也禹之安汝
止惟幾惟康者此極也湯之建中于民以義制
事以禮制心者此極也文之緝熙敬止武之敬
勝義勝此極也禹湯文武用堯舜之中以成夏
商周之治舉千九百年之天下而納之時雍風
動之域者謂非堯舜繼天立極之功乎周衰道
亡天下分為列國孔子大聖不得位而繼往開
來之責有不可辭者於是祖述堯舜之道授之
punctuated: 此堯舜之心也。故孔子刪《書》，斷自唐虞，而詳其授受之旨，明上古之道於是始開，萬世之人極於是始立也。是極也，即《易》所謂太極、《書》所謂皇極者也。建之則君道修，否則蠡；蟊之則天下治，否則亂。如衡之於輕重然，重者過之，輕之者不及也。故衡誠縣，不可欺以輕重。如準之於高下然，高者過之，下之者不及也。故準誠設，不可欺以高下。堯舜之道，天下萬世之衡準也，不可易也。夫堯舜之心無窮，而其道又不可易如此，是故由堯舜以前，繼天以立極者堯舜也；由堯舜以後，繼堯舜以保極者猶夫堯舜也。禹之安汝止、惟幾惟康者，此極也；湯之建中于民、以義制事、以禮制心者，此極也；文之緝熙敬止、武之敬勝義勝，此極也。禹湯文武用堯舜之中，以成夏商周之治，舉千九百年之天下，而納之時雍風動之域者，謂非堯舜繼天立極之功乎？周衰道亡，天下分為列國。孔子大聖，不得位，而繼往開來之責有不可辭者，於是祖述堯舜之道，授之
translation_en:
Such was the intention of Yao and Shun. Thus, when Confucius edited the Book of Documents, he chose to begin with Tang and Yu and set forth in detail the meaning of their transmission and reception of rule. He thereby made clear that the Way of high antiquity first unfolded here, and that the standard for humanity for all ages was first established here. This standard is precisely what the Book of Changes calls the Supreme Ultimate and the Book of Documents calls the Sovereign Ultimate. Establish it, and the ruler’s Way is cultivated; otherwise, it deteriorates [?]. Apply it [?], and all under Heaven is well governed; otherwise, disorder prevails.

It is like a balance in relation to weight: what is heavy exceeds its measure, and what is light falls short. Thus, if a balance is properly suspended, one cannot deceive it about weight. It is like a level in relation to height: what is high exceeds its measure, and what is low falls short. Thus, if a level is properly set, one cannot deceive it about height. The Way of Yao and Shun is the balance and level for all under Heaven through all ages; it cannot be altered. Since the intentions of Yao and Shun extend without limit, and their Way is likewise unalterable, it follows that, considering the ages down to Yao and Shun, those who carried on Heaven’s work and established the standard were Yao and Shun; considering the ages after them, those who continued their work and preserved the standard were still, in this sense, Yao and Shun themselves.

Yu’s injunctions to “rest in your proper stopping place” and to “attend to the incipient signs and to well-being” express this standard. Tang’s establishing the mean among the people, regulating affairs through righteousness, and regulating the mind through ritual propriety express this standard. King Wen’s continuing in luminous virtue and abiding in reverence, and King Wu’s making reverence and righteousness prevail, express this standard. Yu, Tang, Wen, and Wu employed the mean of Yao and Shun to achieve the good government of the Xia, Shang, and Zhou. For nineteen hundred years, they brought all under Heaven into a realm of harmony, transformed as if moved by the wind. Could one say that this was not the achievement of Yao and Shun in carrying on Heaven’s work and establishing the standard?

When the Zhou declined and the Way was lost, all under Heaven divided into separate states. Confucius, though a great sage, did not obtain a position of authority; yet he could not decline the responsibility of carrying forward the past and opening the way for the future. He therefore took the Way of Yao and Shun as his ancestral model and transmitted it to …

title: 隆慶元年應天府鄉試錄
text:
門弟子一貫以傳曾子是堯之中也傳約以示
顏子是舜之精一也而子思復以所受於曾子
者作爲中庸一書首言天命之性以見大道之
原繼言中爲天下之大本而復明以君子之時
中與智愚賢不肖之失中而徵之費隱極之天
人其於堯舜執中精一之旨有所發明宜其與
典謨並傳也嘗統論之堯舜者繼天立極之聖
也得禹湯文武而其道行孔子者繼往開來之
聖也得顏曾思孟而其道明秦漢而下治統道
===
統不能合一世道升降之機則然耳嗚呼古今
一天也萬世而下有堯舜者出焉舉而措之則
堯舜繼天立極之功雖謂之至今存焉可也
表
擬宋輯尚書所載事作敬天圖成輔臣賀
表乾道七年
周汝礪
同考試官教諭楊　批〔駢麗中有典則得宋〕
表體非但工於四六而已錄之
punctuated:
門弟子，一貫以傳曾子，是堯之中也；傳約以示顏子，是舜之精一也。而子思復以所受於曾子者，作爲《中庸》一書，首言天命之性，以見大道之原；繼言中爲天下之大本，而復明以君子之時中與智愚賢不肖之失中，而徵之費隱，極之天人。其於堯舜執中精一之旨有所發明，宜其與典謨並傳也。嘗統論之：堯舜者，繼天立極之聖也，得禹湯文武而其道行；孔子者，繼往開來之聖也，得顏曾思孟而其道明。秦漢而下，治統道統不能合一，世道升降之機則然耳。嗚呼！古今一天也，萬世而下，有堯舜者出焉，舉而措之，則堯舜繼天立極之功，雖謂之至今存焉，可也。
表
擬宋輯《尚書》所載事，作《敬天圖》成，輔臣賀表。乾道七年。
周汝礪
同考試官教諭楊　批〔駢麗中有典則，得宋〕表體，非但工於四六而已，錄之。
translation_en:
…to his disciples. The single thread that he transmitted to Zengzi was Yao’s centrality; the essentials he conveyed to Yanzi were Shun’s refinement and singleness of mind. Zisi, in turn, drew upon what he had received from Zengzi to compose the Doctrine of the Mean. He began by discussing the nature conferred by Heaven’s mandate, thereby revealing the source of the Great Way. He next explained that centrality is the great foundation of all under Heaven, further illuminating it through the gentleman’s accordance with the mean as circumstances require and the departures from it of the wise and foolish, the worthy and unworthy. He demonstrated it through the Way’s pervasive manifestations and hidden subtlety, and pursued it to its ultimate reach in Heaven and humanity. His elucidation of what Yao and Shun meant by holding fast to the mean and maintaining refinement and singleness of mind makes it fitting that his work should be transmitted alongside the Canons and Counsels of the Book of Documents.
Considered together, Yao and Shun were sages who carried on Heaven’s work and established the supreme standard. With Yu, Tang, Wen, and Wu, their Way was put into practice. Kongzi was the sage who continued the past and opened the way for the future. With Yanzi, Zengzi, Zisi, and Mengzi, his Way was made clear. From the Qin and Han onward, the succession of governance and the transmission of the Way could no longer be united: such was the underlying dynamic of the rise and decline of the world’s moral order. Alas! Heaven is the same in antiquity and today. If, ten thousand generations hence, someone like Yao or Shun should arise and put this into practice, then one could indeed say that Yao and Shun’s achievement in carrying on Heaven’s work and establishing the supreme standard endures to this day.
Memorial
Compose a memorial of congratulation in the voice of the Song chief councillors upon completion of the Illustrations of Revering Heaven, compiled from events recorded in the Book of Documents. Seventh year of Qiandao [1171].
By Zhou Ruli.
Comment by Associate Examiner Yang, Instructor: “Amid its elegant parallel prose there is classical propriety; it captures the style of Song memorials. It is more than merely accomplished four-and-six prose. Include it.”

title: 隆慶元年應天府鄉試錄
text:
同考試官推官沈　批〔通篇不離尚書發明人君敬天之道殆盡且句法蒼古不徒以組織〕
〔爲工而規度自在宜式多士〕
考試官左中允孫　批〔頌中有規表體之正者〕
考試官左諭德王　批〔詞典則而旨微婉可以式〕
矣
乾道七年月日具官臣虞允文等恭遇
御製以偶觀無逸一篇有得因取尚書所載敬
天事輯爲兩圖朝夕省覽
===
名曰敬天圖者
皇穹眷命
一人體龍德之純
聖敬傳心
五位覲鴻圖之赫作範遠稽乎墳典成象上契
於高明精萃瑾綸光生
黼座臣等誠懽誠忭稽首頓首竊以惟乾稱
父寵綏必篤於大君惟辟奉天祇敬宜嚴
於宗子欽明啓運在精一以執中文命承
punctuated:
同考試官推官沈批〔通篇不離尚書，發明人君敬天之道殆盡，且句法蒼古，不徒以組織〕〔爲工，而規度自在，宜式多士。〕
考試官左中允孫批〔頌中有規，表體之正者。〕
考試官左諭德王批〔詞典則而旨微婉，可以式〕矣。
乾道七年月日，具官臣虞允文等，恭遇御製以偶觀無逸一篇有得，因取尚書所載敬天事，輯爲兩圖，朝夕省覽，名曰敬天圖者。
皇穹眷命，一人體龍德之純；聖敬傳心，五位覲鴻圖之赫。作範遠稽乎墳典，成象上契於高明。精萃瑾綸，光生黼座。臣等誠懽誠忭，稽首頓首。竊以惟乾稱父，寵綏必篤於大君；惟辟奉天，祇敬宜嚴於宗子。欽明啓運，在精一以執中；文命承
translation_en:
Associate Examiner Shen, Prefectural Judge, comments: 〔The entire piece remains grounded in the Book of Documents and elucidates almost exhaustively the ruler’s way of revering Heaven. Its phrasing is vigorous and antique; its skill lies not merely in verbal arrangement〕〔but also in its assured command of form. It should serve as a model for the many scholars.〕
Examiner Sun, Left Companion to the Heir Apparent, comments: 〔Admonition is present within the praise: this is the proper form of a memorial.〕
Examiner Wang, Left Admonisher to the Heir Apparent, comments: 〔Its language accords with classical standards, and its meaning is subtle and tactful. It may serve as a model〕 indeed.
On a certain day and month in the seventh year of Qiandao, your servants Yu Yunwen and others, holding their respective offices, respectfully commemorate Your Majesty’s imperial composition: having chanced to read the chapter “Against Luxurious Ease” and gained insight from it, you gathered the instances of reverence for Heaven recorded in the Book of Documents and compiled them into two charts for examination morning and evening, naming them “Charts of Reverence for Heaven.”
August Heaven has bestowed its favor and mandate; the One Man embodies the purity of dragon-like virtue. Sagely reverence transmits the inner teaching; those of the five ranks behold the splendor of the magnificent charts. In establishing a model, you consult the ancient canonical writings; in giving it visible form, you accord above with Heaven’s lofty brightness. Their essence is gathered in precious imperial utterances [?], and radiance shines upon the embroidered throne. We, your servants, are truly joyful and truly delighted; we bow our heads to the ground and repeatedly kowtow.
We humbly consider that Qian, Heaven, is called the father: its favor and protection must be bestowed abundantly upon the great sovereign. The ruler serves Heaven: reverent devotion should be most exacting in its principal heir. Reverence and enlightenment inaugurated the age; through refinement and singleness of purpose, the mean was upheld. Wenming [Yu] received …

title: 隆慶元年應天府鄉試錄
text:
休惟幾康而猶直六事救桑林之旱顧諟
斯存七日弭祥穀之災荒寧是懼自我聰
明自我明畏鑒觀常切於下民及爾游衍
及爾出王陟降如臨於上帝理非茫渺本
先天而不違書有明徵俟後聖而無惑淳
風既遠實德寖微玩人時以不修跡三正
五行之軌忽天戒而弗謹乖兩儀四氣之
和間有所爲而爲寔非所敬而敬郊丘有
常祀胡爲東禪西封昊極無加隆奚取稱
名進號天不容僞人亦誰欺命緣是以靡
常時於今而有待茲蓋伏遇
===
則天立極
主敬存神
履位思危纘
心源於
藝祖遇災知懼勤
手札於臣工
punctuated: 休，惟幾康而猶直。六事救桑林之旱，顧諟斯存；七日弭祥穀之災，荒寧是懼。自我聰明，自我明畏，鑒觀常切於下民；及爾游衍，及爾出王，陟降如臨於上帝。理非茫渺，本先天而不違；書有明徵，俟後聖而無惑。淳風既遠，實德寖微，玩人時以不修，跡三正五行之軌；忽天戒而弗謹，乖兩儀四氣之和。間有所爲而爲，寔非所敬而敬。郊丘有常祀，胡爲東禪西封？昊極無加隆，奚取稱名進號？天不容僞，人亦誰欺？命緣是以靡常，時於今而有待。茲蓋伏遇則天立極，主敬存神，履位思危，纘心源於藝祖；遇災知懼，勤手札於臣工。
translation_en:
…blessings, attending to the slightest beginnings, bringing well-being, and keeping deliberations upright. By examining six matters, Tang relieved the drought at Sanglin, ever keeping that heavenly mandate before his eyes. Within seven days, the calamity of the portentous grain [?] was dispelled, through fear of indolence and ease. Heaven’s hearing and sight derive from ours; its manifest awe derives from ours: its scrutiny is ever closely directed toward the people below. Whether you wander at leisure or go forth, in ascending and descending you stand as though in the presence of the Lord on High. This principle is neither vague nor remote: even when preceding Heaven, it does not run counter to Heaven. The writings provide clear testimony, awaiting later sages without occasion for doubt.

Once the age of unspoiled customs had receded, genuine virtue gradually diminished. Men neglected the seasons governing human affairs and failed to cultivate themselves, merely following the patterns of the three calendrical beginnings and the Five Phases. They disregarded Heaven’s warnings and failed to exercise care, disrupting the harmony of the two cosmic powers and the energies of the four seasons. Occasionally they acted merely for the sake of acting; truly, their reverence was not directed toward what deserved reverence. There were established sacrifices at the suburban altar and the round mound: why perform shan rites here and feng rites there? Supreme Heaven’s exalted status admits of no increase: what purpose was served by proclaiming names and presenting honorific titles? Heaven tolerates no falsehood; whom among men could they deceive? Thus the mandate became inconstant, and the age awaited the present moment.

Now, prostrate, we have the good fortune to encounter Your Majesty, who models himself on Heaven and establishes the supreme standard, makes reverence his guiding principle and preserves spiritual awareness. Occupying the throne, you remain mindful of peril, continuing the founding ancestor’s innermost principles. Encountering calamities, you know fear and diligently send handwritten instructions to your officials.

title: 隆慶元年應天府鄉試錄
text:
重道崇儒咨訪特隆平畫接
研經玩史誦習每至於夜分謂載籍記言記
事以來惟尚書大經大法具在若稽古堯
若稽古舜仰帝德之克明鑒於有夏鑒於
有殷謹天命之自度頊緣
覽觀獨得悟周公無逸之篇用是
采輯全書萃列聖敬天之旨彙成一帙猶思
披閱之煩爰
製兩圖庶取對矚之便列在
===
左右揭日月于丹青擬諸形容呈圖書於河
洛彌文匪尚事實悉陳自授曆明時及春
夏秋冬〻四仲之用本察機觀象兼日月星
辰七政之宜賴平治於功成時水時旱之
著其故占庥嘉於類應好風好雨之示其
徵迺若有典有禮有服有刑表欽崇之實
政罔敢于遊于田于觀于逸存儆戒之微
言持此臨兆民凜凜如馭朽索推之警庶
位慄慄若隕深淵蓋古今一天尚論虞夏
punctuated: 重道崇儒，咨訪特隆平畫接，研經玩史，誦習每至於夜分。謂載籍記言記事以來，惟《尚書》大經大法具在。「若稽古堯」「若稽古舜」，仰帝德之克明；「鑒於有夏」「鑒於有殷」，謹天命之自度。頊緣覽觀獨得，悟周公《無逸》之篇，用是采輯全書，萃列聖敬天之旨，彙成一帙。猶思披閱之煩，爰製兩圖，庶取對矚之便，列在左右。揭日月于丹青，擬諸形容；呈圖書於河洛，彌文匪尚，事實悉陳。自授曆明時，及春夏秋冬〻四仲之用，本察機觀象，兼日月星辰七政之宜。賴平治於功成，時水時旱之著其故；占庥嘉於類應，好風好雨之示其徵。迺若有典、有禮、有服、有刑，表欽崇之實政；罔敢于遊、于田、于觀、于逸，存儆戒之微言。持此臨兆民，凜凜如馭朽索；推之警庶位，慄慄若隕深淵。蓋古今一天，尚論虞夏
translation_en:
…You honor the Way and exalt Confucian learning, showing particular regard for consultation and inquiry in your daytime audiences [?]. You study the classics and ponder the histories, often reading and reciting until midnight. You consider that, among all the works recording words and deeds, the Book of Documents alone contains the great guiding principles and laws in their entirety. In “examining antiquity concerning Yao” and “examining antiquity concerning Shun,” you revere the sovereigns’ capacity to make their virtue manifest; in “taking warning from Xia” and “taking warning from Yin,” you carefully assess yourself against Heaven’s mandate. Through your reading [?], you gained a distinctive insight and comprehended the Duke of Zhou’s chapter “Against Idleness.” Accordingly, you compiled material from the whole book, gathering the successive sage rulers’ teachings on revering Heaven into a single volume. Still mindful of the trouble of leafing through it, you then produced two diagrams, so that they could conveniently be viewed directly, placing them to your left and right.

You display the sun and moon in painted colors, representing their forms, and present charts and writings like those revealed in the He and Luo rivers. Elaborate ornament is not prized; actual matters are fully set forth. From issuing the calendar and clarifying the seasons to the functions of the four mid-season months of spring, summer, autumn, and winter [?], everything is grounded in examining the celestial mechanism and observing celestial phenomena, encompassing the proper ordering of the seven celestial regulators—the sun, moon, and five planets. Peace and good order depend upon the successful accomplishment of these tasks; the occurrence of floods or droughts at particular times reveals their causes. Auspicious blessings are discerned through correspondences between things of the same kind; preferences for wind or rain reveal their signs.

As for the established statutes, rites, vestments, and punishments, these demonstrate concrete measures of reverent government. “Not daring to indulge in excursions, hunting, sightseeing, or ease” preserves subtle words of warning and admonition. Holding to these principles as you govern the countless people, you are as apprehensive as one driving with rotten reins; extending them to admonish all officials, you are as fearful as one about to plunge into a deep abyss. For Heaven is one and the same in antiquity and today; looking back and discussing the ages of Yu and Xia …

title: 隆慶元年應天府鄉試錄
text:
商周之世而帝王合敬會通典謨訓誥之
文寓於目即契於心按諸圖如指諸掌豈
曰人道邇天道遠質之無形而不能名寔
則作之聖述之明儼乎有儀而可爲像也
臣等職叨丞弼愧啓沃之未能誼切臣鄰
視贊襄乎何補由觀今之圖以觀古見千
載於羹墻體敬天之
意以敬
君合羣情于怙冒敢不修其可願一念期與天
知慎乃攸司九德其熈
帝載伏願
惟敬作所
能自得師
事天以實不以文法古在心不在迹
思曰睿睿作聖無怠無荒
慮以動動惟時其難其慎納誨常資于朝夕
典學罔間於始終
治享垂衣尤履思艱圖易之念
punctuated:
商周之世，而帝王合敬，會通典謨訓誥之文，寓於目即契於心，按諸圖如指諸掌。豈曰人道邇、天道遠，質之無形而不能名？寔則作之聖、述之明，儼乎有儀而可爲像也。
臣等職叨丞弼，愧啓沃之未能；誼切臣鄰，視贊襄乎何補？由觀今之圖以觀古，見千載於羹墻；體敬天之意以敬君，合羣情于怙冒。敢不修其可願，一念期與天知；慎乃攸司，九德其熈帝載。
伏願惟敬作所，能自得師；事天以實不以文，法古在心不在迹。思曰睿，睿作聖，無怠無荒；慮以動，動惟時，其難其慎。納誨常資于朝夕，典學罔間於始終。治享垂衣，尤履思艱圖易之念，
translation_en:
…the ages of Shang and Zhou: emperors and kings were united in reverence. Bringing together the writings of the Canons, Counsels, Instructions, and Announcements, these illustrations present to the eye what immediately accords with the heart; consulting them makes matters as clear as pointing to one’s own palm. How could one say that the human Way is near but Heaven’s Way distant, that it is formless when examined and cannot be named? Indeed, the sage wisdom of those who originated these teachings and the illumination of those who transmitted them stand solemnly embodied in exemplary forms that can be depicted.
We, your servants, undeservedly occupy offices as your chief assistants, ashamed that we have been unable to enlighten and enrich your understanding. Bound closely to you by our duty as ministers, what contribution have we made to assisting your rule? Looking through the present illustrations to antiquity, we behold a thousand years before us, as though seeing the ancient worthies in our soup and upon our walls. Embodying the intention of revering Heaven, we revere our sovereign; the feelings of all are united in looking to your protection and shelter. How could we dare not cultivate what is worthy of aspiration, hoping that Heaven will know our every thought, and attend carefully to our assigned responsibilities, so that the nine virtues may illuminate Heaven’s work?
We humbly hope that you will make reverence your abiding place and find teachers for yourself; serve Heaven through substance rather than ornament, and emulate antiquity in spirit rather than in outward traces. Thought brings discernment, and discernment makes the sage: be neither indolent nor neglectful. Deliberate before acting, and act at the proper time: approach this with a sense of its difficulty and with caution. Constantly draw upon admonition, morning and evening; let your steadfast study remain uninterrupted from beginning to end. While enjoying the effortless rule symbolized by letting your robes hang down, all the more maintain [?] the resolve to ponder difficulties and address them while they are still easy…

title: 隆慶元年應天府鄉試錄
text:
功收舞羽益宣有備無患之猷則
帝驟王馳備箕疇之歛福而
天長地久過周曆之卜年臣等無任瞻
天仰
聖激切屏營之至謹奉
表稱
賀以
聞
第叅場
策五道
===
第一問
唐鶴徵
同考試官教授梁 批 〔惟〕
高皇
文皇勤政務學遠追帝王之懿範我
皇上嗣統紹休覲揚光烈非淺學所能仰窺萬一此作鋪張揄揚鏗
鏘金石蓋豪傑士也
同考試官教授趙 批 三代以下治法心學
punctuated:
功收舞羽，益宣有備無患之猷，則帝驟王馳，備箕疇之歛福，而天長地久，過周曆之卜年。臣等無任瞻天仰聖、激切屏營之至，謹奉表稱賀以聞。

第叅場
策五道

第一問
唐鶴徵

同考試官教授梁批：〔惟〕高皇、文皇勤政務學，遠追帝王之懿範。我皇上嗣統紹休，覲揚光烈，非淺學所能仰窺萬一。此作鋪張揄揚，鏗鏘金石，蓋豪傑士也。

同考試官教授趙批：三代以下，治法心學
translation_en:
…With pacification achieved through the dance of feathered standards, may you further proclaim the policy of preparedness that averts calamity. Then, advancing swiftly along the way of emperors and kings, may you gather blessings in their fullness according to the categories of Jizi’s Great Plan; may your reign endure as long as Heaven and Earth, exceeding the years divined for the Zhou dynasty. We, your servants, look up to Heaven and revere Your Majesty with the utmost fervor and trembling awe. We respectfully submit this memorial of congratulation for your imperial hearing.

Third Session
Five Policy Questions

First Question
Tang Hezheng

Comment by Associate Examiner Liang, Prefectural School Professor: 〔Reflecting that〕 Emperor Gao and Emperor Wen attended diligently to government and devoted themselves to learning, emulating the admirable models of the emperors and kings of antiquity. Our reigning emperor has succeeded to the imperial line and continued its excellence, manifesting and exalting their glorious achievements. Those of shallow learning cannot glimpse even one ten-thousandth of this. This essay expansively celebrates these achievements, ringing out like bronze bells and stone chimes. Its author is indeed a man of exceptional talent.

Comment by Associate Examiner Zhao, Prefectural School Professor: Since the Three Dynasties, in methods of governance and the learning of the mind…

title: 隆慶元年應天府鄉試錄
text:
嬔美帝王未有如我
二祖者
皇上嗣承大統勤政務學與
二祖同心此策能揄揚其盛未復有惓惓忠懇之懐焉録以登
獻豈但爲文也耶
同考試官知州陳　批　我
二祖勤政務學與帝王同符而正心爲本
皇上嗣承大統政學又與
二祖同符此策獨能揄揚而贊翊之其識遠其志忠矣宜録以
獻
===
考試官左中允孫　批　〔凡我臣子恭遇〕
聖皇嗣統勵治之初勤於政學遠邁百王近符
二祖均切仰戴子備極揄揚未復進正心之論可謂頌而無諂矣
考試官左諭德王　批　我
皇上勤政務學法乎
二祖此作能揄揚之而未所敷陳尤見忠悃是不負所學者
政者其帝王治天下之具乎學者其帝王
出治之本乎夫天下亦大矣四海之廣兆
punctuated:
嬔美帝王，未有如我二祖者。皇上嗣承大統，勤政務學，與二祖同心。此策能揄揚其盛，未復有惓惓忠懇之懐焉，録以登獻，豈但爲文也耶？

同考試官知州陳，批：我二祖勤政務學，與帝王同符，而正心爲本。皇上嗣承大統，政學又與二祖同符。此策獨能揄揚而贊翊之，其識遠，其志忠矣，宜録以獻。

考試官左中允孫，批：〔凡我臣子恭遇〕聖皇嗣統勵治之初，勤於政學，遠邁百王，近符二祖，均切仰戴。子備極揄揚，未復進正心之論，可謂頌而無諂矣。

考試官左諭德王，批：我皇上勤政務學，法乎二祖。此作能揄揚之，而未所敷陳，尤見忠悃，是不負所學者。

政者，其帝王治天下之具乎？學者，其帝王出治之本乎？夫天下亦大矣，四海之廣，兆
translation_en:
…in rivaling the excellence of the ancient emperors and kings [?], none have equaled our Two Founders. His Majesty has succeeded to the great imperial succession; diligent in government and devoted to learning, he shares the purposes of the Two Founders. This policy essay extols that splendor and, toward its close [?], also expresses devoted loyalty and earnest sincerity. It is selected for presentation to the throne: surely this is more than mere literary composition!

Associate Examiner Chen, Department Magistrate, comments: Our Two Founders were diligent in government and devoted to learning, matching the ancient emperors and kings, and made rectifying the mind their foundation. His Majesty has succeeded to the great imperial succession, and his government and learning likewise accord with those of the Two Founders. This policy essay is outstanding in its ability to extol and support these endeavors. Its insight is far-reaching and its intent loyal. It should be selected for presentation to the throne.

Examiner Sun, Left Rectifier, comments: 〔All of us, His servants, respectfully encounter〕 the beginning of our sagely emperor’s reign, when he strives for good government. Diligent in government and learning, he far surpasses the hundred kings of antiquity and closely accords with our Two Founders. We all look up to him with heartfelt allegiance. You have praised him to the fullest and, toward the close [?], further advanced an argument for rectifying the mind. This may be called praise without flattery.

Examiner Wang, Left Admonisher, comments: Our emperor is diligent in government and devoted to learning, taking the Two Founders as his models. This composition succeeds in extolling him, while what it sets forth at the end [?] especially reveals loyal sincerity. Here is someone who has lived up to his learning.

Is government not the instrument by which emperors and kings govern All-under-Heaven? Is learning not the foundation from which emperors and kings bring forth good government? All-under-Heaven is indeed vast: the breadth of the Four Seas, the countless…

title: 隆慶元年應天府鄉試錄
text:
民之衆咸求治於人君之一身使非政以
運之何以兼統而無外天下之政亦大矣
萬幾之裁庶務之理咸取足於人君之一
心使非學以主之何以會應而不窮故齊
衆軌物政之會經也非學無以裕其基崇
志廣業學之懿則也非政無以達其用是
二者固相須也而皆管攝于一心心也者
又政之樞紐而學之本原也知乎此可以
論古帝王之政之學而我
===
二祖之所以匹休帝王與
皇上之作求世德以光揚于
