Thus Duke Xuan once said: “Above, I do not fail the Son of Heaven; below, I do not betray what I have learned. I care nothing for anything else.” Wenzheng likewise said: “As for what I myself undertake, this is how I ought to act. Whether it succeeds or not depends on things beyond my control; even sages and worthies cannot guarantee it.” This is the spirit of Zhuge, Marquis Wu, who did not calculate success or failure, advantage or adversity. The Way of these two gentlemen was luminous and outstanding: from this we may discern its greatness. Yet I, your humble student, have something further to say. Talent is endowed by Heaven; only through its development and enlargement can what one brings to bear become great. Integrity is established by human effort; only through its nurture and cultivation can the responsibilities one shoulders become vast. This is what is meant by sincerity joining with talent. Thus, in contemplating the greatness of these two gentlemen, we must also probe deeply into its foundations. Ouyang Yongshu said that Duke Xuan’s words were rooted in benevolence and righteousness; Lü Benzhong said…

title: 隆慶元年應天府鄉試錄
text:
大正之學本於忠孝夫仁義忠孝之道通
極於性命而置之可以塞乎天地根柢於
綱常而施之可以貫乎金石是則二公之
所存也彼徒負豪傑之才而不本聖賢之
學者或激於意氣之偏而不得其正或墮
於功利之私而不底於純其視二公之作
為何啻霄壤也耶愚生幸生二公之鄉景
行先哲而誦其遺言竊有志於當時之務
久矣然曰以天下自任則非所敢承也謹
===
述二公之槩以為明問復而士之尚志亦
因以自見云
第五問
周汝礪
同考試官教諭楊批更化安民乃圖治首
務此作能以獨得之見裁酌時政鑿鑿可行且
滾滾數千餘言悉秦漢人語足占博雅之學經
濟之才矣宜錄之以傳不朽云
同考試官推官沈批談時務者類多剿襲
alt_text:
□正之學本於忠孝夫仁義忠孝之道通
極於性命而置之可以塞乎天地根柢於
綱常而施之可以貫乎金石是則二公之
所存也彼徒負豪傑之才而不本聖賢之
學者或激於意氣之偏而不得其正或墮
於功利之私而不底於純其視二公之作
爲何啻霄壤也耶愚生幸生二公之鄉景
行先哲而誦其遺言竊有志於當時之務
久矣然曰以天下自任則非所敢承也謹
===
述二公之槩以爲明問復而士之尚志亦
因以自見云
第五問
劉汝弼
同考試官教諭楊 批〔要化民成俗圖治首務此作能以獨得之見裁酌時政藻鑑可行且〕
〔滾滾數千餘言悉秦漢人語足占博雅之學經濟之才矣宜録之以傳不朽云〕
同考試官推官沈 批〔談時務者類多剿襲〕
punctuated:
大正之學本於忠孝。夫仁義忠孝之道，通極於性命，而置之可以塞乎天地；根柢於綱常，而施之可以貫乎金石。是則二公之所存也。彼徒負豪傑之才而不本聖賢之學者，或激於意氣之偏而不得其正，或墮於功利之私而不底於純，其視二公之作為，何啻霄壤也耶！愚生幸生二公之鄉，景行先哲而誦其遺言，竊有志於當時之務久矣。然曰以天下自任，則非所敢承也。謹述二公之槩，以為明問復，而士之尚志亦因以自見云。
第五問
周汝礪
同考試官教諭楊批：更化安民，乃圖治首務。此作能以獨得之見，裁酌時政，鑿鑿可行；且滾滾數千餘言，悉秦漢人語，足占博雅之學、經濟之才矣。宜錄之以傳不朽云。
同考試官推官沈批：談時務者，類多剿襲
translation_en:
…Dazheng’s learning was rooted in loyalty and filial piety. The Way of benevolence, righteousness, loyalty, and filial piety reaches to the utmost depths of human nature and Heaven’s mandate; established, it can fill Heaven and Earth. It is rooted in the cardinal bonds and constant virtues; put into practice, it can penetrate metal and stone. This, then, was what the two gentlemen cherished within. Those who possess merely the talents of outstanding men, without grounding themselves in the learning of sages and worthies, may be driven by one-sided impulses and fail to attain rectitude, or fall into selfish pursuits of achievement and gain and fail to attain purity. Compared with the deeds of these two gentlemen, theirs are more than Heaven and Earth apart! I, an unworthy student, was fortunate to be born in their native region. Admiring these earlier worthies and reciting the words they left behind, I have long privately aspired to address the affairs of my time. Yet I would not dare claim to take responsibility for All-under-Heaven upon myself. I have respectfully outlined the lives of these two gentlemen in reply to your discerning question, thereby also revealing the aspirations that a scholar esteems.
Fifth Question
Zhou Ruli
Comment by Associate Examiner Yang, Instructor: Reforming government and bringing peace to the people are the foremost tasks in seeking good order. With insights independently attained, this essay weighs current government affairs and offers proposals that are demonstrably practicable. Moreover, its several thousand words flow forth entirely in the language of Qin and Han writers, sufficient evidence of broad and refined learning and talent for statecraft. It deserves to be recorded and transmitted to posterity.
Comment by Associate Examiner Shen, Prefectural Judge: Those who discuss current affairs mostly plagiarize…

title: 隆慶元年應天府鄉試錄
text:
陳言無裨實用此策獨能敷陳閭閻疾痛
廊廟隱憂筆端如畫而長慮卓識直與董賈相伯仲蓋識通達國
體者謂爲俊傑非耶是用錄之俟
當宁采焉
考試官左中允孫　批〔書生能言民間利病詳且實而惓惓匡時之抱吐之衷懷非徒工於文者〕
考試官左諭德王　批〔以史漢語而談當世務眞有痛哭流涕長太息之意子其今之賈生耶〕
愚竊聞更化者莫病於重懲乎既往而不
===
慮其遺後來之患安民者莫病於過與以
厚望而不察其藏不測之憂夫所語更化
者何也傳曰更化善治譬諸琴瑟不調必
解而更張之蓋法未有歲久不弊者一旦
掃除其舊而與之以新天下之民延頸望
治何其幸也顧前人之法不皆不善而今
之法未有甚過於前舊弊未袪新患叢生
令有所不行民無時休息譬諸調琴瑟者
鼓之成聲可使人聽而亟乏筆髀雜進竝
punctuated:
陳言，無裨實用。此策獨能敷陳閭閻疾痛、廊廟隱憂，筆端如畫，而長慮卓識，直與董賈相伯仲。蓋識通達國體者謂爲俊傑，非耶？是用錄之，俟當宁采焉。
考試官左中允孫批〔書生能言民間利病，詳且實，而惓惓匡時之抱，吐之衷懷，非徒工於文者。〕
考試官左諭德王批〔以史漢語而談當世務，眞有痛哭流涕長太息之意。子其今之賈生耶？〕
愚竊聞，更化者莫病於重懲乎既往，而不慮其遺後來之患；安民者莫病於過與以厚望，而不察其藏不測之憂。夫所語更化者何也？傳曰：「更化善治，譬諸琴瑟不調，必解而更張之。」蓋法未有歲久不弊者，一旦掃除其舊而與之以新，天下之民延頸望治，何其幸也！顧前人之法不皆不善，而今之法未有甚過於前。舊弊未袪，新患叢生，令有所不行，民無時休息。譬諸調琴瑟者，鼓之成聲，可使人聽，而亟乏筆髀雜進竝
translation_en:
…stale sayings, of no practical benefit. This policy essay alone sets forth the sufferings of ordinary households and the hidden anxieties of the court, depicting them vividly with the brush. Its far-reaching deliberations and outstanding discernment put it on a level with Dong Zhongshu and Jia Yi. Surely those whose understanding comprehends the essentials of governing the state are called outstanding talents? Accordingly, we record it here, awaiting its adoption by His Majesty.
Examiner Sun, Left Mentor, comments: 〔This scholar can discuss the benefits and hardships affecting the common people in detail and with accuracy. His earnest desire to set the times right pours forth from his heart; he is more than merely an accomplished writer.〕
Examiner Wang, Left Admonisher, comments: 〔He discusses contemporary affairs in the language of the Records of the Grand Historian and the History of the Han, truly conveying the feeling of bitter weeping, flowing tears, and long sighs. Are you perhaps the Jia Yi of our day?〕
I humbly understand that, in reforming government, nothing is more harmful than reacting too severely against past failings without considering the troubles thereby bequeathed to the future; in bringing peace to the people, nothing is more harmful than encouraging excessive expectations without examining the unforeseen troubles concealed within. What, then, is meant by reforming government? A transmitted text says: “Reform brings good government. It is like zithers out of tune: their strings must be loosened and strung anew.” No laws remain free of defects after many years. If their old arrangements are swept away at a stroke and replaced with new ones, the people throughout the realm crane their necks in expectation of good government. How fortunate they are! Yet the laws of our predecessors were not all bad, and present laws have not greatly surpassed the earlier ones. Old abuses have yet to be removed, while new troubles spring up in profusion. Some orders cannot be implemented, and the people have no respite. It is like tuning zithers: when plucked, they produce sounds that people can listen to; yet “ji fa bi bi” [?] enter in confusion and together…

title: 隆慶元年應天府鄉試錄
text:
奏則聽之者不知其爲美而且惑矣夫琴
瑟以易人之聽乃致人之惑法制以令人
之喜乃失人之望此其患甚切而其憂益
以長不可不察也且今天下號極治矣
天子仁儉性成今聞方昭公卿大夫百執事布
列在位陳謨獻計者畢智之士也採議集
事者竭忠之臣也愚生伏在南陬無所聽
睹乃亦竊有聞方其
詔令初下鄉人父老扶杖往聽感極而涕何
===
異漢詔之下山東唐令之下河朔也思慕
德化幸見今日莫不說喜何啻恒饑之子
之食大旱之needed之雨也乃後則日異矣又
後則月異矣夫人之情望之過而實不至
則怨生焉今脐之民未怨也其勢則然耳
愚生之見以爲安民莫如恒事吏化莫如
救患今天下民貧矣饑寒切身十人而九
流亡轉徙十地而五疾痛號苦之狀啼號
之聲不可聞且見也往者賦斂無時費出
punctuated:
奏，則聽之者不知其爲美，而且惑矣。夫琴瑟以易人之聽，乃致人之惑；法制以令人之喜，乃失人之望。此其患甚切，而其憂益以長，不可不察也。
且今天下號極治矣。天子仁儉性成，今聞方昭。公卿大夫百執事布列在位，陳謨獻計者，畢智之士也；採議集事者，竭忠之臣也。愚生伏在南陬，無所聽睹，乃亦竊有聞。方其詔令初下，鄉人父老扶杖往聽，感極而涕，何異漢詔之下山東、唐令之下河朔也？思慕德化，幸見今日，莫不說喜，何啻恒饑之子之食、大旱之needed之雨也！乃後則日異矣，又後則月異矣。夫人之情，望之過而實不至，則怨生焉。今脐之民未怨也，其勢則然耳。
愚生之見，以爲安民莫如恒事，吏化莫如救患。今天下民貧矣，饑寒切身，十人而九；流亡轉徙，十地而五。疾痛號苦之狀、啼號之聲，不可聞且見也。往者賦斂無時，費出
translation_en:
…when played together, listeners cannot appreciate their beauty and are instead bewildered. The qin and se zithers are meant to please the ear, yet they cause bewilderment; laws and institutions are meant to delight the people, yet they disappoint their hopes. The harm is most pressing, and the anxiety it brings grows ever more enduring. This must be examined.
Moreover, the realm today is said to enjoy consummate order. The Son of Heaven is benevolent and frugal by nature, and his reputation now shines forth [?]. Dukes, ministers, grandees, and the many officeholders stand arrayed in their posts. Those who present plans and offer counsel are men who devote all their wisdom; those who weigh proposals and accomplish affairs are ministers who exhaust their loyalty. I, an ignorant student dwelling in a remote southern corner, have little opportunity to hear or see affairs, yet even I have heard something of them. When the imperial edicts first came down, the village elders went, leaning on their staffs, to hear them and were moved to tears. How was this different from Han edicts reaching Shandong or Tang commands reaching Heshuo? Longing for transformation through virtue and fortunate enough to witness this day, all rejoiced. Their delight was no less than that of someone perpetually hungry receiving food, or of rain during a great drought [?]. Yet afterward things changed by the day, and later still they changed by the month. It is human nature that when expectations are excessive and reality falls short, resentment arises. The people today [?] have not yet become resentful, but circumstances tend in that direction.
In my humble view, nothing settles the people better than constancy in affairs, and nothing transforms the officials [?] better than remedying distress. Today the people of the realm are impoverished: nine in ten suffer hunger and cold directly; in five places out of ten, people flee and wander. The sight of their suffering and cries of anguish, and the sound of their wailing, are unbearable to hear or witness. Formerly, taxes and levies were imposed at irregular times, and expenditures…

title: 隆慶元年應天府鄉試錄
text:
不經奉行恐後士大夫抵隙而遊談者以
爲非盡有司之過乃今則誰使之然也
詔許內供之費減矣而浸漁之弊數倍也
詔許加派之令止矣而科擾之弊滋甚也江
南財賦之窟久困徵輸江北河流之衝積
苦氾濫日望官吏嗸嗸待哺未之至也一
旦司農告匱持斧之使四出遠邇小民聞
者聳然嚙指而相視曰此何以爲也夫撫
之則親親則安感之則懾懾則感小民之
===
常度也即督責通晉諸路分部盡使職矣
如必假之以權則天下之使在外秉憲者
豈少耶官衆則出令者多權分則任事者
鮮州郡趨承昏夜靡遑坊里供具膏血盡
竭傳曰鳥窮則啄獸窮則攫馬窮則佚此
喜喻也故民不可擾也民擾則不寧居不
寧居則失其故業漢文帝時最號富庶乃
進言者曰方今之務莫若使民務農而已
夫農者天下之本也粢盛之所出財用之
punctuated: 不經，奉行恐後。士大夫抵隙而遊談者，以爲非盡有司之過。乃今則誰使之然也？詔許內供之費減矣，而浸漁之弊數倍也；詔許加派之令止矣，而科擾之弊滋甚也。江南財賦之窟，久困徵輸；江北河流之衝，積苦氾濫。日望官吏，嗸嗸待哺，未之至也。一旦司農告匱，持斧之使四出，遠邇小民聞者聳然，嚙指而相視曰：「此何以爲也？」夫撫之則親，親則安；感之則懾，懾則感，小民之常度也。即督責通晉諸路，分部盡使職矣，如必假之以權，則天下之使在外秉憲者豈少耶？官衆則出令者多，權分則任事者鮮。州郡趨承，昏夜靡遑；坊里供具，膏血盡竭。傳曰：「鳥窮則啄，獸窮則攫，馬窮則佚。」此喜喻也。故民不可擾也。民擾則不寧居，不寧居則失其故業。漢文帝時，最號富庶，乃進言者曰：「方今之務，莫若使民務農而已。」夫農者，天下之本也，粢盛之所出，財用之
translation_en:
…expenditure was unregulated, and those carrying out the orders feared falling behind. Scholar-officials who seized upon openings to offer idle arguments maintained that the fault did not lie entirely with the responsible authorities. But now, who has brought matters to this pass? An imperial edict authorized a reduction in expenditure for supplies to the inner court, yet the abuses of encroachment and extortion have multiplied severalfold. An imperial edict authorized an end to orders for supplementary levies, yet the abuses of exaction and harassment have grown still worse. Jiangnan, the great storehouse of fiscal wealth, has long been exhausted by levies and deliveries; Jiangbei, exposed to the force of the rivers, has suffered repeated flooding. Day after day the people look to the officials, crying out for sustenance, but relief has yet to arrive. Then, suddenly, the fiscal authorities report depleted coffers, and envoys bearing axes of authority are dispatched in every direction. Ordinary people near and far who hear the news recoil in alarm, bite their fingers, and look at one another, saying: “What are we to do about this?” Soothe them and they feel affection; feeling affection, they are at peace. Stir them and they are frightened; frightened, they are stirred [?]. Such is the ordinary disposition of the common people.

Even if responsibility for supervision and enforcement along the various routes of Tong and Jin [?] were divided among the envoys, and all fulfilled their duties, if they must be invested with special authority, are there not already enough envoys throughout the realm exercising censorial authority outside the capital? When officials are numerous, many issue commands; when authority is divided, few take responsibility for affairs. Prefectural and commandery authorities hurry to comply, with no respite even after nightfall; urban wards and villages furnish provisions until their very lifeblood is drained. A transmitted text says: “A bird driven to extremity pecks; a beast driven to extremity claws; a horse driven to extremity bolts.” This is a pleasing analogy [?]. Thus the people must not be harassed. If harassed, they cannot live in peace; unable to live in peace, they lose their accustomed livelihoods. The reign of Emperor Wen of Han was especially renowned for wealth and abundance, yet one who offered counsel said: “Of the tasks before us now, none is more pressing than simply getting the people to devote themselves to farming.” Agriculture is the foundation of all under Heaven, the source of grain for sacrificial offerings, and of financial resources…
